1CO 7:38.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 7] So then, he who marries the virgin does well, but he who does not marry her does even better.

1CO 7:39.text: A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.
1CO 7:39.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 7] A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.

1CO 7:40.text: In my judgment, however, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
1CO 7:40.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 7 · Fruit of the Spirit, Judgment] In my judgment, however, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.

1CO 8:1.text: Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
1CO 8:1.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Love, About Forgiveness] Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

1CO 8:2.text: The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.
1CO 8:2.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8] The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.

1CO 8:3.text: But the one who loves God is known by God.
1CO 8:3.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Love] But the one who loves God is known by God.

1CO 8:4.text: So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.
1CO 8:4.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · About Forgiveness, Idolatry] So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.

1CO 8:5.text: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as there are many so-called gods and lords),
1CO 8:5.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Heaven] For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as there are many so-called gods and lords),

1CO 8:6.text: yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.
1CO 8:6.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Body of Christ, God the Father] yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.

1CO 8:7.text: But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.
1CO 8:7.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Idolatry, Idols] But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.

1CO 8:8.text: But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.
1CO 8:8.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8] But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.

1CO 8:9.text: Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
1CO 8:9.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Freedom] Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.

1CO 8:10.text: For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?
1CO 8:10.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Idolatry, Idols] For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?

1CO 8:11.text: So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
1CO 8:11.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.

1CO 8:12.text: By sinning against your brothers in this way and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
1CO 8:12.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] By sinning against your brothers in this way and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

1CO 8:13.text: Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.
1CO 8:13.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 8] Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.

1CO 9:1.text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you yourselves not my workmanship in the Lord?
1CO 9:1.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Jesus Christ] Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you yourselves not my workmanship in the Lord?

1CO 9:2.text: Even if I am not an apostle to others, surely I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
1CO 9:2.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Even if I am not an apostle to others, surely I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

1CO 9:3.text: This is my defense to those who scrutinize me:
1CO 9:3.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] This is my defense to those who scrutinize me:

1CO 9:4.text: Have we no right to food and to drink?
1CO 9:4.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Have we no right to food and to drink?

1CO 9:5.text: Have we no right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?
1CO 9:5.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Apostles] Have we no right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?

1CO 9:6.text: Or are Barnabas and I the only apostles who must work for a living?
1CO 9:6.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Apostles] Or are Barnabas and I the only apostles who must work for a living?

1CO 9:7.text: Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk?
1CO 9:7.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Fruit of the Spirit] Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk?

1CO 9:8.text: Do I say this from a human perspective? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?
1CO 9:8.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Do I say this from a human perspective? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?

1CO 9:9.text: For it is written in the Law of Moses: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?
1CO 9:9.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · About Forgiveness] For it is written in the Law of Moses: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?

1CO 9:10.text: Isn’t He actually speaking on our behalf? Indeed, this was written for us, because when the plowman plows and the thresher threshes, they should also expect to share in the harvest.
1CO 9:10.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Isn’t He actually speaking on our behalf? Indeed, this was written for us, because when the plowman plows and the thresher threshes, they should also expect to share in the harvest.

1CO 9:11.text: If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?
1CO 9:11.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?

1CO 9:12.text: If others have this right to your support, shouldn’t we have it all the more? But we did not exercise this right. Instead, we put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ.
1CO 9:12.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Body of Christ, Gospel] If others have this right to your support, shouldn’t we have it all the more? But we did not exercise this right. Instead, we put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ.

1CO 9:13.text: Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat of its food, and those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings?
1CO 9:13.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat of its food, and those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings?

1CO 9:14.text: In the same way, the Lord has prescribed that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.
1CO 9:14.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Gospel] In the same way, the Lord has prescribed that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.

1CO 9:15.text: But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this to suggest that something be done for me. Indeed, I would rather die than let anyone nullify my boast.
1CO 9:15.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this to suggest that something be done for me. Indeed, I would rather die than let anyone nullify my boast.

1CO 9:16.text: Yet when I preach the gospel, I have no reason to boast, because I am obligated to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
1CO 9:16.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Gospel] Yet when I preach the gospel, I have no reason to boast, because I am obligated to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!

1CO 9:17.text: If my preaching is voluntary, I have a reward. But if it is not voluntary, I am still entrusted with a responsibility.
1CO 9:17.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Faith] If my preaching is voluntary, I have a reward. But if it is not voluntary, I am still entrusted with a responsibility.

1CO 9:18.text: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it.
1CO 9:18.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Gospel] What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it.

1CO 9:19.text: Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.
1CO 9:19.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.

1CO 9:20.text: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.
1CO 9:20.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.

1CO 9:21.text: To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.
1CO 9:21.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.

1CO 9:22.text: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.
1CO 9:22.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.

1CO 9:23.text: I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.
1CO 9:23.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Gospel] I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.

1CO 9:24.text: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.
1CO 9:24.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.

1CO 9:25.text: Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.
1CO 9:25.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.

1CO 9:26.text: Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.
1CO 9:26.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.

1CO 9:27.text: No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.
1CO 9:27.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 9] No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.

1CO 10:1.text: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our forefathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.
1CO 10:1.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our forefathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.

1CO 10:2.text: They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
1CO 10:2.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.

1CO 10:3.text: They all ate the same spiritual food
1CO 10:3.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] They all ate the same spiritual food

1CO 10:4.text: and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.
1CO 10:4.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.

1CO 10:5.text: Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.
1CO 10:5.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.

1CO 10:6.text: These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.
1CO 10:6.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.

1CO 10:7.text: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and to drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.”
1CO 10:7.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and to drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.”

1CO 10:8.text: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.
1CO 10:8.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.

1CO 10:9.text: We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
1CO 10:9.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.

1CO 10:10.text: And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.
1CO 10:10.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.

1CO 10:11.text: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.
1CO 10:11.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.

1CO 10:12.text: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.
1CO 10:12.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.

1CO 10:13.text: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.
1CO 10:13.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Faith] No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.

1CO 10:14.text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
1CO 10:14.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Love, Idolatry] Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

1CO 10:15.text: I speak to reasonable people; judge for yourselves what I say.
1CO 10:15.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] I speak to reasonable people; judge for yourselves what I say.

1CO 10:16.text: Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?
1CO 10:16.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Blessing, Body of Christ] Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?

1CO 10:17.text: Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.
1CO 10:17.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.

1CO 10:18.text: Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?
1CO 10:18.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Israel] Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?

1CO 10:19.text: Am I suggesting, then, that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
1CO 10:19.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] Am I suggesting, then, that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?

1CO 10:20.text: No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to be participants with demons.
1CO 10:20.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Demons] No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to be participants with demons.

1CO 10:21.text: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.
1CO 10:21.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Demons] You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.

1CO 10:22.text: Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?
1CO 10:22.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Jealousy] Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?

1CO 10:23.text: “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.
1CO 10:23.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.

1CO 10:24.text: No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.
1CO 10:24.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.

1CO 10:25.text: Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,
1CO 10:25.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,

1CO 10:26.text: for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.”
1CO 10:26.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.”

1CO 10:27.text: If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.
1CO 10:27.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Faith] If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.

1CO 10:28.text: But if someone tells you, “This food was offered to idols,” then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience—
1CO 10:28.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Idolatry, Idols] But if someone tells you, “This food was offered to idols,” then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience—

1CO 10:29.text: the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your own. For why should my freedom be determined by someone else’s conscience?
1CO 10:29.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Freedom] the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your own. For why should my freedom be determined by someone else’s conscience?

1CO 10:30.text: If I partake in the meal with thankfulness, why am I denounced because of that for which I give thanks?
1CO 10:30.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Gratitude] If I partake in the meal with thankfulness, why am I denounced because of that for which I give thanks?

1CO 10:31.text: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.
1CO 10:31.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Glory] So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.

1CO 10:32.text: Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God—
1CO 10:32.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Church] Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God—

1CO 10:33.text: as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.
1CO 10:33.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 10] as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.

1CO 11:1.text: You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.
1CO 11:1.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.

1CO 11:2.text: Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.
1CO 11:2.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.

1CO 11:3.text: But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
1CO 11:3.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.

1CO 11:4.text: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
1CO 11:4.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.

1CO 11:5.text: And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.
1CO 11:5.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.

1CO 11:6.text: If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.
1CO 11:6.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.

1CO 11:7.text: A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.
1CO 11:7.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Glory, Graven Image] A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.

1CO 11:8.text: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.
1CO 11:8.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.

1CO 11:9.text: Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.
1CO 11:9.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.

1CO 11:10.text: For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
1CO 11:10.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Angels] For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.

1CO 11:11.text: In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.
1CO 11:11.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.

1CO 11:12.text: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.
1CO 11:12.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.

1CO 11:13.text: Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
1CO 11:13.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?

1CO 11:14.text: Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,
1CO 11:14.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,

1CO 11:15.text: but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.
1CO 11:15.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Glory] but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.

1CO 11:16.text: If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.
1CO 11:16.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.

1CO 11:17.text: In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.
1CO 11:17.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.

1CO 11:18.text: First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.
1CO 11:18.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Faith, Church] First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.

1CO 11:19.text: And indeed, there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.
1CO 11:19.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] And indeed, there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.

1CO 11:20.text: Now then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.
1CO 11:20.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Now then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.

1CO 11:21.text: For as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.
1CO 11:21.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 11] For as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.

1CO 12:14.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 12] For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.

1CO 12:15.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 12] If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

1CO 12:17.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 12] If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?

1CO 12:18.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 12 · Body of Christ] But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.

1CO 12:20.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 12] As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

1CO 12:21.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 12] The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”

1CO 12:24.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 12] whereas our presentable parts have no such need.  But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it,

1CO 12:25.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 12 · Body of Christ] so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.

1CO 12:26.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 12] If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.

1CO 14:4.bm25Text: [1 Corinthians · Chapter 14 · Church] The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.
