1KI 4:32.text: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.
1KI 4:32.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 4] Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.

1KI 4:33.text: He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
1KI 4:33.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 4 · About Forgiveness] He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.

1KI 4:34.text: So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.
1KI 4:34.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 4] So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.

1KI 5:1.text: Now when Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father’s place, he sent envoys to Solomon; for Hiram had always been a friend of David.
1KI 5:1.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5 · God the Father] Now when Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father’s place, he sent envoys to Solomon; for Hiram had always been a friend of David.

1KI 5:2.text: And Solomon relayed this message to Hiram:
1KI 5:2.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] And Solomon relayed this message to Hiram:

1KI 5:3.text: “As you are well aware, due to the wars waged on all sides against my father David, he could not build a house for the Name of the LORD his God until the LORD had put his enemies under his feet.
1KI 5:3.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5 · God the Father] “As you are well aware, due to the wars waged on all sides against my father David, he could not build a house for the Name of the LORD his God until the LORD had put his enemies under his feet.

1KI 5:4.text: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side, and there is no adversary or crisis.
1KI 5:4.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side, and there is no adversary or crisis.

1KI 5:5.text: So behold, I plan to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God, according to what the LORD said to my father David: ‘I will put your son on your throne in your place, and he will build the house for My Name.’
1KI 5:5.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5 · God the Father] So behold, I plan to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God, according to what the LORD said to my father David: ‘I will put your son on your throne in your place, and he will build the house for My Name.’

1KI 5:6.text: Now therefore, order that cedars of Lebanon be cut down for me. My servants will be with your servants, and I will pay your servants whatever wages you set, for you know that there are none among us as skilled in logging as the Sidonians.”
1KI 5:6.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] Now therefore, order that cedars of Lebanon be cut down for me. My servants will be with your servants, and I will pay your servants whatever wages you set, for you know that there are none among us as skilled in logging as the Sidonians.”

1KI 5:7.text: When Hiram received Solomon’s message, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be the LORD this day! He has given David a wise son over this great people!”
1KI 5:7.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] When Hiram received Solomon’s message, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be the LORD this day! He has given David a wise son over this great people!”

1KI 5:8.text: Then Hiram sent a reply to Solomon, saying:  “I have received your message; I will do all you desire regarding the cedar and cypress timber.
1KI 5:8.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5 · Lust] Then Hiram sent a reply to Solomon, saying:  “I have received your message; I will do all you desire regarding the cedar and cypress timber.

1KI 5:9.text: My servants will haul the logs from Lebanon to the Sea, and I will float them as rafts by sea to the place you specify. There I will separate the logs, and you can take them away. And in exchange, you can meet my needs by providing my household with food.”
1KI 5:9.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5 · Family] My servants will haul the logs from Lebanon to the Sea, and I will float them as rafts by sea to the place you specify. There I will separate the logs, and you can take them away. And in exchange, you can meet my needs by providing my household with food.”

1KI 5:10.text: So Hiram provided Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber he wanted,
1KI 5:10.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] So Hiram provided Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber he wanted,

1KI 5:11.text: and year after year Solomon would provide Hiram with 20,000 cors of wheat as food for his household, as well as 20,000 baths of pure olive oil.
1KI 5:11.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5 · Family] and year after year Solomon would provide Hiram with 20,000 cors of wheat as food for his household, as well as 20,000 baths of pure olive oil.

1KI 5:12.text: And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty.
1KI 5:12.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty.

1KI 5:13.text: Then King Solomon conscripted a labor force of 30,000 men from all Israel.
1KI 5:13.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5 · Israel] Then King Solomon conscripted a labor force of 30,000 men from all Israel.

1KI 5:14.text: He sent them to Lebanon in monthly shifts of 10,000 men, so that they would spend one month in Lebanon and two months at home. And Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.
1KI 5:14.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] He sent them to Lebanon in monthly shifts of 10,000 men, so that they would spend one month in Lebanon and two months at home. And Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.

1KI 5:15.text: Solomon had 70,000 porters and 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains,
1KI 5:15.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] Solomon had 70,000 porters and 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains,

1KI 5:16.text: not including his 3,300 foremen who supervised the workers.
1KI 5:16.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] not including his 3,300 foremen who supervised the workers.

1KI 5:17.text: And the king commanded them to quarry large, costly stones to lay the foundation of the temple with dressed stones.
1KI 5:17.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5 · God Commanded Genocide] And the king commanded them to quarry large, costly stones to lay the foundation of the temple with dressed stones.

1KI 5:18.text: So Solomon’s and Hiram’s builders, along with the Gebalites, quarried the stone and prepared the timber and stone for the construction of the temple.
1KI 5:18.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 5] So Solomon’s and Hiram’s builders, along with the Gebalites, quarried the stone and prepared the timber and stone for the construction of the temple.

1KI 6:1.text: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, in the month of Ziv, the second month of the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, he began to build the house of the LORD.
1KI 6:1.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6 · Israel] In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, in the month of Ziv, the second month of the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, he began to build the house of the LORD.

1KI 6:2.text: The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
1KI 6:2.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.

1KI 6:3.text: The portico at the front of the main hall of the temple was twenty cubits long, extending across the width of the temple and projecting out ten cubits in front of the temple.
1KI 6:3.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The portico at the front of the main hall of the temple was twenty cubits long, extending across the width of the temple and projecting out ten cubits in front of the temple.

1KI 6:4.text: He also had narrow windows framed high in the temple.
1KI 6:4.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] He also had narrow windows framed high in the temple.

1KI 6:5.text: Against the walls of the temple and the inner sanctuary, Solomon built a chambered structure around the temple, in which he constructed the side rooms.
1KI 6:5.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] Against the walls of the temple and the inner sanctuary, Solomon built a chambered structure around the temple, in which he constructed the side rooms.

1KI 6:6.text: The bottom floor was five cubits wide, the middle floor six cubits, and the third floor seven cubits. He also placed offset ledges around the outside of the temple, so that nothing would be inserted into its walls.
1KI 6:6.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The bottom floor was five cubits wide, the middle floor six cubits, and the third floor seven cubits. He also placed offset ledges around the outside of the temple, so that nothing would be inserted into its walls.

1KI 6:7.text: The temple was constructed using finished stones cut at the quarry, so that no hammer or chisel or any other iron tool was heard in the temple while it was being built.
1KI 6:7.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The temple was constructed using finished stones cut at the quarry, so that no hammer or chisel or any other iron tool was heard in the temple while it was being built.

1KI 6:8.text: The entrance to the bottom floor was on the south side of the temple. A stairway led up to the middle level, and from there to the third floor.
1KI 6:8.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The entrance to the bottom floor was on the south side of the temple. A stairway led up to the middle level, and from there to the third floor.

1KI 6:9.text: So Solomon built the temple and finished it, roofing it with beams and planks of cedar.
1KI 6:9.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] So Solomon built the temple and finished it, roofing it with beams and planks of cedar.

1KI 6:10.text: He built chambers all along the temple, each five cubits high and attached to the temple with beams of cedar.
1KI 6:10.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] He built chambers all along the temple, each five cubits high and attached to the temple with beams of cedar.

1KI 6:11.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon, saying:
1KI 6:11.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon, saying:

1KI 6:12.text: “As for this temple you are building, if you walk in My statutes, carry out My ordinances, and keep all My commandments by walking in them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David.
1KI 6:12.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6 · Covenant, God the Father] “As for this temple you are building, if you walk in My statutes, carry out My ordinances, and keep all My commandments by walking in them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David.

1KI 6:13.text: And I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel.”
1KI 6:13.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6 · Israel] And I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel.”

1KI 6:14.text: So Solomon built the temple and finished it.
1KI 6:14.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] So Solomon built the temple and finished it.

1KI 6:15.text: He lined the interior walls with cedar paneling from the floor of the temple to the ceiling, and he covered the floor with cypress boards.
1KI 6:15.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] He lined the interior walls with cedar paneling from the floor of the temple to the ceiling, and he covered the floor with cypress boards.

1KI 6:16.text: He partitioned off the twenty cubits at the rear of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling to form within the temple an inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
1KI 6:16.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] He partitioned off the twenty cubits at the rear of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling to form within the temple an inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.

1KI 6:17.text: And the main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long.
1KI 6:17.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] And the main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long.

1KI 6:18.text: The cedar paneling inside the temple was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; not a stone could be seen.
1KI 6:18.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The cedar paneling inside the temple was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; not a stone could be seen.

1KI 6:19.text: Solomon also prepared the inner sanctuary within the temple to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.
1KI 6:19.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6 · Covenant] Solomon also prepared the inner sanctuary within the temple to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.

1KI 6:20.text: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold, and he also overlaid the altar of cedar.
1KI 6:20.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold, and he also overlaid the altar of cedar.

1KI 6:21.text: So Solomon overlaid the inside of the temple with pure gold, and he extended gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was overlaid with gold.
1KI 6:21.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] So Solomon overlaid the inside of the temple with pure gold, and he extended gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was overlaid with gold.

1KI 6:22.text: So he overlaid with gold the whole interior of the temple, until everything was completely finished. He also overlaid with gold the entire altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary.
1KI 6:22.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] So he overlaid with gold the whole interior of the temple, until everything was completely finished. He also overlaid with gold the entire altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary.

1KI 6:23.text: In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim, each ten cubits high, out of olive wood.
1KI 6:23.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim, each ten cubits high, out of olive wood.

1KI 6:24.text: One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was five cubits long as well. So the full wingspan was ten cubits.
1KI 6:24.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was five cubits long as well. So the full wingspan was ten cubits.

1KI 6:25.text: The second cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same size and shape,
1KI 6:25.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The second cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same size and shape,

1KI 6:26.text: and the height of each cherub was ten cubits.
1KI 6:26.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] and the height of each cherub was ten cubits.

1KI 6:27.text: And he placed the cherubim inside the innermost room of the temple. Since their wings were spread out, the wing of the first cherub touched one wall, while the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall, and in the middle of the room their wingtips touched.
1KI 6:27.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] And he placed the cherubim inside the innermost room of the temple. Since their wings were spread out, the wing of the first cherub touched one wall, while the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall, and in the middle of the room their wingtips touched.

1KI 6:28.text: He also overlaid the cherubim with gold.
1KI 6:28.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] He also overlaid the cherubim with gold.

1KI 6:29.text: Then he carved the walls all around the temple, in both the inner and outer sanctuaries, with carved engravings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
1KI 6:29.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] Then he carved the walls all around the temple, in both the inner and outer sanctuaries, with carved engravings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.

1KI 6:30.text: And he overlaid the temple floor with gold in both the inner and outer sanctuaries.
1KI 6:30.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] And he overlaid the temple floor with gold in both the inner and outer sanctuaries.

1KI 6:31.text: For the entrance to the inner sanctuary, Solomon constructed doors of olive wood with five-sided doorposts.
1KI 6:31.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] For the entrance to the inner sanctuary, Solomon constructed doors of olive wood with five-sided doorposts.

1KI 6:32.text: The double doors were made of olive wood, and he carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers and overlaid the cherubim and palm trees with hammered gold.
1KI 6:32.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The double doors were made of olive wood, and he carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers and overlaid the cherubim and palm trees with hammered gold.

1KI 6:33.text: In the same way he made four-sided doorposts of olive wood for the sanctuary entrance.
1KI 6:33.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] In the same way he made four-sided doorposts of olive wood for the sanctuary entrance.

1KI 6:34.text: The two doors were made of cypress wood, and each had two folding panels.
1KI 6:34.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The two doors were made of cypress wood, and each had two folding panels.

1KI 6:35.text: He carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers; and he overlaid them with gold, hammered evenly over the carvings.
1KI 6:35.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] He carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers; and he overlaid them with gold, hammered evenly over the carvings.

1KI 6:36.text: Solomon built the inner courtyard with three rows of dressed stone and one row of trimmed cedar beams.
1KI 6:36.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] Solomon built the inner courtyard with three rows of dressed stone and one row of trimmed cedar beams.

1KI 6:37.text: The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign, in the month of Ziv.
1KI 6:37.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign, in the month of Ziv.

1KI 6:38.text: In his eleventh year and eighth month, the month of Bul, the temple was finished in every detail and according to every specification. So he built the temple in seven years.
1KI 6:38.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 6] In his eleventh year and eighth month, the month of Bul, the temple was finished in every detail and according to every specification. So he built the temple in seven years.

1KI 7:1.text: Solomon, however, took thirteen years to complete the construction of his entire palace.
1KI 7:1.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] Solomon, however, took thirteen years to complete the construction of his entire palace.

1KI 7:2.text: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with four rows of cedar pillars supporting the cedar beams.
1KI 7:2.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with four rows of cedar pillars supporting the cedar beams.

1KI 7:3.text: The house was roofed with cedar above the beams that rested on the pillars—forty-five beams, fifteen per row.
1KI 7:3.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] The house was roofed with cedar above the beams that rested on the pillars—forty-five beams, fifteen per row.

1KI 7:4.text: There were three rows of high windows facing one another in three tiers.
1KI 7:4.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] There were three rows of high windows facing one another in three tiers.

1KI 7:5.text: All the doorways had rectangular frames, with the openings facing one another in three tiers.
1KI 7:5.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] All the doorways had rectangular frames, with the openings facing one another in three tiers.

1KI 7:6.text: Solomon made his colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a portico in front of it and a canopy with pillars in front of the portico.
1KI 7:6.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] Solomon made his colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a portico in front of it and a canopy with pillars in front of the portico.

1KI 7:7.text: In addition, he built a hall for the throne, the Hall of Justice, where he was to judge. It was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.
1KI 7:7.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7 · Justice] In addition, he built a hall for the throne, the Hall of Justice, where he was to judge. It was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.

1KI 7:8.text: And the palace where Solomon would live, set further back, was of similar construction. He also made a palace like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had married.
1KI 7:8.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] And the palace where Solomon would live, set further back, was of similar construction. He also made a palace like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had married.

1KI 7:9.text: All these buildings were constructed with costly stones, cut to size and trimmed with saws inside and out from the foundation to the eaves, and from the outside to the great courtyard.
1KI 7:9.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] All these buildings were constructed with costly stones, cut to size and trimmed with saws inside and out from the foundation to the eaves, and from the outside to the great courtyard.

1KI 7:10.text: The foundations were laid with large, costly stones, some ten cubits long and some eight cubits long.
1KI 7:10.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] The foundations were laid with large, costly stones, some ten cubits long and some eight cubits long.

1KI 7:11.text: Above these were high-grade stones, cut to size, and cedar beams.
1KI 7:11.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] Above these were high-grade stones, cut to size, and cedar beams.

1KI 7:12.text: The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of dressed stone and a row of trimmed cedar beams, as were the inner courtyard and portico of the house of the LORD.
1KI 7:12.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of dressed stone and a row of trimmed cedar beams, as were the inner courtyard and portico of the house of the LORD.

1KI 7:13.text: Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre.
1KI 7:13.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre.

1KI 7:14.text: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Huram had great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work. So he came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
1KI 7:14.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7 · God the Father] He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Huram had great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work. So he came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.

1KI 7:15.text: He cast two pillars of bronze, each eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference.
1KI 7:15.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] He cast two pillars of bronze, each eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference.

1KI 7:16.text: He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each capital five cubits high.
1KI 7:16.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each capital five cubits high.

1KI 7:17.text: For the capitals on top of the pillars he made a network of lattice, with wreaths of chainwork, seven for each capital.
1KI 7:17.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] For the capitals on top of the pillars he made a network of lattice, with wreaths of chainwork, seven for each capital.

1KI 7:18.text: Likewise, he made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates around each grating to cover each capital atop the pillars.
1KI 7:18.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] Likewise, he made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates around each grating to cover each capital atop the pillars.

1KI 7:19.text: And the capitals atop the pillars in the portico were shaped like lilies, four cubits high.
1KI 7:19.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] And the capitals atop the pillars in the portico were shaped like lilies, four cubits high.

1KI 7:20.text: On the capitals of both pillars, just above the rounded projection next to the network, were the two hundred pomegranates in rows encircling each capital.
1KI 7:20.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] On the capitals of both pillars, just above the rounded projection next to the network, were the two hundred pomegranates in rows encircling each capital.

1KI 7:21.text: Thus he set up the pillars at the portico of the temple. The pillar to the south he named Jachin, and the pillar to the north he named Boaz.
1KI 7:21.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] Thus he set up the pillars at the portico of the temple. The pillar to the south he named Jachin, and the pillar to the north he named Boaz.

1KI 7:22.text: And the tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. So the work of the pillars was completed.
1KI 7:22.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] And the tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. So the work of the pillars was completed.

1KI 7:23.text: He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.
1KI 7:23.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.

1KI 7:24.text: Below the rim, ornamental buds encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.
1KI 7:24.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] Below the rim, ornamental buds encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.

1KI 7:25.text: The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.
1KI 7:25.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.

1KI 7:26.text: It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold two thousand baths.
1KI 7:26.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold two thousand baths.

1KI 7:27.text: In addition, he made ten movable stands of bronze, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
1KI 7:27.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] In addition, he made ten movable stands of bronze, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.

1KI 7:28.text: This was the design of the stands: They had side panels attached to uprights,
1KI 7:28.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] This was the design of the stands: They had side panels attached to uprights,

1KI 7:29.text: and on the panels between the uprights were lions, oxen, and cherubim. On the uprights was a pedestal above, and below the lions and oxen were wreaths of beveled work.
1KI 7:29.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] and on the panels between the uprights were lions, oxen, and cherubim. On the uprights was a pedestal above, and below the lions and oxen were wreaths of beveled work.

1KI 7:30.text: Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles and a basin resting on four supports, with wreaths at each side.
1KI 7:30.bm25Text: [1 Kings · Chapter 7] Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles and a basin resting on four supports, with wreaths at each side.

1SA 20:7.text: If he says, ‘Good,’ then your servant is safe, but if he is enraged, you will know he has evil intentions.
1SA 20:7.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] If he says, ‘Good,’ then your servant is safe, but if he is enraged, you will know he has evil intentions.

1SA 20:8.text: Therefore deal faithfully with your servant, for you have brought me into a covenant with you before the LORD. If there is iniquity in me, then kill me yourself; why should you bring me to your father?”
1SA 20:8.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · Faith, Covenant] Therefore deal faithfully with your servant, for you have brought me into a covenant with you before the LORD. If there is iniquity in me, then kill me yourself; why should you bring me to your father?”

1SA 20:9.text: “Never!” Jonathan replied. “If I ever found out that my father had evil intentions against you, would I not tell you?”
1SA 20:9.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · God the Father] “Never!” Jonathan replied. “If I ever found out that my father had evil intentions against you, would I not tell you?”

1SA 20:10.text: Then David asked Jonathan, “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”
1SA 20:10.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · God the Father] Then David asked Jonathan, “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”

1SA 20:11.text: “Come,” he replied, “let us go out to the field.”  So the two of them went out into the field,
1SA 20:11.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] “Come,” he replied, “let us go out to the field.”  So the two of them went out into the field,

1SA 20:12.text: and Jonathan said, “By the LORD, the God of Israel, I will sound out my father by this time tomorrow or the next day. If he is favorable toward you, will I not send for you and tell you?
1SA 20:12.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · God the Father, Israel] and Jonathan said, “By the LORD, the God of Israel, I will sound out my father by this time tomorrow or the next day. If he is favorable toward you, will I not send for you and tell you?

1SA 20:13.text: But if my father intends to bring evil on you, then may the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if I do not tell you and send you on your way in safety. May the LORD be with you, just as He has been with my father.
1SA 20:13.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · God the Father] But if my father intends to bring evil on you, then may the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if I do not tell you and send you on your way in safety. May the LORD be with you, just as He has been with my father.

1SA 20:14.text: And as long as I live, treat me with the LORD’s loving devotion, that I may not die,
1SA 20:14.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · Devotion] And as long as I live, treat me with the LORD’s loving devotion, that I may not die,

1SA 20:15.text: and do not ever cut off your loving devotion from my household—not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.”
1SA 20:15.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · Devotion, Family] and do not ever cut off your loving devotion from my household—not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.”

1SA 20:16.text: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, “May the LORD hold David’s enemies accountable.”
1SA 20:16.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · Covenant] So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, “May the LORD hold David’s enemies accountable.”

1SA 20:17.text: And Jonathan had David reaffirm his vow out of love for him, for Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.
1SA 20:17.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · Love] And Jonathan had David reaffirm his vow out of love for him, for Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.

1SA 20:18.text: Then Jonathan said to David, “Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you will be missed if your seat is empty.
1SA 20:18.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] Then Jonathan said to David, “Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you will be missed if your seat is empty.

1SA 20:19.text: When you have stayed three days, hurry down to the place you hid on the day this trouble began, and remain beside the stone Ezel.
1SA 20:19.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] When you have stayed three days, hurry down to the place you hid on the day this trouble began, and remain beside the stone Ezel.

1SA 20:20.text: I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as if I were aiming at a target.
1SA 20:20.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as if I were aiming at a target.

1SA 20:21.text: Then I will send a boy and say, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ Now, if I expressly say to him, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them,’ then come, because as surely as the LORD lives, it is safe for you and there is no danger.
1SA 20:21.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] Then I will send a boy and say, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ Now, if I expressly say to him, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them,’ then come, because as surely as the LORD lives, it is safe for you and there is no danger.

1SA 20:22.text: But if I say to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then you must go, for the LORD has sent you away.
1SA 20:22.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] But if I say to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then you must go, for the LORD has sent you away.

1SA 20:23.text: And as for the matter you and I have discussed, the LORD is a witness between you and me forever.”
1SA 20:23.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · False Witness] And as for the matter you and I have discussed, the LORD is a witness between you and me forever.”

1SA 20:24.text: So David hid in the field, and when the New Moon had come, the king sat down to eat.
1SA 20:24.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] So David hid in the field, and when the New Moon had come, the king sat down to eat.

1SA 20:25.text: He sat in his usual place by the wall, opposite Jonathan and beside Abner, but David’s place was empty.
1SA 20:25.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] He sat in his usual place by the wall, opposite Jonathan and beside Abner, but David’s place was empty.

1SA 20:26.text: Saul said nothing that day because he thought, “Something has happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean—surely he is unclean.”
1SA 20:26.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] Saul said nothing that day because he thought, “Something has happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean—surely he is unclean.”

1SA 20:27.text: But on the day after the New Moon, the second day, David’s place was still empty, and Saul asked his son Jonathan, “Why hasn’t the son of Jesse come to the meal either yesterday or today?”
1SA 20:27.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] But on the day after the New Moon, the second day, David’s place was still empty, and Saul asked his son Jonathan, “Why hasn’t the son of Jesse come to the meal either yesterday or today?”

1SA 20:28.text: Jonathan answered, “David urgently requested my permission to go to Bethlehem,
1SA 20:28.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] Jonathan answered, “David urgently requested my permission to go to Bethlehem,

1SA 20:29.text: saying, ‘Please let me go, because our clan is holding a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has told me to be there. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me go and see my brothers.’ That is why he did not come to the king’s table.”
1SA 20:29.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · Blessing] saying, ‘Please let me go, because our clan is holding a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has told me to be there. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me go and see my brothers.’ That is why he did not come to the king’s table.”

1SA 20:30.text: Then Saul’s anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, “You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the disgrace of the mother who bore you?
1SA 20:30.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · Election] Then Saul’s anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, “You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the disgrace of the mother who bore you?

1SA 20:31.text: For as long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingship shall be established. Now send for him and bring him to me, for he must surely die!”
1SA 20:31.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] For as long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingship shall be established. Now send for him and bring him to me, for he must surely die!”

1SA 20:32.text: “Why must he be put to death?” Jonathan replied. “What has he done?”
1SA 20:32.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · Death] “Why must he be put to death?” Jonathan replied. “What has he done?”

1SA 20:33.text: Then Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan to kill him; so Jonathan knew that his father was determined to kill David.
1SA 20:33.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · God the Father] Then Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan to kill him; so Jonathan knew that his father was determined to kill David.

1SA 20:34.text: Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger and did not eat any food that second day of the month, for he was grieved by his father’s shameful treatment of David.
1SA 20:34.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · God the Father] Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger and did not eat any food that second day of the month, for he was grieved by his father’s shameful treatment of David.

1SA 20:35.text: In the morning Jonathan went out to the field for the appointment with David, and a small boy was with him.
1SA 20:35.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] In the morning Jonathan went out to the field for the appointment with David, and a small boy was with him.

1SA 20:36.text: He said to the boy, “Run and find the arrows I shoot.” And as the boy ran, Jonathan shot an arrow beyond him.
1SA 20:36.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] He said to the boy, “Run and find the arrows I shoot.” And as the boy ran, Jonathan shot an arrow beyond him.

1SA 20:37.text: When the boy reached the place where Jonathan’s arrow had fallen, Jonathan called to him, “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?”
1SA 20:37.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] When the boy reached the place where Jonathan’s arrow had fallen, Jonathan called to him, “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?”

1SA 20:38.text: Then Jonathan cried out, “Hurry! Make haste! Do not delay!” So the boy picked up the arrow and returned to his master.
1SA 20:38.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] Then Jonathan cried out, “Hurry! Make haste! Do not delay!” So the boy picked up the arrow and returned to his master.

1SA 20:39.text: But the boy did not know anything; only Jonathan and David knew the arrangement.
1SA 20:39.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] But the boy did not know anything; only Jonathan and David knew the arrangement.

1SA 20:40.text: Then Jonathan gave his equipment to the boy and said, “Go, take it back to the city.”
1SA 20:40.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20] Then Jonathan gave his equipment to the boy and said, “Go, take it back to the city.”

1SA 20:41.text: When the young man had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone, fell facedown, and bowed three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together—though David wept more.
1SA 20:41.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · End Times] When the young man had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone, fell facedown, and bowed three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together—though David wept more.

1SA 20:42.text: And Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, for the two of us have sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘May the LORD be a witness between you and me, and between your descendants and mine forever.’” Then David got up and departed, and Jonathan went back into the city.
1SA 20:42.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 20 · False Witness] And Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, for the two of us have sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘May the LORD be a witness between you and me, and between your descendants and mine forever.’” Then David got up and departed, and Jonathan went back into the city.

1SA 21:1.text: Then David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. And when Ahimelech met David, he trembled and asked him, “Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?”
1SA 21:1.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] Then David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. And when Ahimelech met David, he trembled and asked him, “Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?”

1SA 21:2.text: “The king has given me a mission,” David replied. “He told me no one is to know about the mission or charge. And I have directed my young men to meet me at a certain place.
1SA 21:2.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21 · About Forgiveness] “The king has given me a mission,” David replied. “He told me no one is to know about the mission or charge. And I have directed my young men to meet me at a certain place.

1SA 21:3.text: Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever can be found.”
1SA 21:3.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever can be found.”

1SA 21:4.text: “There is no common bread on hand,” the priest replied, “but there is some consecrated bread—provided that the young men have kept themselves from women.”
1SA 21:4.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21 · Biblical Women, Heroic Women] “There is no common bread on hand,” the priest replied, “but there is some consecrated bread—provided that the young men have kept themselves from women.”

1SA 21:5.text: David answered, “Women have indeed been kept from us, as is usual when I set out. And the equipment of the young men is holy, as it is even on common missions, and all the more at this time.”
1SA 21:5.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21 · Biblical Women, Heroic Women] David answered, “Women have indeed been kept from us, as is usual when I set out. And the equipment of the young men is holy, as it is even on common missions, and all the more at this time.”

1SA 21:6.text: So the priest gave him the consecrated bread, since there was no bread there but the Bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD and replaced with hot bread on the day it was taken away.
1SA 21:6.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] So the priest gave him the consecrated bread, since there was no bread there but the Bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD and replaced with hot bread on the day it was taken away.

1SA 21:7.text: Now one of Saul’s servants was there that day, detained before the LORD. And his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief shepherd for Saul.
1SA 21:7.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] Now one of Saul’s servants was there that day, detained before the LORD. And his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief shepherd for Saul.

1SA 21:8.text: Then David asked Ahimelech, “Is there not a spear or sword on hand here? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s business was urgent.”
1SA 21:8.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] Then David asked Ahimelech, “Is there not a spear or sword on hand here? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s business was urgent.”

1SA 21:9.text: The priest replied, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here; it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you want, you may take it. For there is no other but this one.”  And David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.”
1SA 21:9.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] The priest replied, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here; it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you want, you may take it. For there is no other but this one.”  And David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.”

1SA 21:10.text: That day David fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.
1SA 21:10.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] That day David fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.

1SA 21:11.text: But the servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing about him in their dances, saying:  ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”
1SA 21:11.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21 · About Forgiveness] But the servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing about him in their dances, saying:  ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”

1SA 21:12.text: Now David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
1SA 21:12.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21 · Adultery In Heart] Now David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish the king of Gath.

1SA 21:13.text: So he changed his behavior before them and feigned madness in their hands; he scratched on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down his beard.
1SA 21:13.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] So he changed his behavior before them and feigned madness in their hands; he scratched on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down his beard.

1SA 21:14.text: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you can see that the man is insane! Why have you brought him to me?
1SA 21:14.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you can see that the man is insane! Why have you brought him to me?

1SA 21:15.text: Am I in need of madmen, that you have brought this man to rave in my presence? Must this man come into my house?”
1SA 21:15.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 21] Am I in need of madmen, that you have brought this man to rave in my presence? Must this man come into my house?”

1SA 22:1.text: So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.
1SA 22:1.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · About Forgiveness, Family] So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.

1SA 22:2.text: And all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.
1SA 22:2.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · About Forgiveness] And all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.

1SA 22:3.text: From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.”
1SA 22:3.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · God the Father] From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.”

1SA 22:4.text: So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.
1SA 22:4.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.

1SA 22:5.text: Then the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
1SA 22:5.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] Then the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.

1SA 22:6.text: Soon Saul learned that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was in Gibeah, sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in hand and all his servants standing around him.
1SA 22:6.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] Soon Saul learned that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was in Gibeah, sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in hand and all his servants standing around him.

1SA 22:7.text: Then Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Is the son of Jesse giving all of you fields and vineyards and making you commanders of thousands or hundreds?
1SA 22:7.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · Generosity] Then Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Is the son of Jesse giving all of you fields and vineyards and making you commanders of thousands or hundreds?

1SA 22:8.text: Is that why all of you have conspired against me? Not one of you told me that my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you has shown concern for me or revealed to me that my son has stirred up my own servant to lie in wait against me, as is the case today.”
1SA 22:8.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · Covenant] Is that why all of you have conspired against me? Not one of you told me that my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you has shown concern for me or revealed to me that my son has stirred up my own servant to lie in wait against me, as is the case today.”

1SA 22:9.text: But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.
1SA 22:9.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.

1SA 22:10.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him and gave him provisions. He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”

1SA 22:11.text: Then the king sent messengers to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests at Nob. And all of them came to the king.
1SA 22:11.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · Angels, Family] Then the king sent messengers to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests at Nob. And all of them came to the king.

1SA 22:12.text: “Listen now, son of Ahitub,” said Saul.  “Here I am, my lord,” he replied.
1SA 22:12.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] “Listen now, son of Ahitub,” said Saul.  “Here I am, my lord,” he replied.

1SA 22:13.text: And Saul asked him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.”
1SA 22:13.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] And Saul asked him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.”

1SA 22:14.text: Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard who is honored in your house?
1SA 22:14.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · Faith] Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard who is honored in your house?

1SA 22:15.text: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of my father’s household, for your servant knew nothing of this whole affair—not in part or in whole.”
1SA 22:15.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · Family, God the Father] Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of my father’s household, for your servant knew nothing of this whole affair—not in part or in whole.”

1SA 22:16.text: But the king replied, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”
1SA 22:16.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · God the Father] But the king replied, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”

1SA 22:17.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] Then the king ordered the guards at his side, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too sided with David. 1SA 22:18.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] So the king ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!”  And Doeg the Edomite turned and struck down the priests himself. On that day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.

1SA 22:19.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · Biblical Women, Children] He also put to the sword Nob, the city of the priests, with its men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.

1SA 22:20.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] But one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, and he fled to David.

1SA 22:21.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.

1SA 22:22.text: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul. I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.
1SA 22:22.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22 · God the Father] Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul. I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.

1SA 22:23.text: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.”
1SA 22:23.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 22] Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.”

1SA 23:1.text: Now it was reported to David, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and looting the threshing floors.”
1SA 23:1.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 23] Now it was reported to David, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and looting the threshing floors.”

1SA 23:2.text: So David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?”  And the LORD said to David, “Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah.”
1SA 23:2.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 23] So David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?”  And the LORD said to David, “Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah.”

1SA 23:3.text: But David’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
1SA 23:3.bm25Text: [1 Samuel · Chapter 23] But David’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”

1SA 23:4.text: Once again, David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD answered him: “Go at once to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”

2CH 10:7.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 10] They replied, “If you will be kind to these people and please them by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”

2CH 10:9.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 10 · God the Father] He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
