2CH 24:10.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] All the officers and all the people rejoiced and brought their contributions, and they dropped them in the chest until it was full.

2CH 24:11.text: Whenever the chest was brought by the Levites to the king’s overseers and they saw that there was a large amount of money, the royal scribe and the officer of the high priest would come and empty the chest and carry it back to its place. They did this daily and gathered the money in abundance.
2CH 24:11.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] Whenever the chest was brought by the Levites to the king’s overseers and they saw that there was a large amount of money, the royal scribe and the officer of the high priest would come and empty the chest and carry it back to its place. They did this daily and gathered the money in abundance.

2CH 24:12.text: Then the king and Jehoiada would give the money to those who supervised the labor on the house of the LORD to hire stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, as well as workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.
2CH 24:12.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] Then the king and Jehoiada would give the money to those who supervised the labor on the house of the LORD to hire stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, as well as workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.

2CH 24:13.text: So the workmen labored, and in their hands the repair work progressed. They restored the house of God according to its specifications, and they reinforced it.
2CH 24:13.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] So the workmen labored, and in their hands the repair work progressed. They restored the house of God according to its specifications, and they reinforced it.

2CH 24:14.text: When they were finished, they brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada to make with it the articles for the house of the LORD—utensils for the service and for the burnt offerings, dishes, and other objects of gold and silver.  Throughout the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings were presented regularly in the house of the LORD.
2CH 24:14.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] When they were finished, they brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada to make with it the articles for the house of the LORD—utensils for the service and for the burnt offerings, dishes, and other objects of gold and silver.  Throughout the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings were presented regularly in the house of the LORD.

2CH 24:15.text: When Jehoiada was old and full of years, he died at the age of 130.
2CH 24:15.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] When Jehoiada was old and full of years, he died at the age of 130.

2CH 24:16.text: And Jehoiada was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done what was good in Israel for God and His temple.
2CH 24:16.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24 · Israel] And Jehoiada was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done what was good in Israel for God and His temple.

2CH 24:17.text: After the death of Jehoiada, however, the officials of Judah came and paid homage to the king, and he listened to them.
2CH 24:17.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24 · Death] After the death of Jehoiada, however, the officials of Judah came and paid homage to the king, and he listened to them.

2CH 24:18.text: They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherah poles and idols. So wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.
2CH 24:18.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24 · Idolatry, Idols] They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherah poles and idols. So wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.

2CH 24:19.text: Nevertheless, the LORD sent prophets to bring the people back to Him and to testify against them; but they would not listen.
2CH 24:19.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] Nevertheless, the LORD sent prophets to bring the people back to Him and to testify against them; but they would not listen.

2CH 24:20.text: Then the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, who stood up before the people and said to them, “This is what God says: ‘Why do you transgress the commandments of the LORD so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you.’”
2CH 24:20.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24 · Fruit of the Spirit, Law] Then the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, who stood up before the people and said to them, “This is what God says: ‘Why do you transgress the commandments of the LORD so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you.’”

2CH 24:21.text: But they conspired against Zechariah, and by order of the king, they stoned him in the courtyard of the house of the LORD.
2CH 24:21.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] But they conspired against Zechariah, and by order of the king, they stoned him in the courtyard of the house of the LORD.

2CH 24:22.text: Thus King Joash failed to remember the kindness that Zechariah’s father Jehoiada had extended to him. Instead, Joash killed Jehoiada’s son. As he lay dying, Zechariah said, “May the LORD see this and call you to account.”
2CH 24:22.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24 · God the Father, Grace] Thus King Joash failed to remember the kindness that Zechariah’s father Jehoiada had extended to him. Instead, Joash killed Jehoiada’s son. As he lay dying, Zechariah said, “May the LORD see this and call you to account.”

2CH 24:23.text: In the spring, the army of Aram went to war against Joash. They entered Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the leaders of the people, and they sent all the plunder to their king in Damascus.
2CH 24:23.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] In the spring, the army of Aram went to war against Joash. They entered Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the leaders of the people, and they sent all the plunder to their king in Damascus.

2CH 24:24.text: Although the Aramean army had come with only a few men, the LORD delivered into their hand a very great army. Because Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers, judgment was executed on Joash.
2CH 24:24.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24 · Judgment] Although the Aramean army had come with only a few men, the LORD delivered into their hand a very great army. Because Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers, judgment was executed on Joash.

2CH 24:25.text: And when the Arameans had withdrawn, they left Joash severely wounded. His own servants conspired against him for shedding the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed. So he died and was buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
2CH 24:25.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] And when the Arameans had withdrawn, they left Joash severely wounded. His own servants conspired against him for shedding the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed. So he died and was buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

2CH 24:26.text: Those who conspired against Joash were Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonitess and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabitess.
2CH 24:26.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24] Those who conspired against Joash were Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonitess and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabitess.

2CH 24:27.text: The accounts of the sons of Joash, as well as the many pronouncements about him and about the restoration of the house of God, are indeed written in the Treatise of the Book of the Kings. And his son Amaziah reigned in his place.
2CH 24:27.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 24 · About Forgiveness, Healing] The accounts of the sons of Joash, as well as the many pronouncements about him and about the restoration of the house of God, are indeed written in the Treatise of the Book of the Kings. And his son Amaziah reigned in his place.

2CH 25:1.text: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan; she was from Jerusalem.
2CH 25:1.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan; she was from Jerusalem.

2CH 25:2.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not wholeheartedly.
2CH 25:2.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not wholeheartedly.

2CH 25:3.text: As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his grasp, Amaziah executed the servants who had murdered his father the king.
2CH 25:3.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · God the Father, Kingdom of God] As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his grasp, Amaziah executed the servants who had murdered his father the king.

2CH 25:4.text: Yet he did not put their sons to death, but acted according to what is written in the Law, in the Book of Moses, where the LORD commanded: “Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.”
2CH 25:4.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Children, Death] Yet he did not put their sons to death, but acted according to what is written in the Law, in the Book of Moses, where the LORD commanded: “Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.”

2CH 25:5.text: Then Amaziah gathered the people of Judah and assigned them according to their families to commanders of thousands and of hundreds. And he numbered those twenty years of age or older throughout Judah and Benjamin and found 300,000 chosen men able to serve in the army, bearing the spear and shield.
2CH 25:5.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Election] Then Amaziah gathered the people of Judah and assigned them according to their families to commanders of thousands and of hundreds. And he numbered those twenty years of age or older throughout Judah and Benjamin and found 300,000 chosen men able to serve in the army, bearing the spear and shield.

2CH 25:6.text: He also hired 100,000 mighty warriors from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.
2CH 25:6.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Israel] He also hired 100,000 mighty warriors from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.

2CH 25:7.text: But a man of God came to him and said, “O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel—not with any of the Ephraimites.
2CH 25:7.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Israel] But a man of God came to him and said, “O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel—not with any of the Ephraimites.

2CH 25:8.text: Even if you go and fight bravely in battle, God will make you stumble before the enemy, for God has power to help and power to overthrow.”
2CH 25:8.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] Even if you go and fight bravely in battle, God will make you stumble before the enemy, for God has power to help and power to overthrow.”

2CH 25:9.text: Amaziah asked the man of God, “What should I do about the hundred talents I have given to the army of Israel?”  And the man of God replied, “The LORD is able to give you much more than this.”
2CH 25:9.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · About Forgiveness, Israel] Amaziah asked the man of God, “What should I do about the hundred talents I have given to the army of Israel?”  And the man of God replied, “The LORD is able to give you much more than this.”

2CH 25:10.text: So Amaziah dismissed the troops who had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home. And they were furious with Judah and returned home in great anger.
2CH 25:10.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] So Amaziah dismissed the troops who had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home. And they were furious with Judah and returned home in great anger.

2CH 25:11.text: Amaziah, however, summoned his strength and led his troops to the Valley of Salt, where he struck down 10,000 men of Seir,
2CH 25:11.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Calling] Amaziah, however, summoned his strength and led his troops to the Valley of Salt, where he struck down 10,000 men of Seir,

2CH 25:12.text: and the army of Judah also captured 10,000 men alive. They took them to the top of a cliff and threw them down so that all were dashed to pieces.
2CH 25:12.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] and the army of Judah also captured 10,000 men alive. They took them to the top of a cliff and threw them down so that all were dashed to pieces.

2CH 25:13.text: Meanwhile the troops that Amaziah had dismissed from battle raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria to Beth-horon. They struck down 3,000 people and carried off a great deal of plunder.
2CH 25:13.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] Meanwhile the troops that Amaziah had dismissed from battle raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria to Beth-horon. They struck down 3,000 people and carried off a great deal of plunder.

2CH 25:14.text: When Amaziah returned from the slaughter of the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the Seirites, set them up as his own gods, bowed before them, and burned sacrifices to them.
2CH 25:14.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] When Amaziah returned from the slaughter of the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the Seirites, set them up as his own gods, bowed before them, and burned sacrifices to them.

2CH 25:15.text: Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and He sent him a prophet, who said, “Why have you sought this people’s gods, which could not deliver them from your hand?”
2CH 25:15.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and He sent him a prophet, who said, “Why have you sought this people’s gods, which could not deliver them from your hand?”

2CH 25:16.text: While he was still speaking, the king asked, “Have we made you the counselor to the king? Stop! Why be struck down?”  So the prophet stopped, but he said, “I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not heeded my advice.”
2CH 25:16.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] While he was still speaking, the king asked, “Have we made you the counselor to the king? Stop! Why be struck down?”  So the prophet stopped, but he said, “I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not heeded my advice.”

2CH 25:17.text: Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent word to the king of Israel Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu. “Come, let us meet face to face,” he said.
2CH 25:17.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Israel] Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent word to the king of Israel Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu. “Come, let us meet face to face,” he said.

2CH 25:18.text: But Jehoash king of Israel replied to Amaziah king of Judah: “A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son in marriage.’ Then a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle.
2CH 25:18.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Antichrist, Israel] But Jehoash king of Israel replied to Amaziah king of Judah: “A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son in marriage.’ Then a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle.

2CH 25:19.text: You have said, ‘Look, I have defeated Edom,’ and your heart has become proud and boastful. Now stay at home. Why should you stir up trouble so that you fall—you and Judah with you?”
2CH 25:19.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Adultery In Heart] You have said, ‘Look, I have defeated Edom,’ and your heart has become proud and boastful. Now stay at home. Why should you stir up trouble so that you fall—you and Judah with you?”

2CH 25:20.text: But Amaziah would not listen, for this had come from God in order to deliver them into the hand of Jehoash, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
2CH 25:20.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] But Amaziah would not listen, for this had come from God in order to deliver them into the hand of Jehoash, because they had sought the gods of Edom.

2CH 25:21.text: So Jehoash king of Israel advanced, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh in Judah.
2CH 25:21.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Israel] So Jehoash king of Israel advanced, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh in Judah.

2CH 25:22.text: And Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his own home.
2CH 25:22.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Israel] And Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his own home.

2CH 25:23.text: There at Beth-shemesh, Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz.  Then Jehoash brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate—a section of four hundred cubits.
2CH 25:23.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Israel] There at Beth-shemesh, Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz.  Then Jehoash brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate—a section of four hundred cubits.

2CH 25:24.text: He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of God with Obed-edom and in the treasuries of the royal palace, as well as some hostages. Then he returned to Samaria.
2CH 25:24.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of God with Obed-edom and in the treasuries of the royal palace, as well as some hostages. Then he returned to Samaria.

2CH 25:25.text: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
2CH 25:25.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Death, Israel] Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

2CH 25:26.text: As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from beginning to end, are they not written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel?
2CH 25:26.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25 · Israel] As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from beginning to end, are they not written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel?

2CH 25:27.text: From the time that Amaziah turned from following the LORD, a conspiracy was formed against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But men were sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.
2CH 25:27.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] From the time that Amaziah turned from following the LORD, a conspiracy was formed against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But men were sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.

2CH 25:28.text: They carried him back on horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of Judah.
2CH 25:28.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 25] They carried him back on horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of Judah.

2CH 26:1.text: All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
2CH 26:1.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26 · God the Father] All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

2CH 26:2.text: Uzziah was the one who rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah after King Amaziah rested with his fathers.
2CH 26:2.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] Uzziah was the one who rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah after King Amaziah rested with his fathers.

2CH 26:3.text: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. His mother’s name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem.
2CH 26:3.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. His mother’s name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem.

2CH 26:4.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.
2CH 26:4.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26 · God the Father] And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.

2CH 26:5.text: He sought God throughout the days of Zechariah, who instructed him in the fear of God. And as long as he sought the LORD, God gave him success.
2CH 26:5.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] He sought God throughout the days of Zechariah, who instructed him in the fear of God. And as long as he sought the LORD, God gave him success.

2CH 26:6.text: Uzziah went out to wage war against the Philistines, and he tore down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod. Then he built cities near Ashdod and among the Philistines.
2CH 26:6.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] Uzziah went out to wage war against the Philistines, and he tore down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod. Then he built cities near Ashdod and among the Philistines.

2CH 26:7.text: God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs living in Gur-baal, and against the Meunites.
2CH 26:7.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs living in Gur-baal, and against the Meunites.

2CH 26:8.text: The Ammonites brought tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, for he had become exceedingly powerful.
2CH 26:8.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] The Ammonites brought tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, for he had become exceedingly powerful.

2CH 26:9.text: Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the angle in the wall, and he fortified them.
2CH 26:9.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the angle in the wall, and he fortified them.

2CH 26:10.text: Since he had much livestock in the foothills and in the plain, he built towers in the desert and dug many cisterns. And since he was a lover of the soil, he had farmers and vinedressers in the hill country and in the fertile fields.
2CH 26:10.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26 · Love] Since he had much livestock in the foothills and in the plain, he built towers in the desert and dug many cisterns. And since he was a lover of the soil, he had farmers and vinedressers in the hill country and in the fertile fields.

2CH 26:11.text: Uzziah had an army ready for battle that went out to war by assigned divisions, as recorded by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer under the direction of Hananiah, one of the royal officers.
2CH 26:11.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26 · Guidance] Uzziah had an army ready for battle that went out to war by assigned divisions, as recorded by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer under the direction of Hananiah, one of the royal officers.

2CH 26:12.text: The total number of family leaders of the mighty men of valor was 2,600.
2CH 26:12.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26 · Family] The total number of family leaders of the mighty men of valor was 2,600.

2CH 26:13.text: Under their authority was an army of 307,500 trained for war, a powerful force to support the king against his enemies.
2CH 26:13.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] Under their authority was an army of 307,500 trained for war, a powerful force to support the king against his enemies.

2CH 26:14.text: Uzziah supplied the entire army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and slingstones.
2CH 26:14.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26 · Armor of God] Uzziah supplied the entire army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and slingstones.

2CH 26:15.text: And in Jerusalem he made skillfully designed devices to shoot arrows and catapult large stones from the towers and corners. So his fame spread far and wide, for he was helped tremendously so that he became powerful.
2CH 26:15.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] And in Jerusalem he made skillfully designed devices to shoot arrows and catapult large stones from the towers and corners. So his fame spread far and wide, for he was helped tremendously so that he became powerful.

2CH 26:16.text: But when Uzziah grew powerful, his arrogance led to his own destruction. He was unfaithful to the LORD his God, for he entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
2CH 26:16.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26 · Faith, Devote To Destruction] But when Uzziah grew powerful, his arrogance led to his own destruction. He was unfaithful to the LORD his God, for he entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.

2CH 26:17.text: Then Azariah the priest, along with eighty brave priests of the LORD, went in after him.
2CH 26:17.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] Then Azariah the priest, along with eighty brave priests of the LORD, went in after him.

2CH 26:18.text: They took their stand against King Uzziah and said, “Uzziah, you have no right to offer incense to the LORD. Only the priests, the descendants of Aaron, are consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully; you will not receive honor from the LORD God.”
2CH 26:18.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26 · Faith] They took their stand against King Uzziah and said, “Uzziah, you have no right to offer incense to the LORD. Only the priests, the descendants of Aaron, are consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully; you will not receive honor from the LORD God.”

2CH 26:19.text: Uzziah, with a censer in his hand to offer incense, was enraged. But while he raged against the priests in their presence in the house of the LORD before the altar of incense, leprosy broke out on his forehead.
2CH 26:19.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] Uzziah, with a censer in his hand to offer incense, was enraged. But while he raged against the priests in their presence in the house of the LORD before the altar of incense, leprosy broke out on his forehead.

2CH 26:20.text: When Azariah the chief priest and all the priests turned to him and saw his leprous forehead, they rushed him out. Indeed, he himself hurried to get out, because the LORD had afflicted him.
2CH 26:20.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] When Azariah the chief priest and all the priests turned to him and saw his leprous forehead, they rushed him out. Indeed, he himself hurried to get out, because the LORD had afflicted him.

2CH 26:21.text: So King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death. He lived in isolation, leprous and cut off from the house of the LORD, while his son Jotham had charge of the royal palace to govern the people of the land.
2CH 26:21.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26 · Death] So King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death. He lived in isolation, leprous and cut off from the house of the LORD, while his son Jotham had charge of the royal palace to govern the people of the land.

2CH 26:22.text: As for the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from beginning to end, they are recorded by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
2CH 26:22.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] As for the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from beginning to end, they are recorded by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

2CH 26:23.text: And Uzziah rested with his fathers and was buried near them in a field of burial that belonged to the kings; for the people said, “He was a leper.” And his son Jotham reigned in his place.
2CH 26:23.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 26] And Uzziah rested with his fathers and was buried near them in a field of burial that belonged to the kings; for the people said, “He was a leper.” And his son Jotham reigned in his place.

2CH 27:1.text: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. His mother’s name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
2CH 27:1.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 27] Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. His mother’s name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.

2CH 27:2.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Uzziah had done. In addition, he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people still behaved corruptly.
2CH 27:2.bm25Text: [2 Chronicles · Chapter 27 · God the Father] And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Uzziah had done. In addition, he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people still behaved corruptly.

2CO 1:5.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Comfort] For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.

2CO 1:6.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 1 · Comfort] If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience.

2CO 1:7.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 1 · Comfort] And our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort.

2CO 1:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 1] We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.

2CO 1:16.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 1] I wanted to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and to return to you from Macedonia, and then to have you help me on my way to Judea.

2CO 3:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3] Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?

2CO 3:2.text: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
2CO 3:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3] You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.

2CO 3:3.text: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
2CO 3:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Fruit of the Spirit] It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.

2CO 3:4.text: Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.
2CO 3:4.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3 · Assurance, Body of Christ] Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.

2CO 3:5.text: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.
2CO 3:5.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3] Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.

2CO 3:6.text: And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
2CO 3:6.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Fruit of the Spirit] And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

2CO 3:7.text: Now if the ministry of death, which was engraved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of its fleeting glory,

2CO 3:8.text: will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?
2CO 3:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3 · Fruit of the Spirit] will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?

2CO 3:9.text: For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!
2CO 3:9.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3] For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!

2CO 3:10.text: Indeed, what was once glorious has no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it.
2CO 3:10.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3 · Glory] Indeed, what was once glorious has no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it.

2CO 3:11.text: For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which endures!
2CO 3:11.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3 · Glory] For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which endures!

2CO 3:12.text: Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.
2CO 3:12.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3] Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.

2CO 3:13.text: We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.
2CO 3:13.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3] We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.

2CO 3:14.text: But their minds were closed. For to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed.
2CO 3:14.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Covenant] But their minds were closed. For to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed.

2CO 3:15.text: And even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.
2CO 3:15.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3] And even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.

2CO 3:16.text: But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
2CO 3:16.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3] But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

2CO 3:17.text: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
2CO 3:17.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3 · Freedom, Fruit of the Spirit] Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

2CO 3:18.text: And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
2CO 3:18.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 3 · Fruit of the Spirit, Glory] And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

2CO 4:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Forgiveness, Adultery In Heart] Therefore, since God in His mercy has given us this ministry, we do not lose heart.

2CO 4:2.text: Instead, we have renounced secret and shameful ways. We do not practice deceit, nor do we distort the word of God. On the contrary, by open proclamation of the truth, we commend ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
2CO 4:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Deceit] Instead, we have renounced secret and shameful ways. We do not practice deceit, nor do we distort the word of God. On the contrary, by open proclamation of the truth, we commend ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

2CO 4:3.text: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.
2CO 4:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Gospel] And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.

2CO 4:4.text: The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
2CO 4:4.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Faith, Body of Christ] The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

2CO 4:5.text: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.
2CO 4:5.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.

2CO 4:6.text: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
2CO 4:6.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Body of Christ, Glory] For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

2CO 4:7.text: Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.
2CO 4:7.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4] Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.

2CO 4:8.text: We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;
2CO 4:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4] We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;

2CO 4:9.text: persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.
2CO 4:9.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4] persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.

2CO 4:10.text: We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
2CO 4:10.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Death, Jesus Christ] We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.

2CO 4:11.text: For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.
2CO 4:11.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Death, Jesus Christ] For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.

2CO 4:12.text: So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
2CO 4:12.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Death] So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.

2CO 4:13.text: And in keeping with what is written: “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak,
2CO 4:13.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Faith, Fruit of the Spirit] And in keeping with what is written: “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak,

2CO 4:14.text: knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.
2CO 4:14.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Jesus Christ] knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.

2CO 4:15.text: All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may overflow in thanksgiving, to the glory of God.
2CO 4:15.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Glory, Grace] All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may overflow in thanksgiving, to the glory of God.

2CO 4:16.text: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
2CO 4:16.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Adultery In Heart] Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.

2CO 4:17.text: For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond comparison.
2CO 4:17.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Eternal Life, Glory] For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond comparison.

2CO 4:18.text: So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.
2CO 4:18.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 4 · Eternal Life] So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.

2CO 5:1.text: Now we know that if the earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.
2CO 5:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Eternal Life, Heaven] Now we know that if the earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.

2CO 5:2.text: For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,
2CO 5:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,

2CO 5:3.text: because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.
2CO 5:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.

2CO 5:4.text: So while we are in this tent, we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life.
2CO 5:4.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] So while we are in this tent, we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life.

2CO 5:5.text: And God has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.
2CO 5:5.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Fruit of the Spirit] And God has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.

2CO 5:6.text: Therefore we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.
2CO 5:6.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] Therefore we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.

2CO 5:7.text: For we walk by faith, not by sight.
2CO 5:7.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Faith] For we walk by faith, not by sight.

2CO 5:8.text: We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
2CO 5:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.

2CO 5:9.text: So we aspire to please Him, whether we are here in this body or away from it.
2CO 5:9.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] So we aspire to please Him, whether we are here in this body or away from it.

2CO 5:10.text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.
2CO 5:10.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.

2CO 5:11.text: Therefore, since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade men. What we are is clear to God, and I hope it is clear to your conscience as well.
2CO 5:11.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] Therefore, since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade men. What we are is clear to God, and I hope it is clear to your conscience as well.

2CO 5:12.text: We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in the heart.
2CO 5:12.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Adultery In Heart, Generosity] We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in the heart.

2CO 5:13.text: If we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
2CO 5:13.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] If we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.

2CO 5:14.text: For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that One died for all, therefore all died.
2CO 5:14.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Love, Body of Christ] For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that One died for all, therefore all died.

2CO 5:15.text: And He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.
2CO 5:15.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] And He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.

2CO 5:16.text: So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.
2CO 5:16.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.

2CO 5:17.text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!
2CO 5:17.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Body of Christ, Creation] Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!

2CO 5:18.text: All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
2CO 5:18.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Atonement, Body of Christ] All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:

2CO 5:19.text: that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men’s trespasses against them. And He has committed to us the message of reconciliation.
2CO 5:19.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Atonement, Body of Christ] that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men’s trespasses against them. And He has committed to us the message of reconciliation.

2CO 5:20.text: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.
2CO 5:20.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.

2CO 5:21.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 5] God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.

2CO 6:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · Grace] As God’s fellow workers, then, we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.

2CO 6:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · Blessing] For He says:  “In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.”   Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!

2CO 6:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6] We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no one can discredit our ministry.

2CO 6:4.text: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;
2CO 6:4.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6] Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;

2CO 6:5.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6] in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;

2CO 6:6.text: in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;
2CO 6:6.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · Love, Fruit of the Spirit] in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;

2CO 6:7.text: in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;
2CO 6:7.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6] in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;

2CO 6:8.text: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;
2CO 6:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · Glory] through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;

2CO 6:9.text: as unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;
2CO 6:9.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6] as unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;

2CO 6:10.text: sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
2CO 6:10.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · Joy] sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.

2CO 6:11.text: We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide.
2CO 6:11.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6] We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide.

2CO 6:12.text: It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.
2CO 6:12.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6] It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.

2CO 6:13.text: As a fair exchange, I ask you as my children: Open wide your hearts also.
2CO 6:13.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · Children] As a fair exchange, I ask you as my children: Open wide your hearts also.

2CO 6:14.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · Faith, Fellowship] Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?

2CO 6:15.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · Faith, Body of Christ] What harmony is there between Christ and Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?

2CO 6:16.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · Idolatry, Idols] What agreement can exist between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said:  “I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.”

2CO 6:17.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6] “Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”

2CO 6:18.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 6 · God the Father] And:  “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”

2CO 7:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 7 · Love, Fruit of the Spirit] Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

2CO 7:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 7] Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.

2CO 7:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 7] I do not say this to condemn you. I have said before that you so occupy our hearts that we live and die together with you.

2CO 7:4.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 7 · Assurance, Comfort] Great is my confidence in you; great is my pride in you; I am filled with encouragement; in all our troubles my joy overflows.

2CO 7:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 7] Even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Although I did regret it, I now see that my letter caused you sorrow, but only for a short time.

2CO 7:16.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 7 · Assurance] I rejoice that I can have complete confidence in you.
