2CO 8:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · About Forgiveness, Grace] Now, brothers, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the churches of Macedonia.

2CO 8:2.text: In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity.
2CO 8:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Charity, Generosity] In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity.

2CO 8:3.text: For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond it. Of their own accord,
2CO 8:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8] For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond it. Of their own accord,

2CO 8:4.text: they earnestly pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.
2CO 8:4.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8] they earnestly pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.

2CO 8:5.text: And not only did they do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, because it was the will of God.
2CO 8:5.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8] And not only did they do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, because it was the will of God.

2CO 8:6.text: So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.
2CO 8:6.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Grace] So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.

2CO 8:7.text: But just as you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you—see that you also excel in this grace of giving.
2CO 8:7.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Love, Faith] But just as you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you—see that you also excel in this grace of giving.

2CO 8:8.text: I am not making a demand, but I am testing the sincerity of your love in comparison to the earnestness of others.
2CO 8:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Love] I am not making a demand, but I am testing the sincerity of your love in comparison to the earnestness of others.

2CO 8:9.text: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.
2CO 8:9.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Body of Christ, Grace] For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.

2CO 8:10.text: And this is my opinion about what is helpful for you in this matter: Last year you were the first not only to give, but even to have such a desire.
2CO 8:10.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · About Forgiveness, Lust] And this is my opinion about what is helpful for you in this matter: Last year you were the first not only to give, but even to have such a desire.

2CO 8:11.text: Now finish the work, so that you may complete it just as eagerly as you began, according to your means.
2CO 8:11.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8] Now finish the work, so that you may complete it just as eagerly as you began, according to your means.

2CO 8:12.text: For if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what he does not have.
2CO 8:12.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8] For if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what he does not have.

2CO 8:13.text: It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality.
2CO 8:13.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Equality] It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality.

2CO 8:14.text: At the present time, your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need. Then there will be equality.
2CO 8:14.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Equality] At the present time, your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need. Then there will be equality.

2CO 8:15.text: As it is written:  “He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall.”
2CO 8:15.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8] As it is written:  “He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall.”

2CO 8:16.text: But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you.
2CO 8:16.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Adultery In Heart, Devotion] But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you.

2CO 8:17.text: For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition.
2CO 8:17.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8] For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition.

2CO 8:18.text: Along with Titus we are sending the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel.
2CO 8:18.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Gospel] Along with Titus we are sending the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel.

2CO 8:19.text: More than that, this brother was chosen by the churches to accompany us with the offering—the gracious gift we administer to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help.
2CO 8:19.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Election] More than that, this brother was chosen by the churches to accompany us with the offering—the gracious gift we administer to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help.

2CO 8:20.text: We hope to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift.
2CO 8:20.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8] We hope to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift.

2CO 8:21.text: For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men.
2CO 8:21.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8] For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men.

2CO 8:22.text: And we are sending along with them our brother whose earnestness has been proven many times and in many ways, and now even more so by his great confidence in you.
2CO 8:22.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Assurance, End Times] And we are sending along with them our brother whose earnestness has been proven many times and in many ways, and now even more so by his great confidence in you.

2CO 8:23.text: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, to the glory of Christ.
2CO 8:23.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Angels, Body of Christ] As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, to the glory of Christ.

2CO 8:24.text: In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you.
2CO 8:24.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 8 · Love, About Forgiveness] In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you.

2CO 9:1.text: Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you.
2CO 9:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · About Forgiveness] Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you.

2CO 9:2.text: For I know your eagerness to help, and I have been boasting to the Macedonians that since last year you in Achaia were prepared to give. And your zeal has stirred most of them to do likewise.
2CO 9:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9] For I know your eagerness to help, and I have been boasting to the Macedonians that since last year you in Achaia were prepared to give. And your zeal has stirred most of them to do likewise.

2CO 9:3.text: But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said.
2CO 9:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · About Forgiveness] But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said.

2CO 9:4.text: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed of having been so confident.
2CO 9:4.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed of having been so confident.

2CO 9:5.text: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you beforehand and make arrangements for the bountiful gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly.
2CO 9:5.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9] So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you beforehand and make arrangements for the bountiful gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly.

2CO 9:6.text: Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
2CO 9:6.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

2CO 9:7.text: Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.
2CO 9:7.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Love, Adultery In Heart] Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.

2CO 9:8.text: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.
2CO 9:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · End Times, Grace] And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.

2CO 9:9.text: As it is written:  “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”
2CO 9:9.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9] As it is written:  “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”

2CO 9:10.text: Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.
2CO 9:10.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.

2CO 9:11.text: You will be enriched in every way to be generous on every occasion, so that through us your giving will produce thanksgiving to God.
2CO 9:11.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Generosity, Gratitude] You will be enriched in every way to be generous on every occasion, so that through us your giving will produce thanksgiving to God.

2CO 9:12.text: For this ministry of service is not only supplying the needs of the saints, but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.
2CO 9:12.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Gratitude] For this ministry of service is not only supplying the needs of the saints, but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.

2CO 9:13.text: Because of the proof this ministry provides, the saints will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all the others.
2CO 9:13.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Body of Christ, Charity] Because of the proof this ministry provides, the saints will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all the others.

2CO 9:14.text: And their prayers for you will express their affection for you, because of the surpassing grace God has given you.
2CO 9:14.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9 · Grace] And their prayers for you will express their affection for you, because of the surpassing grace God has given you.

2CO 9:15.text: Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!
2CO 9:15.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 9] Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!

2CO 10:1.text: Now by the mildness and gentleness of Christ, I appeal to you—I, Paul, who am humble when face to face with you, but bold when away.
2CO 10:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Body of Christ, Gentleness] Now by the mildness and gentleness of Christ, I appeal to you—I, Paul, who am humble when face to face with you, but bold when away.

2CO 10:2.text: I beg you that when I come I may not need to be as bold as I expect toward those who presume that we live according to the flesh.
2CO 10:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] I beg you that when I come I may not need to be as bold as I expect toward those who presume that we live according to the flesh.

2CO 10:3.text: For though we live in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
2CO 10:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] For though we live in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.

2CO 10:4.text: The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the world. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.
2CO 10:4.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the world. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.

2CO 10:5.text: We tear down arguments and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God; and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
2CO 10:5.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] We tear down arguments and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God; and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.

2CO 10:6.text: And we will be ready to punish every act of disobedience, as soon as your obedience is complete.
2CO 10:6.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] And we will be ready to punish every act of disobedience, as soon as your obedience is complete.

2CO 10:7.text: You are looking at outward appearances. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should remind himself that we belong to Christ just as much as he does.
2CO 10:7.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] You are looking at outward appearances. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should remind himself that we belong to Christ just as much as he does.

2CO 10:8.text: For even if I boast somewhat excessively about the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.
2CO 10:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · About Forgiveness] For even if I boast somewhat excessively about the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.

2CO 10:9.text: I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters.
2CO 10:9.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters.

2CO 10:10.text: For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”
2CO 10:10.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”

2CO 10:11.text: Such people should consider that what we are in our letters when absent, we will be in our actions when present.
2CO 10:11.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] Such people should consider that what we are in our letters when absent, we will be in our actions when present.

2CO 10:12.text: We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they show their ignorance.
2CO 10:12.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they show their ignorance.

2CO 10:13.text: We, however, will not boast beyond our limits, but only within the field of influence that God has assigned to us—a field that reaches even to you.
2CO 10:13.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] We, however, will not boast beyond our limits, but only within the field of influence that God has assigned to us—a field that reaches even to you.

2CO 10:14.text: We are not overstepping our bounds, as if we had not come to you. Indeed, we were the first to reach you with the gospel of Christ.
2CO 10:14.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Body of Christ, Gospel] We are not overstepping our bounds, as if we had not come to you. Indeed, we were the first to reach you with the gospel of Christ.

2CO 10:15.text: Neither do we boast beyond our limits in the labors of others. But we hope that as your faith increases, our area of influence among you will greatly increase as well,
2CO 10:15.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Faith] Neither do we boast beyond our limits in the labors of others. But we hope that as your faith increases, our area of influence among you will greatly increase as well,

2CO 10:16.text: so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. Then we will not be boasting in the work already done in another man’s territory.
2CO 10:16.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10 · Gospel] so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. Then we will not be boasting in the work already done in another man’s territory.

2CO 10:17.text: Rather, “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”
2CO 10:17.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] Rather, “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”

2CO 10:18.text: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
2CO 10:18.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 10] For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.

2CO 11:1.text: I hope you will bear with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.
2CO 11:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] I hope you will bear with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.

2CO 11:2.text: I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
2CO 11:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Body of Christ, Jealousy] I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.

2CO 11:3.text: I am afraid, however, that just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning, your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.
2CO 11:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Body of Christ, Devotion] I am afraid, however, that just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning, your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.

2CO 11:4.text: For if someone comes and proclaims a Jesus other than the One we proclaimed, or if you receive a different spirit than the One you received, or a different gospel than the one you accepted, you put up with it way too easily.
2CO 11:4.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Fruit of the Spirit, Gospel] For if someone comes and proclaims a Jesus other than the One we proclaimed, or if you receive a different spirit than the One you received, or a different gospel than the one you accepted, you put up with it way too easily.

2CO 11:5.text: I consider myself in no way inferior to those “super-apostles.”
2CO 11:5.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Apostles] I consider myself in no way inferior to those “super-apostles.”

2CO 11:6.text: Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge. We have made this clear to you in every way possible.
2CO 11:6.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge. We have made this clear to you in every way possible.

2CO 11:7.text: Was it a sin for me to humble myself in order to exalt you, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?
2CO 11:7.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Gospel] Was it a sin for me to humble myself in order to exalt you, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?

2CO 11:8.text: I robbed other churches by accepting their support in order to serve you.
2CO 11:8.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] I robbed other churches by accepting their support in order to serve you.

2CO 11:9.text: And when I was with you and in need, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my needs. I have refrained from being a burden to you in any way, and I will continue to do so.
2CO 11:9.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] And when I was with you and in need, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my needs. I have refrained from being a burden to you in any way, and I will continue to do so.

2CO 11:10.text: As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
2CO 11:10.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.

2CO 11:11.text: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
2CO 11:11.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Love] Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!

2CO 11:12.text: But I will keep on doing what I am doing, in order to undercut those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things of which they boast.
2CO 11:12.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] But I will keep on doing what I am doing, in order to undercut those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things of which they boast.

2CO 11:13.text: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.
2CO 11:13.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Apostles, Body of Christ] For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.

2CO 11:14.text: And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.
2CO 11:14.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Light] And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.

2CO 11:15.text: It is not surprising, then, if his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their actions.
2CO 11:15.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] It is not surprising, then, if his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their actions.

2CO 11:16.text: I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
2CO 11:16.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.

2CO 11:17.text: In this confident boasting of mine, I am not speaking as the Lord would, but as a fool.
2CO 11:17.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] In this confident boasting of mine, I am not speaking as the Lord would, but as a fool.

2CO 11:18.text: Since many are boasting according to the flesh, I too will boast.
2CO 11:18.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Since many are boasting according to the flesh, I too will boast.

2CO 11:19.text: For you gladly tolerate fools, since you are so wise.
2CO 11:19.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] For you gladly tolerate fools, since you are so wise.

2CO 11:20.text: In fact, you even put up with anyone who enslaves you or exploits you or takes advantage of you or exalts himself or strikes you in the face.
2CO 11:20.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] In fact, you even put up with anyone who enslaves you or exploits you or takes advantage of you or exalts himself or strikes you in the face.

2CO 11:21.text: To my shame I concede that we were too weak for that!  Speaking as a fool, however, I can match what anyone else dares to boast about.
2CO 11:21.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · About Forgiveness] To my shame I concede that we were too weak for that!  Speaking as a fool, however, I can match what anyone else dares to boast about.

2CO 11:22.text: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
2CO 11:22.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.

2CO 11:23.text: Are they servants of Christ? I am speaking like I am out of my mind, but I am so much more: in harder labor, in more imprisonments, in worse beatings, in frequent danger of death.
2CO 11:23.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · Body of Christ, Death] Are they servants of Christ? I am speaking like I am out of my mind, but I am so much more: in harder labor, in more imprisonments, in worse beatings, in frequent danger of death.

2CO 11:24.text: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
2CO 11:24.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · End Times] Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.

2CO 11:25.text: Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.
2CO 11:25.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · End Times] Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.

2CO 11:26.text: In my frequent journeys, I have been in danger from rivers and from bandits, in danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles, in danger in the city and in the country, in danger on the sea and among false brothers,
2CO 11:26.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · False Gods, False Witness] In my frequent journeys, I have been in danger from rivers and from bandits, in danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles, in danger in the city and in the country, in danger on the sea and among false brothers,

2CO 11:27.text: in labor and toil and often without sleep, in hunger and thirst and often without food, in cold and exposure.
2CO 11:27.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] in labor and toil and often without sleep, in hunger and thirst and often without food, in cold and exposure.

2CO 11:28.text: Apart from these external trials, I face daily the pressure of my concern for all the churches.
2CO 11:28.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Apart from these external trials, I face daily the pressure of my concern for all the churches.

2CO 11:29.text: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?
2CO 11:29.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?

2CO 11:30.text: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
2CO 11:30.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.

2CO 11:31.text: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying.
2CO 11:31.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11 · God the Father, Jesus Christ] The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying.

2CO 11:32.text: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas secured the city of the Damascenes in order to arrest me.
2CO 11:32.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas secured the city of the Damascenes in order to arrest me.

2CO 11:33.text: But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.
2CO 11:33.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 11] But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.

2CO 12:1.text: I must go on boasting. Although there is nothing to gain, I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
2CO 12:1.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 12] I must go on boasting. Although there is nothing to gain, I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.

2CO 12:2.text: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven. Whether it was in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows.
2CO 12:2.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 12 · Body of Christ, Heaven] I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven. Whether it was in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows.

2CO 12:3.text: And I know that this man—whether in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows—
2CO 12:3.bm25Text: [2 Corinthians · Chapter 12] And I know that this man—whether in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows—

2CO 12:4.text: was caught up to Paradise. The things he heard were too sacred for words, things that man is not permitted to tell.

2SA 1:1.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Death] After the death of Saul, David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and stayed in Ziklag two days.

2SA 1:2.text: On the third day a man with torn clothes and dust on his head arrived from Saul’s camp. When he came to David, he fell to the ground to pay him homage.
2SA 1:2.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] On the third day a man with torn clothes and dust on his head arrived from Saul’s camp. When he came to David, he fell to the ground to pay him homage.

2SA 1:3.text: “Where have you come from?” David asked.  “I have escaped from the Israelite camp,” he replied.
2SA 1:3.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] “Where have you come from?” David asked.  “I have escaped from the Israelite camp,” he replied.

2SA 1:4.text: “What was the outcome?” David asked. “Please tell me.”  “The troops fled from the battle,” he replied. “Many of them fell and died. And Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”
2SA 1:4.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] “What was the outcome?” David asked. “Please tell me.”  “The troops fled from the battle,” he replied. “Many of them fell and died. And Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”

2SA 1:5.text: Then David asked the young man who had brought him the report, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”
2SA 1:5.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] Then David asked the young man who had brought him the report, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”

2SA 1:6.text: “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa,” he replied, “and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the cavalry closing in on him.
2SA 1:6.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa,” he replied, “and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the cavalry closing in on him.

2SA 1:7.text: When he turned around and saw me, he called out and I answered, ‘Here I am!’
2SA 1:7.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] When he turned around and saw me, he called out and I answered, ‘Here I am!’

2SA 1:8.text: ‘Who are you?’ he asked.  So I told him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
2SA 1:8.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Amalekite] ‘Who are you?’ he asked.  So I told him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’

2SA 1:9.text: Then he begged me, ‘Stand over me and kill me, for agony has seized me, but my life still lingers.’
2SA 1:9.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] Then he begged me, ‘Stand over me and kill me, for agony has seized me, but my life still lingers.’

2SA 1:10.text: So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew that after he had fallen he could not survive. And I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”
2SA 1:10.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew that after he had fallen he could not survive. And I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”

2SA 1:11.text: Then David took hold of his own clothes and tore them, and all the men who were with him did the same.
2SA 1:11.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] Then David took hold of his own clothes and tore them, and all the men who were with him did the same.

2SA 1:12.text: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
2SA 1:12.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Israel] They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

2SA 1:13.text: And David inquired of the young man who had brought him the report, “Where are you from?”  “I am the son of a foreigner,” he answered. “I am an Amalekite.”
2SA 1:13.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Amalekite] And David inquired of the young man who had brought him the report, “Where are you from?”  “I am the son of a foreigner,” he answered. “I am an Amalekite.”

2SA 1:14.text: So David asked him, “Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”
2SA 1:14.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] So David asked him, “Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”

2SA 1:15.text: Then David summoned one of the young men and said, “Go, execute him!” So the young man struck him down, and he died.
2SA 1:15.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Calling] Then David summoned one of the young men and said, “Go, execute him!” So the young man struck him down, and he died.

2SA 1:16.text: For David had said to the Amalekite, “Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the LORD’s anointed.’”
2SA 1:16.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Amalekite] For David had said to the Amalekite, “Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the LORD’s anointed.’”

2SA 1:17.text: Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,
2SA 1:17.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,

2SA 1:18.text: and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:
2SA 1:18.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:

2SA 1:19.text: “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!
2SA 1:19.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Glory, Israel] “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!

2SA 1:20.text: Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
2SA 1:20.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

2SA 1:21.text: O mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.
2SA 1:21.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] O mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.

2SA 1:22.text: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not retreat, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
2SA 1:22.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not retreat, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

2SA 1:23.text: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
2SA 1:23.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Love, Death] Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

2SA 1:24.text: O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.
2SA 1:24.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Israel] O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.

2SA 1:25.text: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.
2SA 1:25.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.

2SA 1:26.text: I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.
2SA 1:26.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1 · Love, Biblical Women] I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.

2SA 1:27.text: How the mighty have fallen and the weapons of war have perished!”
2SA 1:27.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 1] How the mighty have fallen and the weapons of war have perished!”

2SA 2:1.text: Some time later, David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?”  “Go up,” the LORD answered.  Then David asked, “Where should I go?”  “To Hebron,” replied the LORD.
2SA 2:1.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] Some time later, David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?”  “Go up,” the LORD answered.  Then David asked, “Where should I go?”  “To Hebron,” replied the LORD.

2SA 2:2.text: So David went there with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.
2SA 2:2.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] So David went there with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

2SA 2:3.text: David also took the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns near Hebron.
2SA 2:3.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2 · Family] David also took the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns near Hebron.

2SA 2:4.text: Then the men of Judah came to Hebron, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, “It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.”
2SA 2:4.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] Then the men of Judah came to Hebron, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, “It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.”

2SA 2:5.text: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead to tell them, “The LORD bless you, because you showed this kindness to Saul your lord when you buried him.
2SA 2:5.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2 · Angels, Grace] So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead to tell them, “The LORD bless you, because you showed this kindness to Saul your lord when you buried him.

2SA 2:6.text: Now may the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness, and I will also show you the same favor because you have done this.
2SA 2:6.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2 · Faith, Blessing] Now may the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness, and I will also show you the same favor because you have done this.

2SA 2:7.text: Now then, be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead, the house of Judah has anointed me as their king.”
2SA 2:7.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] Now then, be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead, the house of Judah has anointed me as their king.”

2SA 2:8.text: Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul’s army, took Saul’s son Ish-bosheth, moved him to Mahanaim,
2SA 2:8.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul’s army, took Saul’s son Ish-bosheth, moved him to Mahanaim,

2SA 2:9.text: and made him king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin—over all Israel.
2SA 2:9.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2 · Israel] and made him king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin—over all Israel.

2SA 2:10.text: Saul’s son Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned for two years.  The house of Judah, however, followed David.
2SA 2:10.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2 · Israel] Saul’s son Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned for two years.  The house of Judah, however, followed David.

2SA 2:11.text: And the length of time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
2SA 2:11.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] And the length of time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

2SA 2:12.text: One day Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
2SA 2:12.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] One day Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

2SA 2:13.text: So Joab son of Zeruiah, along with the servants of David, marched out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. And the two camps took up positions on opposite sides of the pool.
2SA 2:13.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] So Joab son of Zeruiah, along with the servants of David, marched out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. And the two camps took up positions on opposite sides of the pool.

2SA 2:14.text: Then Abner said to Joab, “Let us have the young men get up and compete before us.”  “Let them get up,” Joab replied.
2SA 2:14.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] Then Abner said to Joab, “Let us have the young men get up and compete before us.”  “Let them get up,” Joab replied.

2SA 2:15.text: So they got up and were counted off—twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve for David.
2SA 2:15.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] So they got up and were counted off—twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve for David.

2SA 2:16.text: Then each man grabbed his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, and they all fell together. So this place, which is in Gibeon, is called Helkath-hazzurim.
2SA 2:16.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] Then each man grabbed his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, and they all fell together. So this place, which is in Gibeon, is called Helkath-hazzurim.

2SA 2:17.text: The battle that day was intense, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by the servants of David.
2SA 2:17.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2 · Israel] The battle that day was intense, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by the servants of David.

2SA 2:18.text: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Now Asahel was fleet of foot like a wild gazelle,
2SA 2:18.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Now Asahel was fleet of foot like a wild gazelle,

2SA 2:19.text: and he chased Abner, not turning to the right or to the left in his pursuit.
2SA 2:19.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] and he chased Abner, not turning to the right or to the left in his pursuit.

2SA 2:20.text: And Abner glanced back and said, “Is that you, Asahel?”  “It is,” Asahel replied.
2SA 2:20.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] And Abner glanced back and said, “Is that you, Asahel?”  “It is,” Asahel replied.

2SA 2:21.text: So Abner told him, “Turn to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men, and take his equipment for yourself.”  But Asahel would not stop chasing him.
2SA 2:21.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] So Abner told him, “Turn to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men, and take his equipment for yourself.”  But Asahel would not stop chasing him.

2SA 2:22.text: Once again, Abner warned Asahel, “Stop chasing me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I show my face to your brother Joab?”
2SA 2:22.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] Once again, Abner warned Asahel, “Stop chasing me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I show my face to your brother Joab?”

2SA 2:23.text: But Asahel refused to turn away; so Abner thrust the butt of his spear into his stomach, and it came out his back, and he fell dead on the spot. And every man paused when he came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died.
2SA 2:23.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] But Asahel refused to turn away; so Abner thrust the butt of his spear into his stomach, and it came out his back, and he fell dead on the spot. And every man paused when he came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died.

2SA 2:24.text: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. By sunset, they had gone as far as the hill of Ammah opposite Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.
2SA 2:24.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. By sunset, they had gone as far as the hill of Ammah opposite Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

2SA 2:25.text: The Benjamites rallied to Abner, formed a single unit, and took their stand atop a hill.
2SA 2:25.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] The Benjamites rallied to Abner, formed a single unit, and took their stand atop a hill.

2SA 2:26.text: Then Abner called out to Joab: “Must the sword devour forever? Do you not realize that this will only end in bitterness? How long before you tell the troops to stop pursuing their brothers?”
2SA 2:26.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] Then Abner called out to Joab: “Must the sword devour forever? Do you not realize that this will only end in bitterness? How long before you tell the troops to stop pursuing their brothers?”

2SA 2:27.text: “As surely as God lives,” Joab replied, “if you had not spoken up, the troops would have continued pursuing their brothers until morning.”
2SA 2:27.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] “As surely as God lives,” Joab replied, “if you had not spoken up, the troops would have continued pursuing their brothers until morning.”

2SA 2:28.text: So Joab blew the ram’s horn, and all the troops stopped; they no longer pursued Israel or continued to fight.
2SA 2:28.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2 · Israel] So Joab blew the ram’s horn, and all the troops stopped; they no longer pursued Israel or continued to fight.

2SA 2:29.text: And all that night Abner and his men marched through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, marched all morning, and arrived at Mahanaim.
2SA 2:29.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] And all that night Abner and his men marched through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, marched all morning, and arrived at Mahanaim.

2SA 2:30.text: When Joab returned from pursuing Abner, he gathered all the troops.  In addition to Asahel, nineteen of David’s servants were missing,
2SA 2:30.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] When Joab returned from pursuing Abner, he gathered all the troops.  In addition to Asahel, nineteen of David’s servants were missing,

2SA 2:31.text: but they had struck down 360 Benjamites who were with Abner.
2SA 2:31.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2] but they had struck down 360 Benjamites who were with Abner.

2SA 2:32.text: Later, they took Asahel and buried him in his father’s tomb in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night and reached Hebron at daybreak.
2SA 2:32.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 2 · God the Father] Later, they took Asahel and buried him in his father’s tomb in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night and reached Hebron at daybreak.

2SA 3:1.text: Now the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was protracted. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.
2SA 3:1.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] Now the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was protracted. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.

2SA 3:2.text: And sons were born to David in Hebron:  His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;
2SA 3:2.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] And sons were born to David in Hebron:  His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;

2SA 3:3.text: his second was Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel;   his third was Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur;
2SA 3:3.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] his second was Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel;   his third was Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur;

2SA 3:4.text: his fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith;   his fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital;
2SA 3:4.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] his fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith;   his fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital;

2SA 3:5.text: and his sixth was Ithream, by David’s wife Eglah.   These sons were born to David in Hebron.
2SA 3:5.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] and his sixth was Ithream, by David’s wife Eglah.   These sons were born to David in Hebron.

2SA 3:6.text: During the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner had continued to strengthen his position in the house of Saul.
2SA 3:6.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] During the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner had continued to strengthen his position in the house of Saul.

2SA 3:7.text: Meanwhile, Saul had a concubine named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. So Ish-bosheth questioned Abner, “Why did you sleep with my father’s concubine?”
2SA 3:7.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · God the Father] Meanwhile, Saul had a concubine named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. So Ish-bosheth questioned Abner, “Why did you sleep with my father’s concubine?”

2SA 3:8.text: Abner was furious over Ish-bosheth’s accusation. “Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah?” he asked. “All this time I have been loyal to the house of your father Saul, to his brothers, and to his friends. I have not delivered you into the hand of David, but now you accuse me of wrongdoing with this woman!
2SA 3:8.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · God the Father] Abner was furious over Ish-bosheth’s accusation. “Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah?” he asked. “All this time I have been loyal to the house of your father Saul, to his brothers, and to his friends. I have not delivered you into the hand of David, but now you accuse me of wrongdoing with this woman!

2SA 3:9.text: May God punish Abner, and ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the LORD has sworn to him:
2SA 3:9.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] May God punish Abner, and ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the LORD has sworn to him:

2SA 3:10.text: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”
2SA 3:10.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · Israel, Kingdom of God] to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”

2SA 3:11.text: And for fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth did not dare to say another word to him.
2SA 3:11.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] And for fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth did not dare to say another word to him.

2SA 3:12.text: Then Abner sent messengers in his place to say to David, “To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and surely my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”
2SA 3:12.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · Angels, Covenant] Then Abner sent messengers in his place to say to David, “To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and surely my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”

2SA 3:13.text: “Good,” replied David, “I will make a covenant with you. But there is one thing I require of you: Do not appear before me unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to see me.”
2SA 3:13.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · Covenant] “Good,” replied David, “I will make a covenant with you. But there is one thing I require of you: Do not appear before me unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to see me.”

2SA 3:14.text: Then David sent messengers to say to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, “Give me back my wife, Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred Philistine foreskins.”
2SA 3:14.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · Angels] Then David sent messengers to say to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, “Give me back my wife, Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred Philistine foreskins.”

2SA 3:15.text: So Ish-bosheth sent and took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish.
2SA 3:15.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] So Ish-bosheth sent and took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish.

2SA 3:16.text: Her husband followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go back.” So he returned home.
2SA 3:16.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] Her husband followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go back.” So he returned home.

2SA 3:17.text: Now Abner conferred with the elders of Israel and said, “In the past you sought David as your king.
2SA 3:17.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · Israel, Leadership] Now Abner conferred with the elders of Israel and said, “In the past you sought David as your king.

2SA 3:18.text: Now take action, because the LORD has said to David, ‘Through My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hands of the Philistines and of all their enemies.’”
2SA 3:18.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · Israel] Now take action, because the LORD has said to David, ‘Through My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hands of the Philistines and of all their enemies.’”

2SA 3:19.text: Abner also spoke to the Benjamites and went to Hebron to tell David all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.
2SA 3:19.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · Israel] Abner also spoke to the Benjamites and went to Hebron to tell David all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.

2SA 3:20.text: When Abner and twenty of his men came to David at Hebron, David held a feast for them.
2SA 3:20.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] When Abner and twenty of his men came to David at Hebron, David held a feast for them.

2SA 3:21.text: Then Abner said to David, “Let me go at once, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may rule over all that your heart desires.”  So David dismissed Abner, and he went in peace.
2SA 3:21.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3 · Adultery In Heart, Covenant] Then Abner said to David, “Let me go at once, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may rule over all that your heart desires.”  So David dismissed Abner, and he went in peace.

2SA 3:22.text: Just then David’s soldiers and Joab returned from a raid, bringing with them a great plunder. But Abner was not with David in Hebron because David had sent him on his way in peace.
2SA 3:22.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] Just then David’s soldiers and Joab returned from a raid, bringing with them a great plunder. But Abner was not with David in Hebron because David had sent him on his way in peace.

2SA 3:23.text: When Joab and all his troops arrived, he was informed, “Abner son of Ner came to see the king, who sent him on his way in peace.”
2SA 3:23.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] When Joab and all his troops arrived, he was informed, “Abner son of Ner came to see the king, who sent him on his way in peace.”

2SA 3:24.text: So Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you dismiss him? Now he is getting away!
2SA 3:24.bm25Text: [2 Samuel · Chapter 3] So Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you dismiss him? Now he is getting away!

2TH 2:15.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 2] Therefore, brothers, stand firm and cling to the traditions we taught you, whether by speech or by letter.

2TH 3:1.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may spread quickly and be held in honor, just as it was with you.

2TH 3:2.text: And pray that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men; for not everyone holds to the faith.
2TH 3:2.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3 · Faith] And pray that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men; for not everyone holds to the faith.

2TH 3:3.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3 · Faith] But the Lord is faithful, and He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.

2TH 3:5.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3 · Love, Body of Christ] May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love and Christ’s perseverance.

2TH 3:7.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not undisciplined among you,

2TH 3:8.text: nor did we eat anyone’s food without paying for it. Instead, in labor and toil, we worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to any of you.
2TH 3:8.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] nor did we eat anyone’s food without paying for it. Instead, in labor and toil, we worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to any of you.

2TH 3:9.text: Not that we lack this right, but we wanted to offer ourselves as an example for you to imitate.
2TH 3:9.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] Not that we lack this right, but we wanted to offer ourselves as an example for you to imitate.

2TH 3:10.text: For even while we were with you, we gave you this command: “If anyone is unwilling to work, he shall not eat.”
2TH 3:10.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] For even while we were with you, we gave you this command: “If anyone is unwilling to work, he shall not eat.”

2TH 3:11.text: Yet we hear that some of you are leading undisciplined lives and accomplishing nothing but being busybodies.
2TH 3:11.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] Yet we hear that some of you are leading undisciplined lives and accomplishing nothing but being busybodies.

2TH 3:12.text: We command and urge such people by our Lord Jesus Christ to begin working quietly to earn their own living.
2TH 3:12.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] We command and urge such people by our Lord Jesus Christ to begin working quietly to earn their own living.

2TH 3:13.text: But as for you, brothers, do not grow weary in well-doing.
2TH 3:13.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] But as for you, brothers, do not grow weary in well-doing.

2TH 3:14.text: Take note of anyone who does not obey the instructions we have given in this letter. Do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.
2TH 3:14.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] Take note of anyone who does not obey the instructions we have given in this letter. Do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.

2TH 3:15.text: Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.
2TH 3:15.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.

2TH 3:16.text: Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
2TH 3:16.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3 · End Times] Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.

2TH 3:17.text: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul. This is my mark in every letter; it is the way I write.
2TH 3:17.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3] This greeting is in my own hand—Paul. This is my mark in every letter; it is the way I write.

2TH 3:18.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.
2TH 3:18.bm25Text: [2 Thessalonians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Grace] The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.

2TI 1:1.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise of life in Christ Jesus,
2TI 1:1.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Covenant] Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise of life in Christ Jesus,

2TI 1:2.text: To Timothy, my beloved child:  Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
2TI 1:2.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Forgiveness, Love] To Timothy, my beloved child:  Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

2TI 1:3.text: I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as did my forefathers, as I constantly remember you night and day in my prayers.
2TI 1:3.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1] I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as did my forefathers, as I constantly remember you night and day in my prayers.

2TI 1:4.text: Recalling your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy.
2TI 1:4.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1] Recalling your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy.

2TI 1:5.text: I am reminded of your sincere faith, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced is in you as well.
2TI 1:5.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Faith] I am reminded of your sincere faith, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced is in you as well.

2TI 1:6.text: For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
2TI 1:6.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1] For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.

2TI 1:7.text: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
2TI 1:7.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Love, Fruit of the Spirit] For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.

2TI 1:8.text: So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, or of me, His prisoner. Instead, join me in suffering for the gospel by the power of God.
2TI 1:8.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Gospel] So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, or of me, His prisoner. Instead, join me in suffering for the gospel by the power of God.

2TI 1:9.text: He has saved us and called us to a holy calling, not because of our works, but by His own purpose and by the grace He granted us in Christ Jesus before time began.
2TI 1:9.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Calling] He has saved us and called us to a holy calling, not because of our works, but by His own purpose and by the grace He granted us in Christ Jesus before time began.

2TI 1:10.text: And now He has revealed this grace through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who has abolished death and illuminated the way to life and immortality through the gospel,
2TI 1:10.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Death] And now He has revealed this grace through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who has abolished death and illuminated the way to life and immortality through the gospel,

2TI 1:11.text: to which I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher.
2TI 1:11.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1] to which I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher.

2TI 1:12.text: For this reason, even though I suffer as I do, I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him for that day.
2TI 1:12.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Faith] For this reason, even though I suffer as I do, I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him for that day.

2TI 1:13.text: Hold on to the pattern of sound teaching you have heard from me, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
2TI 1:13.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Love, Faith] Hold on to the pattern of sound teaching you have heard from me, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.

2TI 1:14.text: Guard the treasure entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
2TI 1:14.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Faith, Fruit of the Spirit] Guard the treasure entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.

2TI 1:15.text: You know that everyone in the Province of Asia has deserted me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
2TI 1:15.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1] You know that everyone in the Province of Asia has deserted me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.

2TI 1:16.text: May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he has often refreshed me and was unashamed of my chains.
2TI 1:16.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Forgiveness, Compassion] May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he has often refreshed me and was unashamed of my chains.

2TI 1:17.text: Indeed, when he arrived in Rome, he searched diligently until he found me.
2TI 1:17.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1] Indeed, when he arrived in Rome, he searched diligently until he found me.

2TI 1:18.text: May the Lord grant Onesiphorus His mercy on that day. You know very well how much he ministered to me in Ephesus.
2TI 1:18.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 1 · Forgiveness, Compassion] May the Lord grant Onesiphorus His mercy on that day. You know very well how much he ministered to me in Ephesus.

2TI 2:1.text: You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
2TI 2:1.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Body of Christ, Grace] You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.

2TI 2:2.text: And the things that you have heard me say among many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be qualified to teach others as well.
2TI 2:2.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Faith] And the things that you have heard me say among many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be qualified to teach others as well.

2TI 2:3.text: Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
2TI 2:3.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

2TI 2:4.text: A soldier refrains from entangling himself in civilian affairs, in order to please the one who enlisted him.
2TI 2:4.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] A soldier refrains from entangling himself in civilian affairs, in order to please the one who enlisted him.

2TI 2:5.text: Likewise, a competitor does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules.
2TI 2:5.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] Likewise, a competitor does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules.

2TI 2:6.text: The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops.
2TI 2:6.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops.

2TI 2:7.text: Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you insight into all things.
2TI 2:7.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you insight into all things.

2TI 2:8.text: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, as proclaimed by my gospel,
2TI 2:8.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Body of Christ, Gospel] Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, as proclaimed by my gospel,

2TI 2:9.text: for which I suffer to the extent of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God cannot be chained!
2TI 2:9.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] for which I suffer to the extent of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God cannot be chained!

2TI 2:10.text: For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
2TI 2:10.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Body of Christ, Eternal Life] For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.

2TI 2:11.text: This is a trustworthy saying:  If we died with Him, we will also live with Him;
2TI 2:11.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Faith] This is a trustworthy saying:  If we died with Him, we will also live with Him;

2TI 2:12.text: if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will also deny us;
2TI 2:12.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will also deny us;

2TI 2:13.text: if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
2TI 2:13.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Faith] if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.

2TI 2:14.text: Remind the believers of these things, charging them before God to avoid quarreling over words, which succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin.
2TI 2:14.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Faith] Remind the believers of these things, charging them before God to avoid quarreling over words, which succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin.

2TI 2:15.text: Make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.
2TI 2:15.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] Make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.

2TI 2:16.text: But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which will only lead to more ungodliness,
2TI 2:16.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which will only lead to more ungodliness,

2TI 2:17.text: and the talk of such men will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
2TI 2:17.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] and the talk of such men will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,

2TI 2:18.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Faith] who have deviated from the truth. They say that the resurrection has already occurred, and they undermine the faith of some.

2TI 2:19.text: Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.”
2TI 2:19.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.”

2TI 2:20.text: A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.
2TI 2:20.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.

2TI 2:21.text: So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work.
2TI 2:21.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work.

2TI 2:22.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2 · Love, Faith] Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.

2TI 2:23.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling.

2TI 2:24.text: And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing.
2TI 2:24.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing.

2TI 2:25.text: He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth.
2TI 2:25.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth.

2TI 2:26.text: Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will.
2TI 2:26.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 2] Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will.

2TI 3:1.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3 · End Times] But understand this: In the last days terrible times will come.

2TI 3:3.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3 · Forgiveness, Love] unloving, unforgiving, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, without love of good,

2TI 3:4.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3 · Love] traitorous, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,

2TI 3:5.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3] having a form of godliness but denying its power. Turn away from such as these!

2TI 3:6.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3 · Biblical Women, Heroic Women] They are the kind who worm their way into households and captivate vulnerable women who are weighed down with sins and led astray by various passions,

2TI 3:7.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3] who are always learning but never able to come to a knowledge of the truth.

2TI 3:8.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3 · Faith] Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so also these men oppose the truth. They are depraved in mind and disqualified from the faith.

2TI 3:9.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3] But they will not advance much further. For just like Jannes and Jambres, their folly will be plain to everyone.

2TI 3:10.text: You, however, have observed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my perseverance,
2TI 3:10.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3 · Love, Faith] You, however, have observed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my perseverance,

2TI 3:11.text: my persecutions, and the sufferings that came upon me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. What persecutions I endured! Yet the Lord rescued me from all of them.
2TI 3:11.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3] my persecutions, and the sufferings that came upon me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. What persecutions I endured! Yet the Lord rescued me from all of them.

2TI 3:12.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Indeed, all who desire to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted,

2TI 3:13.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3] while evil men and imposters go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.

2TI 3:14.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3 · Faith] But as for you, continue in the things you have learned and firmly believed, since you know from whom you have learned them.

2TI 3:15.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3 · Faith, Body of Christ] From infancy you have known the Holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.

2TI 3:16.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3] All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness,

2TI 3:17.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 3] so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.

2TI 4:1.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] I charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead, and in view of His appearing and His kingdom:

2TI 4:2.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4] Preach the word; be prepared in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and encourage with every form of patient instruction.

2TI 4:4.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4] So they will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths.

2TI 4:5.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4] But you, be sober in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry.

2TI 4:6.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4] For I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand.

2TI 4:7.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4 · Faith] I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.

2TI 4:9.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4] Make every effort to come to me quickly,

2TI 4:12.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4] Tychicus, however, I have sent to Ephesus.

2TI 4:14.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4] Alexander the coppersmith did great harm to me. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.

2TI 4:15.bm25Text: [2 Timothy · Chapter 4] You too should beware of him, for he has vigorously opposed our message.
