ACT 16:7.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Fruit of the Spirit, Jesus Christ] And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.

ACT 16:8.text: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
ACT 16:8.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.

ACT 16:9.text: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
ACT 16:9.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”

ACT 16:10.text: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.
ACT 16:10.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Gospel] As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.

ACT 16:11.text: We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.
ACT 16:11.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.

ACT 16:12.text: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.
ACT 16:12.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.

ACT 16:13.text: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.
ACT 16:13.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Biblical Women, Heroic Women] On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.

ACT 16:14.text: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.
ACT 16:14.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Adultery In Heart] Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.

ACT 16:15.text: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.
ACT 16:15.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Faith, Family] And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.

ACT 16:16.text: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.
ACT 16:16.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Fruit of the Spirit] One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.

ACT 16:17.text: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”
ACT 16:17.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”

ACT 16:18.text: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.
ACT 16:18.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Body of Christ, Fruit of the Spirit] She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.

ACT 16:19.text: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.
ACT 16:19.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.

ACT 16:20.text: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil
ACT 16:20.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil

ACT 16:21.text: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”
ACT 16:21.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Explain Romans] by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”

ACT 16:22.text: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.
ACT 16:22.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.

ACT 16:23.text: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.
ACT 16:23.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.

ACT 16:24.text: On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.
ACT 16:24.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.

ACT 16:25.text: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
ACT 16:25.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · About Forgiveness] About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.

ACT 16:26.text: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.
ACT 16:26.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.

ACT 16:27.text: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.
ACT 16:27.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · About Forgiveness] When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.

ACT 16:28.text: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”
ACT 16:28.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”

ACT 16:29.text: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.
ACT 16:29.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Calling] Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.

ACT 16:30.text: Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
ACT 16:30.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”

ACT 16:31.text: They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.”
ACT 16:31.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Faith, Family] They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.”

ACT 16:32.text: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.
ACT 16:32.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.

ACT 16:33.text: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.
ACT 16:33.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Family] At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.

ACT 16:34.text: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.
ACT 16:34.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Faith, Family] Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.

ACT 16:35.text: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”
ACT 16:35.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Freedom] When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”

ACT 16:36.text: The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”
ACT 16:36.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16 · Freedom] The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”

ACT 16:37.text: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”
ACT 16:37.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”

ACT 16:38.text: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
ACT 16:38.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.

ACT 16:39.text: They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.
ACT 16:39.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.

ACT 16:40.text: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.
ACT 16:40.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 16] After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.

ACT 17:1.text: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
ACT 17:1.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

ACT 17:2.text: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
ACT 17:2.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

ACT 17:3.text: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.
ACT 17:3.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.

ACT 17:4.text: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.
ACT 17:4.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Biblical Women, Heroic Women] Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.

ACT 17:5.text: The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.
ACT 17:5.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.

ACT 17:6.text: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,
ACT 17:6.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,

ACT 17:7.text: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”
ACT 17:7.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Jesus Christ] and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”

ACT 17:8.text: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.
ACT 17:8.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.

ACT 17:9.text: And they collected bond from Jason and the others, and then released them.
ACT 17:9.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] And they collected bond from Jason and the others, and then released them.

ACT 17:10.text: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
ACT 17:10.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

ACT 17:11.text: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.
ACT 17:11.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.

ACT 17:12.text: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.
ACT 17:12.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Faith, Biblical Women] As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.

ACT 17:13.text: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.
ACT 17:13.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.

ACT 17:14.text: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.
ACT 17:14.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.

ACT 17:15.text: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.
ACT 17:15.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.

ACT 17:16.text: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.
ACT 17:16.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Fruit of the Spirit, Idolatry] While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.

ACT 17:17.text: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.
ACT 17:17.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.

ACT 17:18.text: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
ACT 17:18.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Gospel, Jesus Christ] Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.

ACT 17:19.text: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?
ACT 17:19.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?

ACT 17:20.text: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”
ACT 17:20.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”

ACT 17:21.text: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.
ACT 17:21.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.

ACT 17:22.text: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.
ACT 17:22.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.

ACT 17:23.text: For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription:  TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.  Therefore what you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.
ACT 17:23.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription:  TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.  Therefore what you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.

ACT 17:24.text: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.
ACT 17:24.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Heaven] The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.

ACT 17:25.text: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.
ACT 17:25.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.

ACT 17:26.text: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.
ACT 17:26.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · End Times] From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.

ACT 17:27.text: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
ACT 17:27.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.

ACT 17:28.text: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’
ACT 17:28.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Children] ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’

ACT 17:29.text: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.
ACT 17:29.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Children, Graven Image] Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.

ACT 17:30.text: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.
ACT 17:30.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · End Times] Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.

ACT 17:31.text: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
ACT 17:31.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Justice] For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”

ACT 17:32.text: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”
ACT 17:32.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · About Forgiveness] When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”

ACT 17:33.text: At that, Paul left the Areopagus.
ACT 17:33.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17] At that, Paul left the Areopagus.

ACT 17:34.text: But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.
ACT 17:34.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 17 · Faith] But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.

ACT 18:1.text: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
ACT 18:1.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

ACT 18:2.text: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them,
ACT 18:2.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them,

ACT 18:3.text: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.
ACT 18:3.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.

ACT 18:4.text: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.
ACT 18:4.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.

ACT 18:5.text: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
ACT 18:5.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

ACT 18:6.text: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
ACT 18:6.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”

ACT 18:7.text: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.
ACT 18:7.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.

ACT 18:8.text: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.
ACT 18:8.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18 · Faith, Family] Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.

ACT 18:9.text: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.
ACT 18:9.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.

ACT 18:10.text: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”
ACT 18:10.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”

ACT 18:11.text: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.
ACT 18:11.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.

ACT 18:12.text: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.
ACT 18:12.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18 · Judgment] While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.

ACT 18:13.text: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.
ACT 18:13.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.

ACT 18:14.text: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.
ACT 18:14.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18 · About Forgiveness] But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.

ACT 18:15.text: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”
ACT 18:15.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18 · About Forgiveness] But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”

ACT 18:16.text: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
ACT 18:16.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18 · Judgment] And he drove them away from the judgment seat.

ACT 18:17.text: At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio.
ACT 18:17.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18 · Judgment] At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio.

ACT 18:18.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.

ACT 18:19.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] When they reached Ephesus, Paul parted ways with Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.

ACT 18:20.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.

ACT 18:21.text: But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.
ACT 18:21.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.

ACT 18:22.text: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch.
ACT 18:22.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18 · Church] When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch.

ACT 18:23.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18 · Apostles, Encouragement] After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

ACT 18:24.text: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.
ACT 18:24.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 18] Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.

ACT 18:25.text: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.

ACT 27:11.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.

ACT 27:12.text: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, if somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.
ACT 27:12.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, if somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.

ACT 27:13.text: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.
ACT 27:13.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.

ACT 27:14.text: But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.
ACT 27:14.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.

ACT 27:15.text: Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.
ACT 27:15.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.

ACT 27:16.text: Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
ACT 27:16.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.

ACT 27:17.text: After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.
ACT 27:17.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.

ACT 27:18.text: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.
ACT 27:18.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.

ACT 27:19.text: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
ACT 27:19.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.

ACT 27:20.text: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.
ACT 27:20.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.

ACT 27:21.text: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.
ACT 27:21.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.

ACT 27:22.text: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.
ACT 27:22.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.

ACT 27:23.text: For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me
ACT 27:23.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me

ACT 27:24.text: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’
ACT 27:24.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’

ACT 27:25.text: So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.
ACT 27:25.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27 · Faith] So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.

ACT 27:26.text: However, we must run aground on some island.”
ACT 27:26.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] However, we must run aground on some island.”

ACT 27:27.text: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
ACT 27:27.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27 · About Forgiveness] On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.

ACT 27:28.text: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.
ACT 27:28.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.

ACT 27:29.text: Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.
ACT 27:29.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.

ACT 27:30.text: Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.
ACT 27:30.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.

ACT 27:31.text: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”
ACT 27:31.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”

ACT 27:32.text: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.
ACT 27:32.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.

ACT 27:33.text: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.
ACT 27:33.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.

ACT 27:34.text: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”
ACT 27:34.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”

ACT 27:35.text: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
ACT 27:35.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.

ACT 27:36.text: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.
ACT 27:36.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.

ACT 27:37.text: In all, there were 276 of us on board.
ACT 27:37.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] In all, there were 276 of us on board.

ACT 27:38.text: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
ACT 27:38.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

ACT 27:39.text: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
ACT 27:39.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.

ACT 27:40.text: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
ACT 27:40.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.

ACT 27:41.text: But the vessel struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.
ACT 27:41.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] But the vessel struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.

ACT 27:42.text: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.
ACT 27:42.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27 · Freedom] The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.

ACT 27:43.text: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
ACT 27:43.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27 · God Commanded Genocide] But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

ACT 27:44.text: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.
ACT 27:44.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 27] The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.

ACT 28:1.text: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
ACT 28:1.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.

ACT 28:2.text: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
ACT 28:2.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · Grace] The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.

ACT 28:3.text: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.
ACT 28:3.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.

ACT 28:4.text: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
ACT 28:4.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · Justice] When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”

ACT 28:5.text: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
ACT 28:5.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.

ACT 28:6.text: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
ACT 28:6.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

ACT 28:7.text: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
ACT 28:7.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.

ACT 28:8.text: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.
ACT 28:8.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · God the Father] The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.

ACT 28:9.text: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.
ACT 28:9.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.

ACT 28:10.text: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.
ACT 28:10.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.

ACT 28:11.text: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.
ACT 28:11.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.

ACT 28:12.text: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
ACT 28:12.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

ACT 28:13.text: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.
ACT 28:13.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.

ACT 28:14.text: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.
ACT 28:14.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.

ACT 28:15.text: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.
ACT 28:15.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · About Forgiveness] The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.

ACT 28:16.text: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
ACT 28:16.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

ACT 28:17.text: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
ACT 28:17.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · Explain Romans] After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.

ACT 28:18.text: They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.
ACT 28:18.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · Death, Freedom] They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.

ACT 28:19.text: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.
ACT 28:19.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.

ACT 28:20.text: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”
ACT 28:20.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · Israel] So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”

ACT 28:21.text: The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.
ACT 28:21.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · About Forgiveness] The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.

ACT 28:22.text: But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”
ACT 28:22.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”

ACT 28:23.text: So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
ACT 28:23.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · About Forgiveness, Jesus Christ] So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.

ACT 28:24.text: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.
ACT 28:24.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · Faith] Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.

ACT 28:25.text: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:
ACT 28:25.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · Fruit of the Spirit] They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:

ACT 28:26.text: ‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”
ACT 28:26.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] ‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”

ACT 28:27.text: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’
ACT 28:27.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · Adultery In Heart] For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’

ACT 28:28.text: Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”
ACT 28:28.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”

ACT 28:30.text: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.
ACT 28:30.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28] Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.

ACT 28:31.text: Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
ACT 28:31.bm25Text: [Acts · Chapter 28 · About Forgiveness, Body of Christ] Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.

AMO 1:2.bm25Text: [Amos · Chapter 1] He said:  “The LORD roars from Zion and raises His voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers.”

AMO 1:4.bm25Text: [Amos · Chapter 1] So I will send fire upon the house of Hazael to consume the citadels of Ben-hadad.

AMO 1:10.bm25Text: [Amos · Chapter 1] So I will send fire upon the walls of Tyre to consume its citadels.”

AMO 1:14.bm25Text: [Amos · Chapter 1] So I will kindle a fire in the walls of Rabbah to consume its citadels amid war cries on the day of battle and a violent wind on the day of tempest.

COL 3:1.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Therefore, since you have been raised with Christ, strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.

COL 3:2.text: Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
COL 3:2.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3] Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.

COL 3:3.text: For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.
COL 3:3.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.

COL 3:4.text: When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.
COL 3:4.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Glory] When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.

COL 3:5.text: Put to death, therefore, the components of your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, lust, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry.
COL 3:5.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Death, Greed] Put to death, therefore, the components of your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, lust, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry.

COL 3:6.text: Because of these, the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience.
COL 3:6.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3] Because of these, the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience.

COL 3:7.text: When you lived among them, you also used to walk in these ways.
COL 3:7.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3] When you lived among them, you also used to walk in these ways.

COL 3:8.text: But now you must put aside all such things as these: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips.
COL 3:8.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3] But now you must put aside all such things as these: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips.

COL 3:9.text: Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices,
COL 3:9.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3] Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices,

COL 3:10.text: and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator.
COL 3:10.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Graven Image] and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator.

COL 3:11.text: Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free, but Christ is all and is in all.
COL 3:11.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free, but Christ is all and is in all.

COL 3:12.text: Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
COL 3:12.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Love, Compassion] Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.

COL 3:13.text: Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
COL 3:13.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Forgiveness] Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.

COL 3:14.text: And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.
COL 3:14.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Love] And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.

COL 3:15.text: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.
COL 3:15.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.

COL 3:16.text: Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.
COL 3:16.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Gratitude] Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.

COL 3:17.text: And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
COL 3:17.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Generosity, God the Father] And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.

COL 3:18.text: Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
COL 3:18.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Husbands] Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.

COL 3:19.text: Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.
COL 3:19.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Love, Husbands] Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.

COL 3:20.text: Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
COL 3:20.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Children] Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.

COL 3:21.text: Fathers, do not provoke your children, so they will not become discouraged.
COL 3:21.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Children] Fathers, do not provoke your children, so they will not become discouraged.

COL 3:22.text: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.
COL 3:22.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Adultery In Heart] Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.

COL 3:23.text: Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men,
COL 3:23.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3] Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men,

COL 3:24.text: because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
COL 3:24.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Inheritance] because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.

COL 3:25.text: Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.
COL 3:25.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 3] Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.

COL 4:1.text: Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven.
COL 4:1.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Heaven] Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven.

COL 4:2.text: Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful,
COL 4:2.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Devote To Destruction] Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful,

COL 4:3.text: as you pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.
COL 4:3.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] as you pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.

COL 4:4.text: Pray that I may declare it clearly, as I should.
COL 4:4.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4] Pray that I may declare it clearly, as I should.

COL 4:5.text: Act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time.
COL 4:5.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4] Act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time.

COL 4:6.text: Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone.
COL 4:6.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4] Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone.

COL 4:7.text: Tychicus will tell you all the news about me. He is a beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord.
COL 4:7.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Love, Faith] Tychicus will tell you all the news about me. He is a beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord.

COL 4:8.text: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know about us, and that he may encourage your hearts.
COL 4:8.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · About Forgiveness] I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know about us, and that he may encourage your hearts.

COL 4:9.text: With him I am sending Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you about everything here.
COL 4:9.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Love, Faith] With him I am sending Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you about everything here.

COL 4:10.text: My fellow prisoner Aristarchus sends you greetings, as does Mark the cousin of Barnabas. You have already received instructions about him: If he comes to you, welcome him.
COL 4:10.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · About Forgiveness] My fellow prisoner Aristarchus sends you greetings, as does Mark the cousin of Barnabas. You have already received instructions about him: If he comes to you, welcome him.

COL 4:11.text: Jesus, who is called Justus, also sends greetings. These are the only Jews among my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.
COL 4:11.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Comfort, Jesus Christ] Jesus, who is called Justus, also sends greetings. These are the only Jews among my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.

COL 4:12.text: Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in the full will of God.
COL 4:12.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in the full will of God.

COL 4:13.text: For I testify about him that he goes to great pains for you and for those at Laodicea and Hierapolis.
COL 4:13.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · About Forgiveness] For I testify about him that he goes to great pains for you and for those at Laodicea and Hierapolis.

COL 4:14.text: Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas send you greetings.
COL 4:14.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Love] Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas send you greetings.

COL 4:15.text: Greet the brothers in Laodicea, as well as Nympha and the church that meets at her house.
COL 4:15.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Church] Greet the brothers in Laodicea, as well as Nympha and the church that meets at her house.

COL 4:16.text: After this letter has been read among you, make sure that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you in turn read the letter from Laodicea.
COL 4:16.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Church] After this letter has been read among you, make sure that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you in turn read the letter from Laodicea.

COL 4:17.text: Tell Archippus: “See to it that you complete the ministry you have received in the Lord.”
COL 4:17.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4] Tell Archippus: “See to it that you complete the ministry you have received in the Lord.”

COL 4:18.text: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul.  Remember my chains.  Grace be with you.
COL 4:18.bm25Text: [Colossians · Chapter 4 · Grace] This greeting is in my own hand—Paul.  Remember my chains.  Grace be with you.

DAN 1:1.text: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
DAN 1:1.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

DAN 1:2.text: And the Lord delivered into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah, along with some of the articles from the house of God. He carried these off to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, where he put them in the treasury of his god.
DAN 1:2.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] And the Lord delivered into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah, along with some of the articles from the house of God. He carried these off to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, where he put them in the treasury of his god.

DAN 1:3.text: Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, the chief of his court officials, to bring in some Israelites from the royal family and the nobility—
DAN 1:3.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1 · Family] Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, the chief of his court officials, to bring in some Israelites from the royal family and the nobility—

DAN 1:4.text: young men without blemish, handsome, gifted in all wisdom, knowledgeable, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace—and to teach them the language and literature of the Chaldeans.
DAN 1:4.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] young men without blemish, handsome, gifted in all wisdom, knowledgeable, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace—and to teach them the language and literature of the Chaldeans.

DAN 1:5.text: The king assigned them daily provisions of the royal food and wine. They were to be trained for three years, after which they were to enter the king’s service.
DAN 1:5.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] The king assigned them daily provisions of the royal food and wine. They were to be trained for three years, after which they were to enter the king’s service.

DAN 1:6.text: Among these young men were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
DAN 1:6.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] Among these young men were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

DAN 1:7.text: The chief official gave them new names: To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
DAN 1:7.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] The chief official gave them new names: To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.

DAN 1:8.text: But Daniel made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine. So he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself.
DAN 1:8.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] But Daniel made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine. So he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself.

DAN 1:9.text: Now God had granted Daniel favor and compassion from the chief official,
DAN 1:9.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1 · Blessing, Compassion] Now God had granted Daniel favor and compassion from the chief official,

DAN 1:10.text: but he said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. For why should he see your faces looking thinner than those of the other young men your age? You would endanger my head before the king!”
DAN 1:10.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] but he said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. For why should he see your faces looking thinner than those of the other young men your age? You would endanger my head before the king!”

DAN 1:11.text: Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
DAN 1:11.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

DAN 1:12.text: “Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.
DAN 1:12.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] “Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.

DAN 1:13.text: Then compare our appearances with those of the young men who are eating the royal food, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”
DAN 1:13.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] Then compare our appearances with those of the young men who are eating the royal food, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”

DAN 1:14.text: So he consented to this and tested them for ten days.
DAN 1:14.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] So he consented to this and tested them for ten days.

DAN 1:15.text: And at the end of ten days, they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who were eating the king’s food.
DAN 1:15.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] And at the end of ten days, they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who were eating the king’s food.

DAN 1:16.text: So the steward continued to withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and he gave them vegetables instead.
DAN 1:16.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] So the steward continued to withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and he gave them vegetables instead.

DAN 1:17.text: To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding in every kind of literature and wisdom. And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.
DAN 1:17.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding in every kind of literature and wisdom. And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.

DAN 1:18.text: Now at the end of the time specified by the king, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.
DAN 1:18.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] Now at the end of the time specified by the king, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.

DAN 1:19.text: And the king spoke with them, and among all the young men he found no one equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they entered the king’s service.
DAN 1:19.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] And the king spoke with them, and among all the young men he found no one equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they entered the king’s service.

DAN 1:20.text: In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king consulted them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.
DAN 1:20.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1 · About Forgiveness, End Times] In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king consulted them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.

DAN 1:21.text: And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
DAN 1:21.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 1] And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.

DAN 2:1.text: In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams that troubled his spirit, and sleep escaped him.
DAN 2:1.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Fruit of the Spirit] In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams that troubled his spirit, and sleep escaped him.

DAN 2:2.text: So the king gave orders to summon the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and astrologers to explain his dreams. When they came and stood before the king,
DAN 2:2.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Explain Romans] So the king gave orders to summon the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and astrologers to explain his dreams. When they came and stood before the king,

DAN 2:3.text: he said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is anxious to understand it.”
DAN 2:3.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Fruit of the Spirit] he said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is anxious to understand it.”

DAN 2:4.text: Then the astrologers answered the king in Aramaic, “O king, may you live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will give the interpretation.”
DAN 2:4.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] Then the astrologers answered the king in Aramaic, “O king, may you live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will give the interpretation.”

DAN 2:5.text: The king replied to the astrologers, “My word is final: If you do not tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut into pieces and your houses will be reduced to rubble.
DAN 2:5.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] The king replied to the astrologers, “My word is final: If you do not tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut into pieces and your houses will be reduced to rubble.

DAN 2:6.text: But if you tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and its interpretation.”
DAN 2:6.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] But if you tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and its interpretation.”

DAN 2:7.text: They answered a second time, “Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will give the interpretation.”
DAN 2:7.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] They answered a second time, “Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will give the interpretation.”

DAN 2:8.text: The king replied, “I know for sure that you are stalling for time, because you see that my word is final.
DAN 2:8.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] The king replied, “I know for sure that you are stalling for time, because you see that my word is final.

DAN 2:9.text: If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one decree for you. You have conspired to speak before me false and fraudulent words, hoping the situation will change. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can give me its interpretation.”
DAN 2:9.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · False Gods, False Witness] If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one decree for you. You have conspired to speak before me false and fraudulent words, hoping the situation will change. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can give me its interpretation.”

DAN 2:10.text: The astrologers answered the king, “No one on earth can do what the king requests! No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked anything like this of any magician, enchanter, or astrologer.
DAN 2:10.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] The astrologers answered the king, “No one on earth can do what the king requests! No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked anything like this of any magician, enchanter, or astrologer.

DAN 2:11.text: What the king requests is so difficult that no one can tell it to him except the gods, whose dwelling is not with mortals.”
DAN 2:11.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] What the king requests is so difficult that no one can tell it to him except the gods, whose dwelling is not with mortals.”

DAN 2:12.text: This response made the king so furious with anger that he gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
DAN 2:12.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] This response made the king so furious with anger that he gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.

DAN 2:13.text: So the decree went out that the wise men were to be executed, and men went to look for Daniel and his friends to execute them.
DAN 2:13.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] So the decree went out that the wise men were to be executed, and men went to look for Daniel and his friends to execute them.

DAN 2:14.text: When Arioch, the commander of the king’s guard, had gone out to execute the wise men of Babylon, Daniel replied with discretion and tact.
DAN 2:14.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] When Arioch, the commander of the king’s guard, had gone out to execute the wise men of Babylon, Daniel replied with discretion and tact.

DAN 2:15.text: “Why is the decree from the king so harsh?” he asked.  At this time Arioch explained the situation to Daniel.
DAN 2:15.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] “Why is the decree from the king so harsh?” he asked.  At this time Arioch explained the situation to Daniel.

DAN 2:16.text: So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him some time, so that he could give him the interpretation.
DAN 2:16.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him some time, so that he could give him the interpretation.

DAN 2:17.text: Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
DAN 2:17.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

DAN 2:18.text: urging them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends would not be killed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
DAN 2:18.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Forgiveness, Compassion] urging them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends would not be killed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

DAN 2:19.text: During the night, the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision, and he blessed the God of heaven
DAN 2:19.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Heaven] During the night, the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision, and he blessed the God of heaven

DAN 2:20.text: and declared:  “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and power belong to Him.
DAN 2:20.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] and declared:  “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and power belong to Him.

DAN 2:21.text: He changes the times and seasons; He removes kings and establishes them. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to the discerning.
DAN 2:21.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · End Times] He changes the times and seasons; He removes kings and establishes them. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to the discerning.

DAN 2:22.text: He reveals the deep and hidden things; He knows what lies in darkness, and light dwells with Him.
DAN 2:22.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Light] He reveals the deep and hidden things; He knows what lies in darkness, and light dwells with Him.

DAN 2:23.text: To You, O God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because You have given me wisdom and power. And now You have made known to me what we have requested, for You have made known to us the dream of the king.”
DAN 2:23.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] To You, O God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because You have given me wisdom and power. And now You have made known to me what we have requested, for You have made known to us the dream of the king.”

DAN 2:24.text: Therefore Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, “Do not execute the wise men of Babylon! Bring me before the king, and I will give him the interpretation.”
DAN 2:24.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] Therefore Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, “Do not execute the wise men of Babylon! Bring me before the king, and I will give him the interpretation.”

DAN 2:25.text: Arioch hastily brought Daniel before the king and said to him, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who will tell the king the interpretation.”
DAN 2:25.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] Arioch hastily brought Daniel before the king and said to him, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who will tell the king the interpretation.”

DAN 2:26.text: The king responded to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to tell me what I saw in the dream, as well as its interpretation?”
DAN 2:26.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] The king responded to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to tell me what I saw in the dream, as well as its interpretation?”

DAN 2:27.text: Daniel answered the king, “No wise man, enchanter, medium, or magician can explain to the king the mystery of which he inquires.
DAN 2:27.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Explain Romans] Daniel answered the king, “No wise man, enchanter, medium, or magician can explain to the king the mystery of which he inquires.

DAN 2:28.text: But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the latter days. Your dream and the visions that came into your mind as you lay on your bed were these:
DAN 2:28.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2 · Heaven] But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the latter days. Your dream and the visions that came into your mind as you lay on your bed were these:

DAN 2:29.text: As you lay on your bed, O king, your thoughts turned to the future, and the Revealer of Mysteries made known to you what will happen.
DAN 2:29.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 2] As you lay on your bed, O king, your thoughts turned to the future, and the Revealer of Mysteries made known to you what will happen.

DAN 2:30.text: And to me this mystery has been revealed, not because I have more wisdom than any man alive, but in order that the interpretation might be made known to the king, and that you may understand the thoughts of your mind.

DAN 7:5.text: Suddenly another beast appeared, which looked like a bear. It was raised up on one of its sides, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. So it was told, ‘Get up and gorge yourself on flesh!’
DAN 7:5.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Antichrist] Suddenly another beast appeared, which looked like a bear. It was raised up on one of its sides, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. So it was told, ‘Get up and gorge yourself on flesh!’
