DAN 7:7.text: After this, as I watched in my vision in the night, suddenly a fourth beast appeared, and it was terrifying—dreadful and extremely strong—with large iron teeth. It devoured and crushed; then it trampled underfoot whatever was left. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.
DAN 7:7.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Antichrist] After this, as I watched in my vision in the night, suddenly a fourth beast appeared, and it was terrifying—dreadful and extremely strong—with large iron teeth. It devoured and crushed; then it trampled underfoot whatever was left. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.

DAN 7:8.text: While I was contemplating the horns, suddenly another horn, a little one, came up among them, and three of the first horns were uprooted before it. This horn had eyes like those of a man and a mouth that spoke words of arrogance.
DAN 7:8.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7] While I was contemplating the horns, suddenly another horn, a little one, came up among them, and three of the first horns were uprooted before it. This horn had eyes like those of a man and a mouth that spoke words of arrogance.

DAN 7:9.text: As I continued to watch,  thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took His seat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of His head was like pure wool. His throne was flaming with fire, and its wheels were all ablaze.
DAN 7:9.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7] As I continued to watch,  thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took His seat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of His head was like pure wool. His throne was flaming with fire, and its wheels were all ablaze.

DAN 7:10.text: A river of fire was flowing, coming out from His presence. Thousands upon thousands attended Him, and myriads upon myriads stood before Him. The court was convened, and the books were opened.
DAN 7:10.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7] A river of fire was flowing, coming out from His presence. Thousands upon thousands attended Him, and myriads upon myriads stood before Him. The court was convened, and the books were opened.

DAN 7:11.text: Then I kept watching because of the arrogant words the horn was speaking. As I continued to watch, the beast was slain, and its body was destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.
DAN 7:11.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Antichrist] Then I kept watching because of the arrogant words the horn was speaking. As I continued to watch, the beast was slain, and its body was destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.

DAN 7:12.text: As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was removed, but they were granted an extension of life for a season and a time.
DAN 7:12.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7] As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was removed, but they were granted an extension of life for a season and a time.

DAN 7:13.text: In my vision in the night I continued to watch,  and I saw One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into His presence.
DAN 7:13.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Heaven] In my vision in the night I continued to watch,  and I saw One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into His presence.

DAN 7:14.text: And He was given dominion, glory, and kingship, that the people of every nation and language should serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and His kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.
DAN 7:14.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Glory, Kingdom of God] And He was given dominion, glory, and kingship, that the people of every nation and language should serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and His kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.

DAN 7:15.text: I, Daniel, was grieved in my spirit, and the visions in my mind alarmed me.
DAN 7:15.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Fruit of the Spirit] I, Daniel, was grieved in my spirit, and the visions in my mind alarmed me.

DAN 7:16.text: I approached one of those who were standing there, and I asked him the true meaning of all this.  So he told me the interpretation of these things:
DAN 7:16.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7] I approached one of those who were standing there, and I asked him the true meaning of all this.  So he told me the interpretation of these things:

DAN 7:17.text: ‘These four great beasts are four kings who will arise from the earth.
DAN 7:17.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7] ‘These four great beasts are four kings who will arise from the earth.

DAN 7:18.text: But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever—yes, forever and ever.’
DAN 7:18.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Kingdom of God] But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever—yes, forever and ever.’

DAN 7:19.text: Then I wanted to know the true meaning of the fourth beast, which was different from all the others—extremely terrifying—devouring and crushing with iron teeth and bronze claws, then trampling underfoot whatever was left.
DAN 7:19.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Antichrist] Then I wanted to know the true meaning of the fourth beast, which was different from all the others—extremely terrifying—devouring and crushing with iron teeth and bronze claws, then trampling underfoot whatever was left.

DAN 7:20.text: I also wanted to know about the ten horns on its head and the other horn that came up, before which three of them fell—the horn whose appearance was more imposing than the others, with eyes and with a mouth that spoke words of arrogance.
DAN 7:20.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · About Forgiveness] I also wanted to know about the ten horns on its head and the other horn that came up, before which three of them fell—the horn whose appearance was more imposing than the others, with eyes and with a mouth that spoke words of arrogance.

DAN 7:21.text: As I watched, this horn was waging war against the saints and prevailing against them,
DAN 7:21.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7] As I watched, this horn was waging war against the saints and prevailing against them,

DAN 7:22.text: until the Ancient of Days arrived and pronounced judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High, and the time came for them to possess the kingdom.
DAN 7:22.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Blessing, Judgment] until the Ancient of Days arrived and pronounced judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High, and the time came for them to possess the kingdom.

DAN 7:23.text: This is what he said: ‘The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will appear on the earth, different from all the other kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth, trample it down, and crush it.
DAN 7:23.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Antichrist, Kingdom of God] This is what he said: ‘The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will appear on the earth, different from all the other kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth, trample it down, and crush it.

DAN 7:24.text: And the ten horns are ten kings who will rise from this kingdom. After them another king, different from the earlier ones, will rise and subdue three kings.
DAN 7:24.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Kingdom of God] And the ten horns are ten kings who will rise from this kingdom. After them another king, different from the earlier ones, will rise and subdue three kings.

DAN 7:25.text: He will speak out against the Most High and oppress the saints of the Most High, intending to change the appointed times and laws; and the saints will be given into his hand for a time, and times, and half a time.
DAN 7:25.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · End Times] He will speak out against the Most High and oppress the saints of the Most High, intending to change the appointed times and laws; and the saints will be given into his hand for a time, and times, and half a time.

DAN 7:26.text: But the court will convene, and his dominion will be taken away and completely destroyed forever.
DAN 7:26.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7] But the court will convene, and his dominion will be taken away and completely destroyed forever.

DAN 7:27.text: Then the sovereignty, dominion, and greatness of the kingdoms under all of heaven will be given to the people, the saints of the Most High. His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will serve and obey Him.’
DAN 7:27.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7 · Heaven, Kingdom of God] Then the sovereignty, dominion, and greatness of the kingdoms under all of heaven will be given to the people, the saints of the Most High. His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will serve and obey Him.’

DAN 7:28.text: Thus ends the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my face turned pale. But I kept the matter to myself.”
DAN 7:28.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 7] Thus ends the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my face turned pale. But I kept the matter to myself.”

DAN 8:1.text: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, subsequent to the one that had appeared to me earlier.
DAN 8:1.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, subsequent to the one that had appeared to me earlier.

DAN 8:2.text: And in the vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision that I was beside the Ulai Canal.
DAN 8:2.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] And in the vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision that I was beside the Ulai Canal.

DAN 8:3.text: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw a ram with two horns standing beside the canal. The horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one grew up later.
DAN 8:3.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] Then I lifted up my eyes and saw a ram with two horns standing beside the canal. The horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one grew up later.

DAN 8:4.text: I saw the ram charging toward the west and the north and the south. No animal could stand against him, and there was no deliverance from his power. He did as he pleased and became great.
DAN 8:4.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] I saw the ram charging toward the west and the north and the south. No animal could stand against him, and there was no deliverance from his power. He did as he pleased and became great.

DAN 8:5.text: As I was contemplating all this, suddenly a goat with a prominent horn between his eyes came out of the west, crossing the surface of the entire earth without touching the ground.
DAN 8:5.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] As I was contemplating all this, suddenly a goat with a prominent horn between his eyes came out of the west, crossing the surface of the entire earth without touching the ground.

DAN 8:6.text: He came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal and rushed at him with furious power.
DAN 8:6.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] He came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal and rushed at him with furious power.

DAN 8:7.text: I saw him approach the ram in a rage against him, and he struck the ram and shattered his two horns. The ram was powerless to stand against him, and the goat threw him to the ground and trampled him, and no one could deliver the ram from his power.
DAN 8:7.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] I saw him approach the ram in a rage against him, and he struck the ram and shattered his two horns. The ram was powerless to stand against him, and the goat threw him to the ground and trampled him, and no one could deliver the ram from his power.

DAN 8:8.text: Thus the goat became very great, but at the height of his power, his large horn was broken off, and four prominent horns came up in its place, pointing toward the four winds of heaven.
DAN 8:8.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8 · Heaven] Thus the goat became very great, but at the height of his power, his large horn was broken off, and four prominent horns came up in its place, pointing toward the four winds of heaven.

DAN 8:9.text: From one of these horns a little horn emerged and grew extensively toward the south and the east and toward the Beautiful Land.
DAN 8:9.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] From one of these horns a little horn emerged and grew extensively toward the south and the east and toward the Beautiful Land.

DAN 8:10.text: It grew as high as the host of heaven, and it cast down some of the host and some of the stars to the earth, and trampled them.
DAN 8:10.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8 · Heaven] It grew as high as the host of heaven, and it cast down some of the host and some of the stars to the earth, and trampled them.

DAN 8:11.text: It magnified itself, even to the Prince of the host; it removed His daily sacrifice and overthrew the place of His sanctuary.
DAN 8:11.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] It magnified itself, even to the Prince of the host; it removed His daily sacrifice and overthrew the place of His sanctuary.

DAN 8:12.text: And in the rebellion, the host and the daily sacrifice were given over to the horn, and it flung truth to the ground and prospered in whatever it did.
DAN 8:12.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] And in the rebellion, the host and the daily sacrifice were given over to the horn, and it flung truth to the ground and prospered in whatever it did.

DAN 8:13.text: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to him, “How long until the fulfillment of the vision of the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the surrender of the sanctuary and of the host to be trampled?”
DAN 8:13.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to him, “How long until the fulfillment of the vision of the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the surrender of the sanctuary and of the host to be trampled?”

DAN 8:14.text: He said to me, “It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be properly restored.”
DAN 8:14.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] He said to me, “It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be properly restored.”

DAN 8:15.text: While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there stood before me one having the appearance of a man.
DAN 8:15.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there stood before me one having the appearance of a man.

DAN 8:16.text: And I heard the voice of a man calling from between the banks of the Ulai: “Gabriel, explain the vision to this man.”
DAN 8:16.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8 · Calling, Explain Romans] And I heard the voice of a man calling from between the banks of the Ulai: “Gabriel, explain the vision to this man.”

DAN 8:17.text: As he came near to where I stood, I was terrified and fell facedown.  “Son of man,” he said to me, “understand that the vision concerns the time of the end.”
DAN 8:17.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] As he came near to where I stood, I was terrified and fell facedown.  “Son of man,” he said to me, “understand that the vision concerns the time of the end.”

DAN 8:18.text: While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground.  Then he touched me, helped me to my feet,
DAN 8:18.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground.  Then he touched me, helped me to my feet,

DAN 8:19.text: and said, “Behold, I will make known to you what will happen in the latter time of wrath, because it concerns the appointed time of the end.
DAN 8:19.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] and said, “Behold, I will make known to you what will happen in the latter time of wrath, because it concerns the appointed time of the end.

DAN 8:20.text: The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.
DAN 8:20.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.

DAN 8:21.text: The shaggy goat represents the king of Greece, and the large horn between his eyes is the first king.
DAN 8:21.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] The shaggy goat represents the king of Greece, and the large horn between his eyes is the first king.

DAN 8:22.text: The four horns that replaced the broken one represent four kingdoms that will rise from that nation, but will not have the same power.
DAN 8:22.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] The four horns that replaced the broken one represent four kingdoms that will rise from that nation, but will not have the same power.

DAN 8:23.text: In the latter part of their reign, when the rebellion has reached its full measure, an insolent king, skilled in intrigue, will come to the throne.
DAN 8:23.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] In the latter part of their reign, when the rebellion has reached its full measure, an insolent king, skilled in intrigue, will come to the throne.

DAN 8:24.text: His power will be great, but it will not be his own. He will cause terrible destruction and succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy the mighty men along with the holy people.
DAN 8:24.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] His power will be great, but it will not be his own. He will cause terrible destruction and succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy the mighty men along with the holy people.

DAN 8:25.text: Through his craft and by his hand, he will cause deceit to prosper, and in his own mind he will make himself great. In a time of peace he will destroy many, and he will even stand against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be broken off, but not by human hands.
DAN 8:25.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8 · Deceit, Destroy Canaan] Through his craft and by his hand, he will cause deceit to prosper, and in his own mind he will make himself great. In a time of peace he will destroy many, and he will even stand against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be broken off, but not by human hands.

DAN 8:26.text: The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been spoken is true. Now you must seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future.”
DAN 8:26.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8] The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been spoken is true. Now you must seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future.”

DAN 8:27.text: I, Daniel, was exhausted and lay ill for days. Then I got up and went about the king’s business. I was confounded by the vision; it was beyond understanding.
DAN 8:27.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 8 · About Forgiveness] I, Daniel, was exhausted and lay ill for days. Then I got up and went about the king’s business. I was confounded by the vision; it was beyond understanding.

DAN 9:1.text: In the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede by descent, who was made ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans—
DAN 9:1.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Kingdom of God] In the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede by descent, who was made ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans—

DAN 9:2.text: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the sacred books, according to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet, that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years.
DAN 9:2.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the sacred books, according to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet, that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years.

DAN 9:3.text: So I turned my attention to the Lord God to seek Him by prayer and petition, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
DAN 9:3.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Fasting] So I turned my attention to the Lord God to seek Him by prayer and petition, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.

DAN 9:4.text: And I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed, “O, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments,
DAN 9:4.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Love, Covenant] And I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed, “O, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments,

DAN 9:5.text: we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled. We have turned away from Your commandments and ordinances.
DAN 9:5.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Law] we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled. We have turned away from Your commandments and ordinances.

DAN 9:6.text: We have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, leaders, and fathers, and to all the people of the land.
DAN 9:6.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] We have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, leaders, and fathers, and to all the people of the land.

DAN 9:7.text: To You, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but this day we are covered with shame—the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel near and far, in all the countries to which You have driven us because of our unfaithfulness to You.
DAN 9:7.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Faith, Adultery] To You, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but this day we are covered with shame—the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel near and far, in all the countries to which You have driven us because of our unfaithfulness to You.

DAN 9:8.text: O LORD, we are covered with shame—our kings, our leaders, and our fathers—because we have sinned against You.
DAN 9:8.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] O LORD, we are covered with shame—our kings, our leaders, and our fathers—because we have sinned against You.

DAN 9:9.text: To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, even though we have rebelled against Him
DAN 9:9.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Forgiveness, About Forgiveness] To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, even though we have rebelled against Him

DAN 9:10.text: and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God to walk in His laws, which He set before us through His servants the prophets.
DAN 9:10.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God to walk in His laws, which He set before us through His servants the prophets.

DAN 9:11.text: All Israel has transgressed Your law and turned away, refusing to obey Your voice; so the oath and the curse written in the Law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out on us, because we have sinned against You.
DAN 9:11.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Curse God, Israel] All Israel has transgressed Your law and turned away, refusing to obey Your voice; so the oath and the curse written in the Law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out on us, because we have sinned against You.

DAN 9:12.text: You have carried out the words spoken against us and against our rulers by bringing upon us a great disaster. For under all of heaven, nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.
DAN 9:12.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Heaven] You have carried out the words spoken against us and against our rulers by bringing upon us a great disaster. For under all of heaven, nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.

DAN 9:13.text: Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come upon us, yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquities and giving attention to Your truth.
DAN 9:13.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Blessing, Generosity] Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come upon us, yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquities and giving attention to Your truth.

DAN 9:14.text: Therefore the LORD has kept the calamity in store and brought it upon us. For the LORD our God is righteous in all He does; yet we have not obeyed His voice.
DAN 9:14.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] Therefore the LORD has kept the calamity in store and brought it upon us. For the LORD our God is righteous in all He does; yet we have not obeyed His voice.

DAN 9:15.text: Now, O Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and who made for Yourself a name renowned to this day, we have sinned; we have acted wickedly.
DAN 9:15.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] Now, O Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and who made for Yourself a name renowned to this day, we have sinned; we have acted wickedly.

DAN 9:16.text: O Lord, in keeping with all Your righteous acts, I pray that Your anger and wrath may turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people are a reproach to all around us.
DAN 9:16.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] O Lord, in keeping with all Your righteous acts, I pray that Your anger and wrath may turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people are a reproach to all around us.

DAN 9:17.text: So now, our God, hear the prayers and petitions of Your servant. For Your sake, O Lord, cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary.
DAN 9:17.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] So now, our God, hear the prayers and petitions of Your servant. For Your sake, O Lord, cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary.

DAN 9:18.text: Incline Your ear, O my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see the desolation of the city that bears Your name. For we are not presenting our petitions before You because of our righteous acts, but because of Your great compassion.
DAN 9:18.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Compassion] Incline Your ear, O my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see the desolation of the city that bears Your name. For we are not presenting our petitions before You because of our righteous acts, but because of Your great compassion.

DAN 9:19.text: O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act! For Your sake, O my God, do not delay, because Your city and Your people bear Your name.”
DAN 9:19.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Forgiveness] O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act! For Your sake, O my God, do not delay, because Your city and Your people bear Your name.”

DAN 9:20.text: While I was speaking, praying, confessing my sin and that of my people Israel, and presenting my petition before the LORD my God concerning His holy mountain—
DAN 9:20.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Israel] While I was speaking, praying, confessing my sin and that of my people Israel, and presenting my petition before the LORD my God concerning His holy mountain—

DAN 9:21.text: while I was still praying, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.
DAN 9:21.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · About Forgiveness] while I was still praying, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.

DAN 9:22.text: He instructed me and spoke with me, saying: “O Daniel, I have come now to give you insight and understanding.
DAN 9:22.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] He instructed me and spoke with me, saying: “O Daniel, I have come now to give you insight and understanding.

DAN 9:23.text: At the beginning of your petitions, an answer went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are highly precious. So consider the message and understand the vision:
DAN 9:23.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9] At the beginning of your petitions, an answer went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are highly precious. So consider the message and understand the vision:

DAN 9:24.text: Seventy weeks are decreed for your people and your holy city to stop their transgression, to put an end to sin, to make atonement for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy Place.
DAN 9:24.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Daniel's Seventy Weeks] Seventy weeks are decreed for your people and your holy city to stop their transgression, to put an end to sin, to make atonement for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy Place.

DAN 9:25.text: Know and understand this: From the issuance of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem, until the Messiah, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of distress.
DAN 9:25.bm25Text: [Daniel · Chapter 9 · Daniel's Seventy Weeks] Know and understand this: From the issuance of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem, until the Messiah, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. DEU 23:1.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23 · Church] No man with crushed or severed genitals may enter the assembly of the LORD.

DEU 23:2.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23 · Church] No one of illegitimate birth may enter the assembly of the LORD, nor may any of his descendants, even to the tenth generation.

DEU 23:3.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23 · Church] No Ammonite or Moabite or any of their descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD, even to the tenth generation.

DEU 23:7.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23] Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not despise an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.

DEU 23:9.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23] When you are encamped against your enemies, then you shall keep yourself from every wicked thing.

DEU 23:10.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23] If any man among you becomes unclean because of a nocturnal emission, he must leave the camp and stay outside.

DEU 23:11.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23] When evening approaches, he must wash with water, and when the sun sets he may return to the camp.

DEU 23:12.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23] You must have a place outside the camp to go and relieve yourself.

DEU 23:13.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23] And you must have a digging tool in your equipment so that when you relieve yourself you can dig a hole and cover up your excrement.

DEU 23:14.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23] For the LORD your God walks throughout your camp to protect you and deliver your enemies to you. Your camp must be holy, lest He see anything unclean among you and turn away from you.

DEU 23:20.bm25Text: [Deuteronomy · Chapter 23] You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything to which you put your hand in the land that you are entering to possess.

ECC 1:1.text: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
ECC 1:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:

ECC 1:2.text: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”
ECC 1:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”

ECC 1:3.text: What does a man gain from all his labor, at which he toils under the sun?
ECC 1:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] What does a man gain from all his labor, at which he toils under the sun?

ECC 1:4.text: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.
ECC 1:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.

ECC 1:5.text: The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries back to where it rises.
ECC 1:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries back to where it rises.

ECC 1:6.text: The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.
ECC 1:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.

ECC 1:7.text: All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.
ECC 1:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.

ECC 1:8.text: All things are wearisome, more than one can describe; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear content with hearing.
ECC 1:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] All things are wearisome, more than one can describe; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear content with hearing.

ECC 1:9.text: What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.
ECC 1:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.

ECC 1:10.text: Is there a case where one can say, “Look, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages before us.
ECC 1:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] Is there a case where one can say, “Look, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages before us.

ECC 1:11.text: There is no remembrance of those who came before, and those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow after.
ECC 1:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] There is no remembrance of those who came before, and those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow after.

ECC 1:12.text: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
ECC 1:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1 · Israel] I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

ECC 1:13.text: And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a heavy burden God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!
ECC 1:13.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1 · Heaven] And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a heavy burden God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!

ECC 1:14.text: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.
ECC 1:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.

ECC 1:15.text: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
ECC 1:15.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.

ECC 1:16.text: I said to myself, “Behold, I have grown and increased in wisdom beyond all those before me who were over Jerusalem, and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.”
ECC 1:16.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] I said to myself, “Behold, I have grown and increased in wisdom beyond all those before me who were over Jerusalem, and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.”

ECC 1:17.text: So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.
ECC 1:17.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.

ECC 1:18.text: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.
ECC 1:18.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 1] For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.

ECC 2:1.text: I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!”  But it proved to be futile.
ECC 2:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!”  But it proved to be futile.

ECC 2:2.text: I said of laughter, “It is folly,” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”
ECC 2:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] I said of laughter, “It is folly,” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”

ECC 2:3.text: I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom—until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.
ECC 2:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2 · Heaven] I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom—until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.

ECC 2:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] I expanded my pursuits. I built houses and planted vineyards for myself.

ECC 2:5.text: I made gardens and parks for myself, where I planted all kinds of fruit trees.
ECC 2:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2 · Fruit of the Spirit] I made gardens and parks for myself, where I planted all kinds of fruit trees.

ECC 2:6.text: I built reservoirs to water my groves of flourishing trees.
ECC 2:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] I built reservoirs to water my groves of flourishing trees.

ECC 2:7.text: I acquired menservants and maidservants, and servants were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me,
ECC 2:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] I acquired menservants and maidservants, and servants were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me,

ECC 2:8.text: and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men—many concubines.
ECC 2:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2 · Female] and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men—many concubines.

ECC 2:9.text: So I became great and surpassed all in Jerusalem who had preceded me; and my wisdom remained with me.
ECC 2:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] So I became great and surpassed all in Jerusalem who had preceded me; and my wisdom remained with me.

ECC 2:10.text: Anything my eyes desired, I did not deny myself. I refused my heart no pleasure. For my heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.
ECC 2:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2 · Adultery In Heart] Anything my eyes desired, I did not deny myself. I refused my heart no pleasure. For my heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.

ECC 2:11.text: Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
ECC 2:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.

ECC 2:12.text: Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what more can the king’s successor do than what has already been accomplished?
ECC 2:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what more can the king’s successor do than what has already been accomplished?

ECC 2:13.text: And I saw that wisdom exceeds folly, just as light exceeds darkness:
ECC 2:13.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2 · Light] And I saw that wisdom exceeds folly, just as light exceeds darkness:

ECC 2:14.text: The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness.   Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.
ECC 2:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness.   Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.

ECC 2:15.text: So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?”  And I said to myself that this too is futile.
ECC 2:15.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?”  And I said to myself that this too is futile.

ECC 2:16.text: For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, just as with the fool, seeing that both will be forgotten in the days to come. Alas, the wise man will die just like the fool!
ECC 2:16.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, just as with the fool, seeing that both will be forgotten in the days to come. Alas, the wise man will die just like the fool!

ECC 2:17.text: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC 2:17.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

ECC 2:18.text: I hated all for which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
ECC 2:18.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] I hated all for which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.

ECC 2:19.text: And who knows whether that man will be wise or foolish? Yet he will take over all the labor at which I have worked skillfully under the sun. This too is futile.
ECC 2:19.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] And who knows whether that man will be wise or foolish? Yet he will take over all the labor at which I have worked skillfully under the sun. This too is futile.

ECC 2:20.text: So my heart began to despair over all the labor that I had done under the sun.
ECC 2:20.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2 · Adultery In Heart] So my heart began to despair over all the labor that I had done under the sun.

ECC 2:21.text: When there is a man who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and he must give his portion to a man who has not worked for it, this too is futile and a great evil.
ECC 2:21.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2 · Inheritance] When there is a man who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and he must give his portion to a man who has not worked for it, this too is futile and a great evil.

ECC 2:22.text: For what does a man get for all the toil and striving with which he labors under the sun?
ECC 2:22.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] For what does a man get for all the toil and striving with which he labors under the sun?

ECC 2:23.text: Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.
ECC 2:23.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.

ECC 2:24.text: Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.
ECC 2:24.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.

ECC 2:25.text: For apart from Him, who can eat and who can find enjoyment?
ECC 2:25.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] For apart from Him, who can eat and who can find enjoyment?

ECC 2:26.text: To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC 2:26.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 2] To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
