ECC 3:14.text: I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.
ECC 3:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 3] I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.

ECC 3:15.text: What exists has already been, and what will be has already been, for God will call to account what has passed.
ECC 3:15.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 3] What exists has already been, and what will be has already been, for God will call to account what has passed.

ECC 3:16.text: Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
ECC 3:16.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 3 · Judgment] Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.

ECC 3:17.text: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”
ECC 3:17.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 3 · Adultery In Heart] I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”

ECC 3:18.text: I said to myself, “As for the sons of men, God tests them so that they may see for themselves that they are but beasts.”
ECC 3:18.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 3] I said to myself, “As for the sons of men, God tests them so that they may see for themselves that they are but beasts.”

ECC 3:19.text: For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other—they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.
ECC 3:19.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 3] For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other—they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.

ECC 3:20.text: All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.
ECC 3:20.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 3] All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.

ECC 3:21.text: Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and the spirit of the animal descends into the earth?
ECC 3:21.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 3 · Fruit of the Spirit] Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and the spirit of the animal descends into the earth?

ECC 3:22.text: I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?
ECC 3:22.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 3] I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?

ECC 4:1.text: Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.
ECC 4:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.

ECC 4:2.text: So I admired the dead, who had already died, above the living, who are still alive.
ECC 4:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] So I admired the dead, who had already died, above the living, who are still alive.

ECC 4:3.text: But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
ECC 4:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.

ECC 4:4.text: I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC 4:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4 · Jealousy] I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

ECC 4:5.text: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.
ECC 4:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.

ECC 4:6.text: Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.
ECC 4:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.

ECC 4:7.text: Again, I saw futility under the sun.
ECC 4:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] Again, I saw futility under the sun.

ECC 4:8.text: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.
ECC 4:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.

ECC 4:9.text: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.
ECC 4:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.

ECC 4:10.text: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
ECC 4:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4 · Compassion] For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!

ECC 4:11.text: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?
ECC 4:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?

ECC 4:12.text: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
ECC 4:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

ECC 4:13.text: Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.
ECC 4:13.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.

ECC 4:14.text: For the youth has come from the prison to the kingship, though he was born poor in his own kingdom.
ECC 4:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4 · Kingdom of God] For the youth has come from the prison to the kingship, though he was born poor in his own kingdom.

ECC 4:15.text: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed this second one, the youth who succeeded the king.
ECC 4:15.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed this second one, the youth who succeeded the king.

ECC 4:16.text: There is no limit to all the people who were before them. Yet the successor will not be celebrated by those who come even later. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC 4:16.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 4] There is no limit to all the people who were before them. Yet the successor will not be celebrated by those who come even later. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

ECC 5:1.text: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.
ECC 5:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.

ECC 5:2.text: Do not be quick to speak, and do not be hasty in your heart to utter a word before God. After all, God is in heaven and you are on earth. So let your words be few.
ECC 5:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5 · Adultery In Heart, Heaven] Do not be quick to speak, and do not be hasty in your heart to utter a word before God. After all, God is in heaven and you are on earth. So let your words be few.

ECC 5:3.text: As a dream comes through many cares, so the speech of a fool comes with many words.
ECC 5:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] As a dream comes through many cares, so the speech of a fool comes with many words.

ECC 5:4.text: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.
ECC 5:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.

ECC 5:5.text: It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.
ECC 5:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.

ECC 5:6.text: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?
ECC 5:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?

ECC 5:7.text: For as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. Therefore, fear God.
ECC 5:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] For as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. Therefore, fear God.

ECC 5:8.text: If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.
ECC 5:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5 · Justice] If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.

ECC 5:9.text: The produce of the earth is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.
ECC 5:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] The produce of the earth is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.

ECC 5:10.text: He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.
ECC 5:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5 · Love] He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.

ECC 5:11.text: When good things increase, so do those who consume them; what then is the profit to the owner, except to behold them with his eyes?
ECC 5:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] When good things increase, so do those who consume them; what then is the profit to the owner, except to behold them with his eyes?

ECC 5:12.text: The sleep of the worker is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich man permits him no sleep.
ECC 5:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] The sleep of the worker is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich man permits him no sleep.

ECC 5:13.text: There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,
ECC 5:13.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,

ECC 5:14.text: or wealth lost in a failed venture, so when that man has a son there is nothing to pass on.
ECC 5:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] or wealth lost in a failed venture, so when that man has a son there is nothing to pass on.

ECC 5:15.text: As a man came from his mother’s womb, so he will depart again, naked as he arrived. He takes nothing for his labor to carry in his hands.
ECC 5:15.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] As a man came from his mother’s womb, so he will depart again, naked as he arrived. He takes nothing for his labor to carry in his hands.

ECC 5:16.text: This too is a grievous evil: Exactly as a man is born, so he will depart. What does he gain as he toils for the wind?
ECC 5:16.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] This too is a grievous evil: Exactly as a man is born, so he will depart. What does he gain as he toils for the wind?

ECC 5:17.text: Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and anger.
ECC 5:17.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and anger.

ECC 5:18.text: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him—for this is his lot.
ECC 5:18.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5 · Contentment] Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him—for this is his lot.

ECC 5:19.text: Furthermore, God has given riches and wealth to every man, and He has enabled him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor. This is a gift from God.
ECC 5:19.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5] Furthermore, God has given riches and wealth to every man, and He has enabled him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor. This is a gift from God.

ECC 5:20.text: For a man seldom considers the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.
ECC 5:20.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 5 · Adultery In Heart] For a man seldom considers the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.

ECC 6:1.text: There is another evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:
ECC 6:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6] There is another evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:

ECC 6:2.text: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.
ECC 6:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6 · Adultery In Heart] God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.

ECC 6:3.text: A man may father a hundred children and live for many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not even receive a proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.
ECC 6:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6 · Blessing, Children] A man may father a hundred children and live for many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not even receive a proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

ECC 6:4.text: For a stillborn child enters in futility and departs in darkness, and his name is shrouded in obscurity.
ECC 6:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6] For a stillborn child enters in futility and departs in darkness, and his name is shrouded in obscurity.

ECC 6:5.text: The child, though neither seeing the sun nor knowing anything, has more rest than that man,
ECC 6:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6] The child, though neither seeing the sun nor knowing anything, has more rest than that man,

ECC 6:6.text: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?
ECC 6:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6 · Blessing] even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?

ECC 6:7.text: All a man’s labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.
ECC 6:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6] All a man’s labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.

ECC 6:8.text: What advantage, then, has the wise man over the fool? What gain comes to the poor man who knows how to conduct himself before others?
ECC 6:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6] What advantage, then, has the wise man over the fool? What gain comes to the poor man who knows how to conduct himself before others?

ECC 6:9.text: Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC 6:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6 · Lust] Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

ECC 6:10.text: Whatever exists was named long ago, and what happens to a man is foreknown; but he cannot contend with one stronger than he.
ECC 6:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6 · Election] Whatever exists was named long ago, and what happens to a man is foreknown; but he cannot contend with one stronger than he.

ECC 6:11.text: For the more words, the more futility—and how does that profit anyone?
ECC 6:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6] For the more words, the more futility—and how does that profit anyone?

ECC 6:12.text: For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?
ECC 6:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 6] For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?

ECC 7:1.text: A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
ECC 7:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Death] A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.

ECC 7:2.text: It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.
ECC 7:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Adultery In Heart, Death] It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.

ECC 7:3.text: Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart.
ECC 7:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Adultery In Heart] Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart.

ECC 7:4.text: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
ECC 7:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Adultery In Heart] The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.

ECC 7:5.text: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.
ECC 7:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.

ECC 7:6.text: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.
ECC 7:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.

ECC 7:7.text: Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
ECC 7:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Adultery In Heart] Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.

ECC 7:8.text: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.
ECC 7:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Fruit of the Spirit] The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.

ECC 7:9.text: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a fool.
ECC 7:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Fruit of the Spirit] Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a fool.

ECC 7:10.text: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.
ECC 7:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · About Forgiveness] Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.

ECC 7:11.text: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.
ECC 7:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Inheritance] Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.

ECC 7:12.text: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
ECC 7:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.

ECC 7:13.text: Consider the work of God: Who can straighten what He has bent?
ECC 7:13.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] Consider the work of God: Who can straighten what He has bent?

ECC 7:14.text: In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.
ECC 7:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Blessing] In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.

ECC 7:15.text: In my futile life I have seen both of these:  A righteous man perishing in his righteousness,   and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.
ECC 7:15.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] In my futile life I have seen both of these:  A righteous man perishing in his righteousness,   and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.

ECC 7:16.text: Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
ECC 7:16.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?

ECC 7:17.text: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
ECC 7:17.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?

ECC 7:18.text: It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand. For he who fears God will follow both warnings.
ECC 7:18.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand. For he who fears God will follow both warnings.

ECC 7:19.text: Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.
ECC 7:19.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.

ECC 7:20.text: Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
ECC 7:20.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.

ECC 7:21.text: Do not pay attention to every word that is spoken, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
ECC 7:21.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] Do not pay attention to every word that is spoken, or you may hear your servant cursing you.

ECC 7:22.text: For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.
ECC 7:22.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Adultery In Heart, End Times] For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.

ECC 7:23.text: All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.
ECC 7:23.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.

ECC 7:24.text: What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?
ECC 7:24.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?

ECC 7:25.text: I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.
ECC 7:25.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.

ECC 7:26.text: And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.
ECC 7:26.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7 · Adultery In Heart, Death] And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.

ECC 7:27.text: “Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.
ECC 7:27.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] “Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.

ECC 7:28.text: While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.
ECC 7:28.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.

ECC 7:29.text: Only this have I found: I have discovered that God made men upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
ECC 7:29.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 7] Only this have I found: I have discovered that God made men upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”

ECC 8:1.text: Who is like the wise man? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A man’s wisdom brightens his face, and the sternness of his face is changed.
ECC 8:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] Who is like the wise man? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A man’s wisdom brightens his face, and the sternness of his face is changed.

ECC 8:2.text: Keep the king’s command, I say, because of your oath before God.
ECC 8:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] Keep the king’s command, I say, because of your oath before God.

ECC 8:3.text: Do not hasten to leave his presence, and do not persist in a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.
ECC 8:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] Do not hasten to leave his presence, and do not persist in a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.

ECC 8:4.text: For the king’s word is supreme, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
ECC 8:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] For the king’s word is supreme, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”

ECC 8:5.text: Whoever keeps his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart knows the right time and procedure.
ECC 8:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8 · Adultery In Heart] Whoever keeps his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart knows the right time and procedure.

ECC 8:6.text: For there is a right time and procedure to every purpose, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.
ECC 8:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] For there is a right time and procedure to every purpose, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.

ECC 8:7.text: Since no one knows what will happen, who can tell him what is to come?
ECC 8:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] Since no one knows what will happen, who can tell him what is to come?

ECC 8:8.text: As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.
ECC 8:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8 · Death, Freedom] As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.

ECC 8:9.text: All this I have seen, applying my mind to every deed that is done under the sun; there is a time when one man lords it over another to his own detriment.
ECC 8:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] All this I have seen, applying my mind to every deed that is done under the sun; there is a time when one man lords it over another to his own detriment.

ECC 8:10.text: Then too, I saw the burial of the wicked who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they were praised in the city where they had done so. This too is futile.
ECC 8:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] Then too, I saw the burial of the wicked who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they were praised in the city where they had done so. This too is futile.

ECC 8:11.text: When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.
ECC 8:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.

ECC 8:12.text: Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I also know that it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence.
ECC 8:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8 · End Times] Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I also know that it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence.

ECC 8:13.text: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.
ECC 8:13.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.

ECC 8:14.text: There is a futility that is done on the earth: There are righteous men who get what the actions of the wicked deserve, and there are wicked men who get what the actions of the righteous deserve. I say that this too is futile.
ECC 8:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] There is a futility that is done on the earth: There are righteous men who get what the actions of the wicked deserve, and there are wicked men who get what the actions of the righteous deserve. I say that this too is futile.

ECC 8:15.text: So I commended the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry. For this joy will accompany him in his labor during the days of his life that God gives him under the sun.
ECC 8:15.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] So I commended the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry. For this joy will accompany him in his labor during the days of his life that God gives him under the sun.

ECC 8:16.text: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth—though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night—
ECC 8:16.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth—though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night—

ECC 8:17.text: I saw every work of God, and that a man is unable to comprehend the work that is done under the sun. Despite his efforts to search it out, he cannot find its meaning; even if the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend.
ECC 8:17.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 8] I saw every work of God, and that a man is unable to comprehend the work that is done under the sun. Despite his efforts to search it out, he cannot find its meaning; even if the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend.

ECC 9:1.text: So I took all this to heart and concluded that the righteous and the wise, as well as their deeds, are in God’s hands. Man does not know what lies ahead, whether love or hate.
ECC 9:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9 · Love, Adultery In Heart] So I took all this to heart and concluded that the righteous and the wise, as well as their deeds, are in God’s hands. Man does not know what lies ahead, whether love or hate.

ECC 9:2.text: It is the same for all: There is a common fate for the righteous and the wicked, for the good and the bad, for the clean and the unclean, for the one who sacrifices and the one who does not. As it is for the good, so it is for the sinner; as it is for the one who makes a vow, so it is for the one who refuses to take a vow.
ECC 9:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] It is the same for all: There is a common fate for the righteous and the wicked, for the good and the bad, for the clean and the unclean, for the one who sacrifices and the one who does not. As it is for the good, so it is for the sinner; as it is for the one who makes a vow, so it is for the one who refuses to take a vow.

ECC 9:3.text: This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun: There is one fate for everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of men are full of evil and madness while they are alive, and afterward they join the dead.
ECC 9:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun: There is one fate for everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of men are full of evil and madness while they are alive, and afterward they join the dead.

ECC 9:4.text: There is hope, however, for anyone who is among the living; for even a live dog is better than a dead lion.
ECC 9:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] There is hope, however, for anyone who is among the living; for even a live dog is better than a dead lion.

ECC 9:5.text: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
ECC 9:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.

ECC 9:6.text: Their love, their hate, and their envy have already vanished, and they will never again have a share in all that is done under the sun.
ECC 9:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9 · Love, Jealousy] Their love, their hate, and their envy have already vanished, and they will never again have a share in all that is done under the sun.

ECC 9:7.text: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:
ECC 9:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9 · Adultery In Heart] Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:

ECC 9:8.text: Let your garments always be white, and never spare the oil for your head.
ECC 9:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] Let your garments always be white, and never spare the oil for your head.

ECC 9:9.text: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.
ECC 9:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9 · Love, Inheritance] Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.

ECC 9:10.text: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
ECC 9:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9 · Death] Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.

ECC 9:11.text: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.
ECC 9:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9 · Blessing] I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.

ECC 9:12.text: For surely no man knows his time: Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, so men are ensnared in an evil time that suddenly falls upon them.
ECC 9:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] For surely no man knows his time: Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, so men are ensnared in an evil time that suddenly falls upon them.

ECC 9:13.text: I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:
ECC 9:13.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:

ECC 9:14.text: There was a small city with few men. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.
ECC 9:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] There was a small city with few men. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.

ECC 9:15.text: Now a poor wise man was found in the city, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
ECC 9:15.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] Now a poor wise man was found in the city, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.

ECC 9:16.text: And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.”
ECC 9:16.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.”

ECC 9:17.text: The calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools.
ECC 9:17.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] The calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools.

ECC 9:18.text: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
ECC 9:18.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 9] Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

ECC 10:1.text: As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
ECC 10:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.

ECC 10:2.text: A wise man’s heart inclines to the right, but the heart of a fool to the left.
ECC 10:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10 · Adultery In Heart] A wise man’s heart inclines to the right, but the heart of a fool to the left.

ECC 10:3.text: Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
ECC 10:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.

ECC 10:4.text: If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.
ECC 10:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.

ECC 10:5.text: There is an evil I have seen under the sun— an error that proceeds from the ruler:
ECC 10:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] There is an evil I have seen under the sun— an error that proceeds from the ruler:

ECC 10:6.text: Folly is appointed to great heights, but the rich sit in lowly positions.
ECC 10:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] Folly is appointed to great heights, but the rich sit in lowly positions.

ECC 10:7.text: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.
ECC 10:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.

ECC 10:8.text: He who digs a pit may fall into it, and he who breaches a wall may be bitten by a snake.
ECC 10:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] He who digs a pit may fall into it, and he who breaches a wall may be bitten by a snake.

ECC 10:9.text: The one who quarries stones may be injured by them, and he who splits logs endangers himself.
ECC 10:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] The one who quarries stones may be injured by them, and he who splits logs endangers himself.

ECC 10:10.text: If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but skill produces success.
ECC 10:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but skill produces success.

ECC 10:11.text: If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.
ECC 10:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.

ECC 10:12.text: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.
ECC 10:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.

ECC 10:13.text: The beginning of his talk is folly, and the end of his speech is evil madness.
ECC 10:13.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] The beginning of his talk is folly, and the end of his speech is evil madness.

ECC 10:14.text: Yet the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming, and who can tell him what will come after him?
ECC 10:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] Yet the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming, and who can tell him what will come after him?

ECC 10:15.text: The toil of a fool wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.
ECC 10:15.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] The toil of a fool wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.

ECC 10:16.text: Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth, and whose princes feast in the morning.
ECC 10:16.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth, and whose princes feast in the morning.

ECC 10:17.text: Blessed are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes feast at the proper time— for strength and not for drunkenness.
ECC 10:17.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10 · Beatitudes] Blessed are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes feast at the proper time— for strength and not for drunkenness.

ECC 10:18.text: Through laziness the roof caves in, and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.
ECC 10:18.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] Through laziness the roof caves in, and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.

ECC 10:19.text: A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.
ECC 10:19.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10] A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.

ECC 10:20.text: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich even in your bedroom, for a bird of the air may carry your words, and a winged creature may report your speech.
ECC 10:20.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 10 · Curse God] Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich even in your bedroom, for a bird of the air may carry your words, and a winged creature may report your speech.

ECC 11:1.text: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.
ECC 11:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11] Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.

ECC 11:2.text: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.
ECC 11:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11 · Inheritance] Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.

ECC 11:3.text: If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.
ECC 11:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11] If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.

ECC 11:4.text: He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.
ECC 11:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11] He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.

ECC 11:5.text: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
ECC 11:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11 · Creation] As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.

ECC 11:6.text: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.
ECC 11:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11] Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.

ECC 11:7.text: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.
ECC 11:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11 · Light] Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.

ECC 11:8.text: So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is futile.
ECC 11:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11] So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is futile.

ECC 11:9.text: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.
ECC 11:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11 · Adultery In Heart, Judgment] Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.

ECC 11:10.text: So banish sorrow from your heart, and cast off pain from your body, for youth and vigor are fleeting.
ECC 11:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 11 · Adultery In Heart] So banish sorrow from your heart, and cast off pain from your body, for youth and vigor are fleeting.

ECC 12:1.text: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”
ECC 12:1.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12] Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”

ECC 12:2.text: before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain,
ECC 12:2.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12 · Light] before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain,

ECC 12:3.text: on the day the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when those grinding cease because they are few and those watching through windows see dimly,
ECC 12:3.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12] on the day the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when those grinding cease because they are few and those watching through windows see dimly,

ECC 12:4.text: when the doors to the street are shut and the sound of the mill fades away, when one rises at the sound of a bird and all the daughters of song grow faint,
ECC 12:4.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12] when the doors to the street are shut and the sound of the mill fades away, when one rises at the sound of a bird and all the daughters of song grow faint,

ECC 12:5.text: when men fear the heights and dangers of the road, when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper loses its spring, and the caper berry shrivels— for then man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.
ECC 12:5.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12 · Eternal Life] when men fear the heights and dangers of the road, when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper loses its spring, and the caper berry shrivels— for then man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.

ECC 12:6.text: Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel is broken at the well,
ECC 12:6.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12] Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel is broken at the well,

ECC 12:7.text: before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
ECC 12:7.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12 · Fruit of the Spirit] before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

ECC 12:8.text: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”
ECC 12:8.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12] “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”

ECC 12:9.text: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
ECC 12:9.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12] Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.

ECC 12:10.text: The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth.
ECC 12:10.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12] The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth.

ECC 12:11.text: The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.
ECC 12:11.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12] The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.

ECC 12:12.text: And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.
ECC 12:12.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12] And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.

ECC 12:13.text: When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.
ECC 12:13.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12 · Law] When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.

ECC 12:14.text: For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
ECC 12:14.bm25Text: [Ecclesiastes · Chapter 12 · Judgment] For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.

EPH 1:1.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God,  To the saints in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus:
EPH 1:1.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Faith, Body of Christ] Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God,  To the saints in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus:

EPH 1:2.text: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
EPH 1:2.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, God the Father] Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

EPH 1:3.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms.
EPH 1:3.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Blessing, Body of Christ] Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms.

EPH 1:4.text: For He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless in His presence. In love
EPH 1:4.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Love] For He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless in His presence. In love

EPH 1:5.text: He predestined us for adoption as His sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of His will,
EPH 1:5.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Adoption, Body of Christ] He predestined us for adoption as His sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of His will,

EPH 1:6.text: to the praise of His glorious grace, which He has freely given us in the Beloved One.
EPH 1:6.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Love, Grace] to the praise of His glorious grace, which He has freely given us in the Beloved One.

EPH 1:7.text: In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace
EPH 1:7.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Forgiveness, About Forgiveness] In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace

EPH 1:8.text: that He lavished on us with all wisdom and understanding.
EPH 1:8.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1] that He lavished on us with all wisdom and understanding.

EPH 1:9.text: And He has made known to us the mystery of His will according to His good pleasure, which He purposed in Christ
EPH 1:9.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] And He has made known to us the mystery of His will according to His good pleasure, which He purposed in Christ

EPH 1:10.text: as a plan for the fullness of time, to bring all things in heaven and on earth together in Christ.
EPH 1:10.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Heaven] as a plan for the fullness of time, to bring all things in heaven and on earth together in Christ.

EPH 1:11.text: In Him we were also chosen as God’s own, having been predestined according to the plan of Him who works out everything by the counsel of His will,
EPH 1:11.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Election] In Him we were also chosen as God’s own, having been predestined according to the plan of Him who works out everything by the counsel of His will,

EPH 1:12.text: in order that we, who were the first to hope in Christ, would be for the praise of His glory.
EPH 1:12.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Glory] in order that we, who were the first to hope in Christ, would be for the praise of His glory.

EPH 1:13.text: And in Him, having heard and believed the word of truth—the gospel of your salvation—you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,
EPH 1:13.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Faith, Fruit of the Spirit] And in Him, having heard and believed the word of truth—the gospel of your salvation—you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,

EPH 1:14.text: who is the pledge of our inheritance until the redemption of those who are God’s possession, to the praise of His glory.
EPH 1:14.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Glory, Inheritance] who is the pledge of our inheritance until the redemption of those who are God’s possession, to the praise of His glory.

EPH 1:15.text: For this reason, ever since I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,
EPH 1:15.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Love, Faith] For this reason, ever since I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,

EPH 1:16.text: I have not stopped giving thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers,
EPH 1:16.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Generosity] I have not stopped giving thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers,

EPH 1:17.text: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him.
EPH 1:17.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Fruit of the Spirit] that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him.

EPH 1:18.text: I ask that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened, so that you may know the hope of His calling, the riches of His glorious inheritance in the saints,
EPH 1:18.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Adultery In Heart, Calling] I ask that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened, so that you may know the hope of His calling, the riches of His glorious inheritance in the saints,

EPH 1:19.text: and the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe. These are in accordance with the working of His mighty strength,
EPH 1:19.bm25Text: [Ephesians · Chapter 1 · Faith] and the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe. These are in accordance with the working of His mighty strength,

EPH 1:20.text: which He exerted in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly realms,

EXO 22:1.text: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters or sells it, he must repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
EXO 22:1.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 22] “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters or sells it, he must repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.

EXO 22:2.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 22 · Death] If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed.

EXO 22:4.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 22] If what was stolen is actually found alive in his possession—whether ox or donkey or sheep—he must pay back double.

EXO 22:5.text: If a man grazes his livestock in a field or vineyard and allows them to stray so that they graze in someone else’s field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard.
EXO 22:5.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 22] If a man grazes his livestock in a field or vineyard and allows them to stray so that they graze in someone else’s field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard.

EXO 22:6.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 22] If a fire breaks out and spreads to thornbushes so that it consumes stacked or standing grain, or the whole field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.

EXO 22:7.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 22] If a man gives his neighbor money or goods for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house, the thief, if caught, must pay back double.

EXO 22:8.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 22] If the thief is not found, the owner of the house must appear before the judges to determine whether he has taken his neighbor’s property.

EXO 22:9.text: In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims, ‘This is mine,’ both parties shall bring their cases before the judges. The one whom the judges find guilty must pay back double to his neighbor.
EXO 22:9.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 22] In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims, ‘This is mine,’ both parties shall bring their cases before the judges. EXO 22:15.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 22] If the owner was present, no restitution is required. If the animal was rented, the fee covers the loss.

EXO 23:2.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23 · Justice] You shall not follow the crowd in wrongdoing. When you testify in a lawsuit, do not pervert justice by siding with the crowd.

EXO 23:3.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] And do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.

EXO 23:4.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] If you encounter your enemy’s stray ox or donkey, you must return it to him.

EXO 23:5.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] If you see the donkey of one who hates you fallen under its load, do not leave it there; you must help him with it.

EXO 23:6.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23 · Justice] You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.

EXO 23:7.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23 · False Gods, False Witness] Stay far away from a false accusation. Do not kill the innocent or the just, for I will not acquit the guilty.

EXO 23:8.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.

EXO 23:9.text: Do not oppress a foreign resident, since you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
EXO 23:9.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] Do not oppress a foreign resident, since you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

EXO 23:10.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] For six years you are to sow your land and gather its produce,

EXO 23:13.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] Pay close attention to everything I have said to you. You must not invoke the names of other gods; they must not be heard on your lips.

EXO 23:16.text: You are also to keep the Feast of Harvest with the firstfruits of the produce from what you sow in the field.  And keep the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather your produce from the field.

EXO 23:18.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] You must not offer the blood of My sacrifices with anything leavened, nor may the fat of My feast remain until morning.

EXO 23:19.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God.  You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.

EXO 23:20.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] Behold, I am sending an angel before you to protect you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.

EXO 23:21.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23 · Forgiveness] Pay attention to him and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.

EXO 23:22.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] But if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.

EXO 23:24.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] You must not bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their practices. Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.

EXO 23:25.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. And I will take away sickness from among you.

EXO 23:26.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] No woman in your land will miscarry or be barren; I will fulfill the number of your days.

EXO 23:27.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] I will send My terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn and run.

EXO 23:30.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.

EXO 23:33.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 23] They must not remain in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me. For if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”

EXO 24:2.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 24] Moses alone shall approach the LORD, but the others must not come near. And the people may not go up with him.”

EXO 24:5.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 24 · Israel] Then he sent out some young men of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.

EXO 24:11.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 24 · Israel] But God did not lay His hand on the nobles of Israel; they saw Him, and they ate and drank.

EXO 24:12.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 24 · Law] Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to Me on the mountain and stay here, so that I may give you the tablets of stone, with the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.”

EXO 24:13.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 24] So Moses set out with Joshua his attendant and went up on the mountain of God.

EXO 24:14.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 24 · Leadership] And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute can go to them.”

EXO 24:18.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 24] Moses entered the cloud as he went up on the mountain, and he remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

EXO 25:3.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] This is the offering you are to accept from them:  gold, silver, and bronze;

EXO 25:4.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] blue, purple, and scarlet yarn;   fine linen and goat hair;

EXO 25:6.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25 · Anointing, Light] olive oil for the light;   spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;

EXO 25:7.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] and onyx stones and gemstones to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.

EXO 25:10.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] And they are to construct an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.

EXO 25:11.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] Overlay it with pure gold both inside and out, and make a gold molding around it.

EXO 25:12.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.

EXO 25:14.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, in order to carry it.

EXO 25:16.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] And place inside the ark the Testimony, which I will give you.

EXO 25:17.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25 · Forgiveness, Compassion] And you are to construct a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.

EXO 25:18.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25 · Forgiveness, Compassion] Make two cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the mercy seat,

EXO 25:19.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] one cherub on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold.

EXO 25:21.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25 · Forgiveness, Compassion] Set the mercy seat atop the ark, and put the Testimony that I will give you into the ark.

EXO 25:23.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] You are also to make a table of acacia wood two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.

EXO 25:24.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding around it.

EXO 25:25.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] And make a rim around it a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.

EXO 25:26.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] Make four gold rings for the table and fasten them to the four corners at its four legs.

EXO 25:27.text: The rings are to be close to the rim, to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
EXO 25:27.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] The rings are to be close to the rim, to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table.

EXO 25:28.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, so that the table may be carried with them.

EXO 25:29.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] You are also to make the plates and dishes, as well as the pitchers and bowls for pouring drink offerings. Make them out of pure gold.

EXO 25:30.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25 · End Times] And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times.

EXO 25:31.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] Then you are to make a lampstand of pure, hammered gold. It shall be made of one piece, including its base and shaft, its cups, and its buds and petals.

EXO 25:32.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] Six branches are to extend from the sides of the lampstand—three on one side and three on the other.

EXO 25:33.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] There are to be three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the first branch, each with buds and petals, three on the next branch, and the same for all six branches that extend from the lampstand.

EXO 25:34.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] And on the lampstand there shall be four cups shaped like almond blossoms with buds and petals.

EXO 25:35.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] For the six branches that extend from the lampstand, a bud must be under the first pair of branches, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair.

EXO 25:36.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] The buds and branches are to be all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.

EXO 25:37.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 25] Make seven lamps and set them up on the lampstand so that they illuminate the area in front of it.

EXO 26:1.text: “You are to construct the tabernacle itself with ten curtains of finely spun linen, each with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and cherubim skillfully worked into them.
EXO 26:1.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] “You are to construct the tabernacle itself with ten curtains of finely spun linen, each with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and cherubim skillfully worked into them.

EXO 26:2.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide—all curtains the same size.

EXO 26:3.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] Five of the curtains are to be joined together, and the other five joined as well.

EXO 26:4.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] Make loops of blue material on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same for the end curtain in the second set.

EXO 26:5.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, so that the loops line up opposite one another.

EXO 26:6.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] Make fifty gold clasps as well, and join the curtains together with the clasps, so that the tabernacle will be a unit.

EXO 26:7.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] You are to make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle—eleven curtains in all.

EXO 26:8.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] Each of the eleven curtains is to be the same size—thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.

EXO 26:9.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] Join five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another. Then fold the sixth curtain over double at the front of the tent.

EXO 26:10.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.

EXO 26:11.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] Make fifty bronze clasps and put them through the loops to join the tent together as a unit.

EXO 26:12.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] As for the overlap that remains of the tent curtains, the half curtain that is left over shall hang down over the back of the tabernacle.

EXO 26:19.bm25Text: [Exodus · Chapter 26] with forty silver bases under the twenty frames—two bases for each frame, one under each tenon.
