EZR 9:1.text: After these things had been accomplished, the leaders approached me and said, “The people of Israel, including the priests and Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the surrounding peoples whose abominations are like those of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.
EZR 9:1.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] After these things had been accomplished, the leaders approached me and said, “The people of Israel, including the priests and Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the surrounding peoples whose abominations are like those of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.

EZR 9:2.text: Indeed, the Israelites have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed has been mixed with the people of the land. And the leaders and officials have taken the lead in this unfaithfulness!”
EZR 9:2.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9 · Faith, Adultery] Indeed, the Israelites have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed has been mixed with the people of the land. And the leaders and officials have taken the lead in this unfaithfulness!”

EZR 9:3.text: When I heard this report, I tore my tunic and cloak, pulled out some hair from my head and beard, and sat down in horror.
EZR 9:3.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9] When I heard this report, I tore my tunic and cloak, pulled out some hair from my head and beard, and sat down in horror.

EZR 9:4.text: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I sat there in horror until the evening offering.
EZR 9:4.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9 · Faith, Adultery] Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I sat there in horror until the evening offering.

EZR 9:5.text: At the evening offering, I got up from my humiliation with my tunic and cloak torn, and I fell on my knees, spread out my hands to the LORD my God,
EZR 9:5.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9] At the evening offering, I got up from my humiliation with my tunic and cloak torn, and I fell on my knees, spread out my hands to the LORD my God,

EZR 9:6.text: and said:  “O my God, I am ashamed and embarrassed to lift up my face to You, my God, because our iniquities are higher than our heads, and our guilt has reached the heavens.
EZR 9:6.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9] and said:  “O my God, I am ashamed and embarrassed to lift up my face to You, my God, because our iniquities are higher than our heads, and our guilt has reached the heavens.

EZR 9:7.text: From the days of our fathers to this day, our guilt has been great. Because of our iniquities, we and our kings and priests have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the earth and put to the sword and captivity, to pillage and humiliation, as we are this day.
EZR 9:7.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9] From the days of our fathers to this day, our guilt has been great. Because of our iniquities, we and our kings and priests have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the earth and put to the sword and captivity, to pillage and humiliation, as we are this day.

EZR 9:8.text: But now, for a brief moment, grace has come from the LORD our God to preserve for us a remnant and to give us a stake in His holy place. Even in our bondage, our God has given us new life and light to our eyes.
EZR 9:8.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9 · Grace, Light] But now, for a brief moment, grace has come from the LORD our God to preserve for us a remnant and to give us a stake in His holy place. Even in our bondage, our God has given us new life and light to our eyes.

EZR 9:9.text: Though we are slaves, our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but He has extended to us grace in the sight of the kings of Persia, giving us new life to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins, and giving us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.
EZR 9:9.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9 · Generosity, Grace] Though we are slaves, our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but He has extended to us grace in the sight of the kings of Persia, giving us new life to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins, and giving us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.

EZR 9:10.text: And now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have forsaken the commandments
EZR 9:10.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9 · Law] And now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have forsaken the commandments

EZR 9:11.text: that You gave through Your servants the prophets, saying: ‘The land that you are entering to possess is a land polluted by the impurity of its peoples and the abominations with which they have filled it from end to end.
EZR 9:11.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9] that You gave through Your servants the prophets, saying: ‘The land that you are entering to possess is a land polluted by the impurity of its peoples and the abominations with which they have filled it from end to end.

EZR 9:12.text: Now, therefore, do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or prosperity, so that you may be strong and may eat the good things of the land, leaving it as an inheritance to your sons forever.’
EZR 9:12.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9 · Blessing, Inheritance] Now, therefore, do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or prosperity, so that you may be strong and may eat the good things of the land, leaving it as an inheritance to your sons forever.’

EZR 9:13.text: After all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt (though You, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve and have given us such a remnant as this),
EZR 9:13.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9] After all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt (though You, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve and have given us such a remnant as this),

EZR 9:14.text: shall we again break Your commandments and intermarry with the peoples who commit these abominations? Would You not become so angry with us as to wipe us out, leaving no remnant or survivor?
EZR 9:14.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9 · Law] shall we again break Your commandments and intermarry with the peoples who commit these abominations? Would You not become so angry with us as to wipe us out, leaving no remnant or survivor?

EZR 9:15.text: O LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous! For we remain this day as a remnant. Here we are before You in our guilt, though because of it no one can stand before You.”
EZR 9:15.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 9 · Israel] O LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous! For we remain this day as a remnant. Here we are before You in our guilt, though because of it no one can stand before You.”

EZR 10:1.text: While Ezra prayed and made this confession, weeping and falling facedown before the house of God, a very large assembly of Israelites—men, women, and children—gathered around him, and the people wept bitterly as well.
EZR 10:1.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 10 · Biblical Women, Children] While Ezra prayed and made this confession, weeping and falling facedown before the house of God, a very large assembly of Israelites—men, women, and children—gathered around him, and the people wept bitterly as well.

EZR 10:2.text: Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, an Elamite, said to Ezra: “We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the people of the land, yet in spite of this, there is hope for Israel.
EZR 10:2.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 10 · Faith, Biblical Women] Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, an Elamite, said to Ezra: “We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the people of the land, yet in spite of this, there is hope for Israel.

EZR 10:3.text: So now let us make a covenant before our God to send away all the foreign wives and their children, according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the command of our God. Let it be done according to the Law.
EZR 10:3.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 10 · Children, Covenant] So now let us make a covenant before our God to send away all the foreign wives and their children, according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the command of our God. Let it be done according to the Law.

EZR 10:4.text: Get up, for this matter is your responsibility, and we will support you. Be strong and take action!”
EZR 10:4.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 10] Get up, for this matter is your responsibility, and we will support you. Be strong and take action!”

EZR 10:5.text: So Ezra got up and made the leading priests, Levites, and all Israel take an oath to do what had been said. And they took the oath.
EZR 10:5.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 10 · Israel] So Ezra got up and made the leading priests, Levites, and all Israel take an oath to do what had been said. And they took the oath.

EZR 10:6.text: Then Ezra withdrew from before the house of God and walked to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. And while he stayed there, he ate no food and drank no water, because he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
EZR 10:6.bm25Text: [Ezra · Chapter 10 · Faith, Adultery] Then Ezra withdrew from before the house of God and walked to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. And while he stayed there, he ate no food and drank no water, because he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.

EZR 10:7.text: And a proclamation was issued throughout Judah and Jerusalem that all the exiles should gather at Jerusalem.

EZR 10:8.text: Whoever failed to appear within three days would forfeit all his property, according to the counsel of the leaders and elders, and would himself be expelled from the assembly of the exiles.

GAL 1:1.text: Paul, an apostle—sent not from men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead—
GAL 1:1.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, God the Father] Paul, an apostle—sent not from men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead—

GAL 1:2.text: and all the brothers with me,  To the churches of Galatia:
GAL 1:2.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1] and all the brothers with me,  To the churches of Galatia:

GAL 1:3.text: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
GAL 1:3.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, God the Father] Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,

GAL 1:4.text: who gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
GAL 1:4.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · God the Father] who gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,

GAL 1:5.text: to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
GAL 1:5.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Glory] to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

GAL 1:6.text: I am amazed how quickly you are deserting the One who called you by the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel—
GAL 1:6.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Gospel] I am amazed how quickly you are deserting the One who called you by the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel—

GAL 1:7.text: which is not even a gospel. Evidently some people are troubling you and trying to distort the gospel of Christ.
GAL 1:7.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Gospel] which is not even a gospel. Evidently some people are troubling you and trying to distort the gospel of Christ.

GAL 1:8.text: But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be under a curse!
GAL 1:8.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Curse God, Gospel] But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be under a curse!

GAL 1:9.text: As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be under a curse!
GAL 1:9.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Curse God, Gospel] As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be under a curse!

GAL 1:10.text: Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
GAL 1:10.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ.

GAL 1:11.text: For I certify to you, brothers, that the gospel I preached was not devised by man.
GAL 1:11.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Gospel] For I certify to you, brothers, that the gospel I preached was not devised by man.

GAL 1:12.text: I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it; rather, I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ.
GAL 1:12.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it; rather, I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ.

GAL 1:13.text: For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.
GAL 1:13.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Church, Destroy Canaan] For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.

GAL 1:14.text: I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries and was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
GAL 1:14.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1] I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries and was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

GAL 1:15.text: But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by His grace, was pleased
GAL 1:15.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Grace] But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by His grace, was pleased

GAL 1:16.text: to reveal His Son in me so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood,
GAL 1:16.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1] to reveal His Son in me so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood,

GAL 1:17.text: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the apostles who came before me, but I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.
GAL 1:17.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Apostles] nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the apostles who came before me, but I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.

GAL 1:18.text: Only after three years did I go up to Jerusalem to confer with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
GAL 1:18.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1] Only after three years did I go up to Jerusalem to confer with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.

GAL 1:19.text: But I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.
GAL 1:19.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Apostles] But I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.

GAL 1:20.text: I assure you before God that what I am writing to you is no lie.
GAL 1:20.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1] I assure you before God that what I am writing to you is no lie.

GAL 1:21.text: Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
GAL 1:21.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1] Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

GAL 1:22.text: I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
GAL 1:22.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.

GAL 1:23.text: They only heard the account: “The man who formerly persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.”
GAL 1:23.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1 · Faith, Destroy Canaan] They only heard the account: “The man who formerly persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.”

GAL 1:24.text: And they glorified God because of me.
GAL 1:24.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 1] And they glorified God because of me.

GAL 2:1.text: Fourteen years later I went up again to Jerusalem, accompanied by Barnabas. I took Titus along also.
GAL 2:1.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] Fourteen years later I went up again to Jerusalem, accompanied by Barnabas. I took Titus along also.

GAL 2:2.text: I went in response to a revelation and set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders, for fear that I was running or had already run in vain.
GAL 2:2.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Gospel] I went in response to a revelation and set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders, for fear that I was running or had already run in vain.

GAL 2:3.text: Yet not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.
GAL 2:3.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] Yet not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.

GAL 2:4.text: This issue arose because some false brothers had come in under false pretenses to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.
GAL 2:4.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Body of Christ, False Gods] This issue arose because some false brothers had come in under false pretenses to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.

GAL 2:5.text: We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.
GAL 2:5.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Gospel] We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.

GAL 2:6.text: But as for the highly esteemed—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism—those leaders added nothing to me.
GAL 2:6.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] But as for the highly esteemed—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism—those leaders added nothing to me.

GAL 2:7.text: On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted to preach the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised.
GAL 2:7.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Faith, Gospel] On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted to preach the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised.

GAL 2:8.text: For the One who was at work in Peter’s apostleship to the circumcised was also at work in my apostleship to the Gentiles.
GAL 2:8.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] For the One who was at work in Peter’s apostleship to the circumcised was also at work in my apostleship to the Gentiles.

GAL 2:9.text: And recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
GAL 2:9.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Fellowship, Grace] And recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.

GAL 2:10.text: They only asked us to remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do.
GAL 2:10.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] They only asked us to remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do.

GAL 2:11.text: When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face, because he stood to be condemned.
GAL 2:11.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face, because he stood to be condemned.

GAL 2:12.text: For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, for fear of those in the circumcision group.
GAL 2:12.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, for fear of those in the circumcision group.

GAL 2:13.text: The other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.
GAL 2:13.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] The other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.

GAL 2:14.text: When I saw that they were not walking in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”
GAL 2:14.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Gospel] When I saw that they were not walking in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”

GAL 2:15.text: We who are Jews by birth and not Gentile “sinners”
GAL 2:15.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] We who are Jews by birth and not Gentile “sinners”

GAL 2:16.text: know that a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ. So we, too, have believed in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.
GAL 2:16.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Faith, Body of Christ] know that a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ. So we, too, have believed in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.

GAL 2:17.text: But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin? Certainly not!
GAL 2:17.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin? Certainly not!

GAL 2:18.text: If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I prove myself to be a lawbreaker.
GAL 2:18.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I prove myself to be a lawbreaker.

GAL 2:19.text: For through the law I died to the law so that I might live to God.
GAL 2:19.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2] For through the law I died to the law so that I might live to God.

GAL 2:20.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.
GAL 2:20.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Love, Faith] I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.

GAL 2:21.text: I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, Christ died for nothing.
GAL 2:21.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 2 · Body of Christ, Grace] I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, Christ died for nothing.

GAL 3:1.text: O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your very eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified.
GAL 3:1.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your very eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified.

GAL 3:2.text: I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith?
GAL 3:2.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Faith] I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith?

GAL 3:3.text: Are you so foolish? After starting in the Spirit, are you now finishing in the flesh?
GAL 3:3.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Fruit of the Spirit] Are you so foolish? After starting in the Spirit, are you now finishing in the flesh?

GAL 3:4.text: Have you suffered so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing?
GAL 3:4.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3] Have you suffered so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing?

GAL 3:5.text: Does God lavish His Spirit on you and work miracles among you because you practice the law, or because you hear and believe?
GAL 3:5.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Faith] Does God lavish His Spirit on you and work miracles among you because you practice the law, or because you hear and believe?

GAL 3:6.text: So also, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
GAL 3:6.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Faith] So also, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

GAL 3:7.text: Understand, then, that those who have faith are sons of Abraham.
GAL 3:7.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Faith] Understand, then, that those who have faith are sons of Abraham.

GAL 3:8.text: The Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and foretold the gospel to Abraham: “All nations will be blessed through you.”
GAL 3:8.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Faith, Gospel] The Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and foretold the gospel to Abraham: “All nations will be blessed through you.”

GAL 3:9.text: So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
GAL 3:9.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Faith] So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.

GAL 3:10.text: All who rely on works of the law are under a curse. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law.”
GAL 3:10.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Curse God] All who rely on works of the law are under a curse. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law.”

GAL 3:11.text: Now it is clear that no one is justified before God by the law, because, “The righteous will live by faith.”
GAL 3:11.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Faith] Now it is clear that no one is justified before God by the law, because, “The righteous will live by faith.”

GAL 3:12.text: The law, however, is not based on faith; on the contrary, “The man who does these things will live by them.”
GAL 3:12.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Faith] The law, however, is not based on faith; on the contrary, “The man who does these things will live by them.”

GAL 3:13.text: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”
GAL 3:13.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Body of Christ] Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”

GAL 3:14.text: He redeemed us in order that the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit.
GAL 3:14.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Faith] He redeemed us in order that the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit.

GAL 3:15.text: Brothers, let me put this in human terms. Even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.
GAL 3:15.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant] Brothers, let me put this in human terms. Even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.

GAL 3:16.text: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.
GAL 3:16.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.

GAL 3:17.text: What I mean is this: The law that came 430 years later does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.
GAL 3:17.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant] What I mean is this: The law that came 430 years later does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.

GAL 3:18.text: For if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise; but God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.
GAL 3:18.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Inheritance] For if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise; but God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.

GAL 3:19.text: Why then was the law given? It was added because of transgressions, until the arrival of the seed to whom the promise referred. It was administered through angels by a mediator.
GAL 3:19.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Angels] Why then was the law given? It was added because of transgressions, until the arrival of the seed to whom the promise referred. It was administered through angels by a mediator.

GAL 3:20.text: A mediator is unnecessary, however, for only one party; but God is one.
GAL 3:20.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3] A mediator is unnecessary, however, for only one party; but God is one.

GAL 3:21.text: Is the law, then, opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would certainly have come from the law.
GAL 3:21.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant] Is the law, then, opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would certainly have come from the law.

GAL 3:22.text: But the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin, so that by faith in Jesus Christ the promise might be given to those who believe.
GAL 3:22.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Faith] But the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin, so that by faith in Jesus Christ the promise might be given to those who believe.

GAL 3:23.text: Before this faith came, we were held in custody under the law, locked up until faith should be revealed.
GAL 3:23.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Faith] Before this faith came, we were held in custody under the law, locked up until faith should be revealed.

GAL 3:24.text: So the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
GAL 3:24.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Faith] So the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

GAL 3:25.text: Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
GAL 3:25.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Faith] Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.

GAL 3:26.text: You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
GAL 3:26.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Faith, Adoption] You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.

GAL 3:27.text: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
GAL 3:27.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.

GAL 3:28.text: There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
GAL 3:28.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Body of Christ, Female] There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.

GAL 3:29.text: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.
GAL 3:29.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 3 · Covenant, Adoption] And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.

GAL 4:1.text: What I am saying is that as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, although he is the owner of everything.
GAL 4:1.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Inheritance] What I am saying is that as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, although he is the owner of everything.

GAL 4:2.text: He is subject to guardians and trustees until the date set by his father.
GAL 4:2.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Faith, God the Father] He is subject to guardians and trustees until the date set by his father.

GAL 4:3.text: So also, when we were children, we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world.
GAL 4:3.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Children] So also, when we were children, we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world.

GAL 4:4.text: But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
GAL 4:4.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,

GAL 4:5.text: to redeem those under the law, that we might receive our adoption as sons.
GAL 4:5.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Adoption] to redeem those under the law, that we might receive our adoption as sons.

GAL 4:6.text: And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”
GAL 4:6.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Fruit of the Spirit, God the Father] And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”

GAL 4:7.text: So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God.
GAL 4:7.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Inheritance] So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God.

GAL 4:8.text: Formerly, when you did not know God, you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods.
GAL 4:8.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] Formerly, when you did not know God, you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods.

GAL 4:9.text: But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles? Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again?
GAL 4:9.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles? Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again?

GAL 4:10.text: You are observing special days and months and seasons and years!
GAL 4:10.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] You are observing special days and months and seasons and years!

GAL 4:11.text: I fear for you, that my efforts for you may have been in vain.
GAL 4:11.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] I fear for you, that my efforts for you may have been in vain.

GAL 4:12.text: I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you. You have done me no wrong.
GAL 4:12.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you. You have done me no wrong.

GAL 4:13.text: You know that it was because of an illness that I first preached the gospel to you.
GAL 4:13.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Gospel] You know that it was because of an illness that I first preached the gospel to you.

GAL 4:14.text: And although my illness was a trial to you, you did not despise or reject me. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God, as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.
GAL 4:14.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] And although my illness was a trial to you, you did not despise or reject me. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God, as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.

GAL 4:15.text: What then has become of your blessing? For I can testify that, if it were possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
GAL 4:15.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Blessing] What then has become of your blessing? For I can testify that, if it were possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.

GAL 4:16.text: Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?
GAL 4:16.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?

GAL 4:17.text: Those people are zealous for you, but not in a good way. Instead, they want to isolate you from us, so that you may be zealous for them.
GAL 4:17.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] Those people are zealous for you, but not in a good way. Instead, they want to isolate you from us, so that you may be zealous for them.

GAL 4:18.text: Nevertheless, it is good to be zealous if it serves a noble purpose—at any time, and not only when I am with you.
GAL 4:18.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] Nevertheless, it is good to be zealous if it serves a noble purpose—at any time, and not only when I am with you.

GAL 4:19.text: My children, for whom I am again in the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you,
GAL 4:19.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Body of Christ, Children] My children, for whom I am again in the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you,

GAL 4:20.text: how I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.
GAL 4:20.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · About Forgiveness] how I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.

GAL 4:21.text: Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not understand what the law says?
GAL 4:21.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not understand what the law says?

GAL 4:22.text: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman.
GAL 4:22.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman.

GAL 4:23.text: His son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, but his son by the free woman was born through the promise.
GAL 4:23.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Covenant] His son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, but his son by the free woman was born through the promise.

GAL 4:24.text: These things serve as illustrations, for the women represent two covenants. One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery: This is Hagar.
GAL 4:24.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Biblical Women, Children] These things serve as illustrations, for the women represent two covenants. One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery: This is Hagar.

GAL 4:25.text: Now Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem, because she is in slavery with her children.
GAL 4:25.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Children] Now Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem, because she is in slavery with her children.

GAL 4:26.text: But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
GAL 4:26.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4] But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.

GAL 4:27.text: For it is written:  “Rejoice, O barren woman, who bears no children; break forth and cry aloud, you who have never travailed; because more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband.”
GAL 4:27.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Children] For it is written:  “Rejoice, O barren woman, who bears no children; break forth and cry aloud, you who have never travailed; because more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband.”

GAL 4:28.text: Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise.
GAL 4:28.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Children, Covenant] Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise.

GAL 4:29.text: At that time, however, the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit. It is the same now.
GAL 4:29.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Fruit of the Spirit] At that time, however, the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit. It is the same now.

GAL 4:30.text: But what does the Scripture say? “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with the free woman’s son.”
GAL 4:30.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Inheritance] But what does the Scripture say? “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with the free woman’s son.”

GAL 4:31.text: Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.
GAL 4:31.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 4 · Children] Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.

GAL 5:1.text: It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.
GAL 5:1.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Body of Christ, Freedom] It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.

GAL 5:2.text: Take notice: I, Paul, tell you that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all.
GAL 5:2.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Take notice: I, Paul, tell you that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all.

GAL 5:3.text: Again I testify to every man who gets himself circumcised that he is obligated to obey the whole law.
GAL 5:3.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Covenant] Again I testify to every man who gets himself circumcised that he is obligated to obey the whole law.

GAL 5:4.text: You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.
GAL 5:4.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Covenant, Body of Christ] You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.

GAL 5:5.text: But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.
GAL 5:5.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Faith, Fruit of the Spirit] But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.

GAL 5:6.text: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value. All that matters is faith, expressed through love.
GAL 5:6.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Love, Faith] For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value. All that matters is faith, expressed through love.

GAL 5:7.text: You were running so well. Who has obstructed you from obeying the truth?
GAL 5:7.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5] You were running so well. Who has obstructed you from obeying the truth?

GAL 5:8.text: Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.
GAL 5:8.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5] Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.

GAL 5:9.text: A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.
GAL 5:9.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5] A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.

GAL 5:10.text: I am confident in the Lord that you will take no other view. The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
GAL 5:10.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Eschatology, Judgment] I am confident in the Lord that you will take no other view. The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.

GAL 5:11.text: Now, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the offense of the cross has been abolished.
GAL 5:11.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Cross] Now, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the offense of the cross has been abolished.

GAL 5:12.text: As for those who are agitating you, I wish they would proceed to emasculate themselves!
GAL 5:12.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5] As for those who are agitating you, I wish they would proceed to emasculate themselves!

GAL 5:13.text: For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh. Rather, serve one another in love.
GAL 5:13.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Love, Freedom] For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh. Rather, serve one another in love.

GAL 5:14.text: The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
GAL 5:14.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Covenant, Love] The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

GAL 5:15.text: But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another.
GAL 5:15.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5] But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another.

GAL 5:16.text: So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
GAL 5:16.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Fruit of the Spirit] So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.

GAL 5:17.text: For the flesh craves what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh. They are opposed to each other, so that you do not do what you want.
GAL 5:17.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Fruit of the Spirit] For the flesh craves what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh. They are opposed to each other, so that you do not do what you want.

GAL 5:18.text: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.
GAL 5:18.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Covenant, Fruit of the Spirit] But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.

GAL 5:19.text: The acts of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, and debauchery;
GAL 5:19.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5] The acts of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, and debauchery;

GAL 5:20.text: idolatry and sorcery; hatred, discord, jealousy, and rage; rivalries, divisions, factions,
GAL 5:20.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Idolatry, Jealousy] idolatry and sorcery; hatred, discord, jealousy, and rage; rivalries, divisions, factions,

GAL 5:21.text: and envy; drunkenness, orgies, and the like. I warn you, as I did before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
GAL 5:21.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · Jealousy, Kingdom of God] and envy; drunkenness, orgies, and the like. I warn you, as I did before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.

GAL 5:22.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
GAL 5:22.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · The Fruit of the Spirit] But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

GAL 5:23.text: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
GAL 5:23.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · The Fruit of the Spirit] gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

GAL 5:24.text: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
GAL 5:24.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · The Fruit of the Spirit] Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.

GAL 5:25.text: Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit.
GAL 5:25.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · The Fruit of the Spirit] Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit.

GAL 5:26.text: Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.
GAL 5:26.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 5 · The Fruit of the Spirit] Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.

GAL 6:1.text: Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.
GAL 6:1.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Fruit of the Spirit, Gentleness] Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.

GAL 6:2.text: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
GAL 6:2.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.

GAL 6:3.text: If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
GAL 6:3.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6] If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.

GAL 6:4.text: Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.
GAL 6:4.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6] Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.

GAL 6:5.text: For each one should carry his own load.
GAL 6:5.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6] For each one should carry his own load.

GAL 6:6.text: Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word must share in all good things with his instructor.
GAL 6:6.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6] Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word must share in all good things with his instructor.

GAL 6:7.text: Do not be deceived: God is not to be mocked. Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.
GAL 6:7.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6] Do not be deceived: God is not to be mocked. Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.

GAL 6:8.text: The one who sows to please his flesh, from the flesh will reap destruction; but the one who sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life.
GAL 6:8.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Devote To Destruction, Eternal Life] The one who sows to please his flesh, from the flesh will reap destruction; but the one who sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life.

GAL 6:9.text: Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
GAL 6:9.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6] Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.

GAL 6:10.text: Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to the family of faith.
GAL 6:10.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Faith, Family] Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to the family of faith.

GAL 6:11.text: See what large letters I am using to write to you with my own hand!
GAL 6:11.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6] See what large letters I am using to write to you with my own hand!

GAL 6:12.text: Those who want to make a good impression outwardly are trying to compel you to be circumcised. They only do this to avoid persecution for the cross of Christ.
GAL 6:12.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Body of Christ, Cross] Those who want to make a good impression outwardly are trying to compel you to be circumcised. They only do this to avoid persecution for the cross of Christ.

GAL 6:13.text: For the circumcised do not even keep the law themselves, yet they want you to be circumcised that they may boast in your flesh.
GAL 6:13.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6] For the circumcised do not even keep the law themselves, yet they want you to be circumcised that they may boast in your flesh.

GAL 6:14.text: But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
GAL 6:14.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Body of Christ, Cross] But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.

GAL 6:15.text: For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything. What counts is a new creation.
GAL 6:15.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Creation] For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything. What counts is a new creation.

GAL 6:16.text: Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule, even to the Israel of God.
GAL 6:16.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Forgiveness, Compassion] Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule, even to the Israel of God.

GAL 6:17.text: From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.
GAL 6:17.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Jesus Christ] From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.

GAL 6:18.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers.  Amen.
GAL 6:18.bm25Text: [Galatians · Chapter 6 · Body of Christ, Fruit of the Spirit] The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers.  Amen.
