HOS 2:1.text: “Say of your brothers, ‘My people,’ and of your sisters, ‘My loved one.’
HOS 2:1.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Love] “Say of your brothers, ‘My people,’ and of your sisters, ‘My loved one.’

HOS 2:2.text: Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, for she is not My wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove the adultery from her face and the unfaithfulness from between her breasts.
HOS 2:2.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Faith, Adultery] Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, for she is not My wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove the adultery from her face and the unfaithfulness from between her breasts.

HOS 2:3.text: Otherwise, I will strip her naked and expose her like the day of her birth. I will make her like a desert and turn her into a parched land, and I will let her die of thirst.
HOS 2:3.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] Otherwise, I will strip her naked and expose her like the day of her birth. I will make her like a desert and turn her into a parched land, and I will let her die of thirst.

HOS 2:4.text: I will have no compassion on her children, because they are the children of adultery.
HOS 2:4.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Adultery, Adultery In Heart] I will have no compassion on her children, because they are the children of adultery.

HOS 2:5.text: For their mother has played the harlot and has conceived them in disgrace. For she thought, ‘I will go after my lovers, who give me bread and water, wool and linen, oil and drink.’
HOS 2:5.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Love] For their mother has played the harlot and has conceived them in disgrace. For she thought, ‘I will go after my lovers, who give me bread and water, wool and linen, oil and drink.’

HOS 2:6.text: Therefore, behold, I will hedge up her path with thorns; I will enclose her with a wall, so she cannot find her way.
HOS 2:6.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] Therefore, behold, I will hedge up her path with thorns; I will enclose her with a wall, so she cannot find her way.

HOS 2:7.text: She will pursue her lovers but not catch them; she will seek them but not find them. Then she will say, ‘I will return to my first husband, for then I was better off than now.’
HOS 2:7.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Love] She will pursue her lovers but not catch them; she will seek them but not find them. Then she will say, ‘I will return to my first husband, for then I was better off than now.’

HOS 2:8.text: For she does not acknowledge that it was I who gave her grain, new wine, and oil, who lavished on her silver and gold— which they crafted for Baal.
HOS 2:8.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] For she does not acknowledge that it was I who gave her grain, new wine, and oil, who lavished on her silver and gold— which they crafted for Baal.

HOS 2:9.text: Therefore I will take back My grain in its time and My new wine in its season; I will take away My wool and linen, which were given to cover her nakedness.
HOS 2:9.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] Therefore I will take back My grain in its time and My new wine in its season; I will take away My wool and linen, which were given to cover her nakedness.

HOS 2:10.text: And then I will expose her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will deliver her out of My hands.
HOS 2:10.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Love] And then I will expose her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will deliver her out of My hands.

HOS 2:11.text: I will put an end to all her exultation: her feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths— all her appointed feasts.
HOS 2:11.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] I will put an end to all her exultation: her feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths— all her appointed feasts.

HOS 2:12.text: I will destroy her vines and fig trees, which she thinks are the wages paid by her lovers. So I will make them into a thicket, and the beasts of the field will devour them.
HOS 2:12.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Love, Destroy Canaan] I will destroy her vines and fig trees, which she thinks are the wages paid by her lovers. So I will make them into a thicket, and the beasts of the field will devour them.

HOS 2:13.text: I will punish her for the days of the Baals when she burned incense to them, when she decked herself with rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers.   But Me she forgot,” declares the LORD.
HOS 2:13.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Love] I will punish her for the days of the Baals when she burned incense to them, when she decked herself with rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers.   But Me she forgot,” declares the LORD.

HOS 2:14.text: “Therefore, behold, I will allure her and lead her to the wilderness, and speak to her tenderly.
HOS 2:14.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] “Therefore, behold, I will allure her and lead her to the wilderness, and speak to her tenderly.

HOS 2:15.text: There I will give back her vineyards and make the Valley of Achor into a gateway of hope. There she will respond as she did in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt.
HOS 2:15.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] There I will give back her vineyards and make the Valley of Achor into a gateway of hope. There she will respond as she did in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt.

HOS 2:16.text: In that day,” declares the LORD, “you will call Me ‘my Husband,’ and no longer call Me ‘my Master.’
HOS 2:16.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] In that day,” declares the LORD, “you will call Me ‘my Husband,’ and no longer call Me ‘my Master.’

HOS 2:17.text: For I will remove from her lips the names of the Baals; no longer will their names be invoked.
HOS 2:17.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] For I will remove from her lips the names of the Baals; no longer will their names be invoked.

HOS 2:18.text: On that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground. And I will abolish bow and sword and weapons of war in the land, and will make them lie down in safety.
HOS 2:18.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Covenant] On that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground. And I will abolish bow and sword and weapons of war in the land, and will make them lie down in safety.

HOS 2:19.text: So I will betroth you to Me forever; I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in loving devotion and compassion.
HOS 2:19.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Compassion, Devotion] So I will betroth you to Me forever; I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in loving devotion and compassion.

HOS 2:20.text: And I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.”
HOS 2:20.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Faith, Marital Faithfulness] And I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.”

HOS 2:21.text: “On that day I will respond—” declares the LORD— “I will respond to the heavens, and they will respond to the earth.
HOS 2:21.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] “On that day I will respond—” declares the LORD— “I will respond to the heavens, and they will respond to the earth.

HOS 2:22.text: And the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine and oil, and they will respond to Jezreel.
HOS 2:22.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2] And the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine and oil, and they will respond to Jezreel.

HOS 2:23.text: And I will sow her as My own in the land, and I will have compassion on ‘No Compassion.’ I will say to those called ‘Not My People,’ ‘You are My people,’ and they will say, ‘You are my God.’”
HOS 2:23.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 2 · Compassion] And I will sow her as My own in the land, and I will have compassion on ‘No Compassion.’ I will say to those called ‘Not My People,’ ‘You are My people,’ and they will say, ‘You are my God.’”

HOS 3:1.text: Then the LORD said to me, “Go show love to your wife again, though she is loved by another and is an adulteress. Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and offer raisin cakes to idols.”
HOS 3:1.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 3 · Love, Idolatry] Then the LORD said to me, “Go show love to your wife again, though she is loved by another and is an adulteress. Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and offer raisin cakes to idols.”

HOS 3:2.text: So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.
HOS 3:2.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 3] So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.

HOS 3:3.text: Then I said to her, “You must live with me for many days; you must not be promiscuous or belong to another, and I will do the same for you.”
HOS 3:3.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 3] Then I said to her, “You must live with me for many days; you must not be promiscuous or belong to another, and I will do the same for you.”

HOS 3:4.text: For the Israelites must live many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, and without ephod or idol.
HOS 3:4.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 3] For the Israelites must live many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, and without ephod or idol.

HOS 3:5.text: Afterward, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days.
HOS 3:5.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 3 · End Times, Israel] Afterward, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days.

HOS 4:1.text: Hear the word of the LORD, O children of Israel, for the LORD has a case against the people of the land:   “There is no truth, no loving devotion, and no knowledge of God in the land!
HOS 4:1.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Children, Devotion] Hear the word of the LORD, O children of Israel, for the LORD has a case against the people of the land:   “There is no truth, no loving devotion, and no knowledge of God in the land!

HOS 4:2.text: Cursing and lying, murder and stealing, and adultery are rampant; one act of bloodshed follows another.
HOS 4:2.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Adultery, Adultery In Heart] Cursing and lying, murder and stealing, and adultery are rampant; one act of bloodshed follows another.

HOS 4:3.text: Therefore the land mourns, and all who dwell in it will waste away with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air; even the fish of the sea disappear.
HOS 4:3.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4] Therefore the land mourns, and all who dwell in it will waste away with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air; even the fish of the sea disappear.

HOS 4:4.text: But let no man contend; let no man offer reproof; for your people are like those who contend with a priest.
HOS 4:4.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4] But let no man contend; let no man offer reproof; for your people are like those who contend with a priest.

HOS 4:5.text: You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night; so I will destroy your mother—
HOS 4:5.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night; so I will destroy your mother—

HOS 4:6.text: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you as My priests. Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I will also forget your children.
HOS 4:6.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Children] My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you as My priests. Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I will also forget your children.

HOS 4:7.text: The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against Me; they exchanged their Glory for a thing of disgrace.
HOS 4:7.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Glory] The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against Me; they exchanged their Glory for a thing of disgrace.

HOS 4:8.text: They feed on the sins of My people and set their hearts on iniquity.
HOS 4:8.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4] They feed on the sins of My people and set their hearts on iniquity.

HOS 4:9.text: And it shall be like people, like priest. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
HOS 4:9.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4] And it shall be like people, like priest. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.

HOS 4:10.text: They will eat but not be satisfied; they will be promiscuous but not multiply. For they have stopped obeying the LORD.
HOS 4:10.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4] They will eat but not be satisfied; they will be promiscuous but not multiply. For they have stopped obeying the LORD.

HOS 4:11.text: Promiscuity, wine, and new wine take away understanding.
HOS 4:11.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4] Promiscuity, wine, and new wine take away understanding.

HOS 4:12.text: My people consult their wooden idols, and their divining rods inform them. For a spirit of prostitution leads them astray and they have played the harlot against their God.
HOS 4:12.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Fruit of the Spirit, Idolatry] My people consult their wooden idols, and their divining rods inform them. For a spirit of prostitution leads them astray and they have played the harlot against their God.

HOS 4:13.text: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant. And so your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law to adultery.
HOS 4:13.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Adultery, Adultery In Heart] They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant. And so your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law to adultery.

HOS 4:14.text: I will not punish your daughters when they prostitute themselves, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery. For the men themselves go off with prostitutes and offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes. So a people without understanding will come to ruin.
HOS 4:14.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Adultery, Adultery In Heart] I will not punish your daughters when they prostitute themselves, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery. For the men themselves go off with prostitutes and offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes. So a people without understanding will come to ruin.

HOS 4:15.text: Though you prostitute yourself, O Israel, may Judah avoid such guilt! Do not journey to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear on oath, ‘As surely as the LORD lives!’
HOS 4:15.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Israel] Though you prostitute yourself, O Israel, may Judah avoid such guilt! Do not journey to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear on oath, ‘As surely as the LORD lives!’

HOS 4:16.text: For Israel is as obstinate as a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now shepherd them like lambs in an open meadow?
HOS 4:16.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Israel] For Israel is as obstinate as a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now shepherd them like lambs in an open meadow?

HOS 4:17.text: Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!
HOS 4:17.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Idolatry, Idols] Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!

HOS 4:18.text: When their liquor is gone, they turn to prostitution; their rulers dearly love disgrace.
HOS 4:18.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4 · Love] When their liquor is gone, they turn to prostitution; their rulers dearly love disgrace.

HOS 4:19.text: The whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.
HOS 4:19.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 4] The whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.

HOS 5:1.text: “Hear this, O priests! Take heed, O house of Israel! Give ear, O royal house! For this judgment is against you because you have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.
HOS 5:1.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5 · Israel, Judgment] “Hear this, O priests! Take heed, O house of Israel! Give ear, O royal house! For this judgment is against you because you have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.

HOS 5:2.text: The rebels are deep in slaughter; but I will chastise them all.
HOS 5:2.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5] The rebels are deep in slaughter; but I will chastise them all.

HOS 5:3.text: I know all about Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from Me. For now, O Ephraim, you have turned to prostitution; Israel is defiled.
HOS 5:3.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5 · About Forgiveness, Israel] I know all about Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from Me. For now, O Ephraim, you have turned to prostitution; Israel is defiled.

HOS 5:4.text: Their deeds do not permit them to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.
HOS 5:4.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5 · Fruit of the Spirit] Their deeds do not permit them to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.

HOS 5:5.text: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their iniquity; even Judah stumbles with them.
HOS 5:5.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5 · Israel] Israel’s arrogance testifies against them; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their iniquity; even Judah stumbles with them.

HOS 5:6.text: They go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, but they do not find Him; He has withdrawn Himself from them.
HOS 5:6.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5] They go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, but they do not find Him; He has withdrawn Himself from them.

HOS 5:7.text: They have been unfaithful to the LORD; for they have borne illegitimate children. Now the New Moon will devour them along with their land.
HOS 5:7.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5 · Faith, Children] They have been unfaithful to the LORD; for they have borne illegitimate children. Now the New Moon will devour them along with their land.

HOS 5:8.text: Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah; raise the battle cry in Beth-aven: Lead on, O Benjamin!
HOS 5:8.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5] Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah; raise the battle cry in Beth-aven: Lead on, O Benjamin!

HOS 5:9.text: Ephraim will be laid waste on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I proclaim what is certain.
HOS 5:9.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5 · Israel] Ephraim will be laid waste on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I proclaim what is certain.

HOS 5:10.text: The princes of Judah are like those who move boundary stones; I will pour out My fury upon them like water.
HOS 5:10.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5] The princes of Judah are like those who move boundary stones; I will pour out My fury upon them like water.

HOS 5:11.text: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, for he is determined to follow worthless idols.
HOS 5:11.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5 · Idolatry, Idols] Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, for he is determined to follow worthless idols.

HOS 5:12.text: So I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like decay to the house of Judah.
HOS 5:12.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5] So I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like decay to the house of Judah.

HOS 5:13.text: When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, then Ephraim turned to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he cannot cure you or heal your wound.
HOS 5:13.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5] When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, then Ephraim turned to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he cannot cure you or heal your wound.

HOS 5:14.text: For I am like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, even I, will tear them to pieces and then go away. I will carry them off where no one can rescue them.
HOS 5:14.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5] For I am like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, even I, will tear them to pieces and then go away. I will carry them off where no one can rescue them.

HOS 5:15.text: Then I will return to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face; in their affliction they will earnestly seek Me.”
HOS 5:15.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 5] Then I will return to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face; in their affliction they will earnestly seek Me.”

HOS 6:1.text: Come, let us return to the LORD.   For He has torn us to pieces, but He will heal us; He has wounded us, but He will bind up our wounds.
HOS 6:1.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6] Come, let us return to the LORD.   For He has torn us to pieces, but He will heal us; He has wounded us, but He will bind up our wounds.

HOS 6:2.text: After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up, that we may live in His presence.
HOS 6:2.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6] After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up, that we may live in His presence.

HOS 6:3.text: So let us know— let us press on to know the LORD. As surely as the sun rises, He will appear; He will come to us like the rain, like the spring showers that water the earth.
HOS 6:3.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6] So let us know— let us press on to know the LORD. As surely as the sun rises, He will appear; He will come to us like the rain, like the spring showers that water the earth.

HOS 6:4.text: What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah? For your loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes.
HOS 6:4.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6] What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah? For your loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes.

HOS 6:5.text: Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of My mouth, and My judgments go forth like lightning.
HOS 6:5.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6] Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of My mouth, and My judgments go forth like lightning.

HOS 6:6.text: For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
HOS 6:6.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6 · Forgiveness, Compassion] For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.

HOS 6:7.text: But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they were unfaithful to Me.
HOS 6:7.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6 · Faith, Covenant] But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they were unfaithful to Me.

HOS 6:8.text: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with footprints of blood.
HOS 6:8.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6] Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with footprints of blood.

HOS 6:9.text: Like raiders who lie in ambush, so does a band of priests; they murder on the way to Shechem; surely they have committed atrocities.
HOS 6:9.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6] Like raiders who lie in ambush, so does a band of priests; they murder on the way to Shechem; surely they have committed atrocities.

HOS 6:10.text: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: Ephraim practices prostitution there, and Israel is defiled.
HOS 6:10.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6 · Israel] In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: Ephraim practices prostitution there, and Israel is defiled.

HOS 6:11.text: Also for you, O Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore My people from captivity.
HOS 6:11.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 6] Also for you, O Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore My people from captivity.

HOS 7:1.text: When I heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim will be exposed, as well as the crimes of Samaria. For they practice deceit and thieves break in; bandits raid in the streets.
HOS 7:1.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7 · Deceit, Israel] When I heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim will be exposed, as well as the crimes of Samaria. For they practice deceit and thieves break in; bandits raid in the streets.

HOS 7:2.text: But they fail to consider in their hearts that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds are all around them; they are before My face.
HOS 7:2.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7] But they fail to consider in their hearts that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds are all around them; they are before My face.

HOS 7:3.text: They delight the king with their evil, and the princes with their lies.
HOS 7:3.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7] They delight the king with their evil, and the princes with their lies.

HOS 7:4.text: They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker who needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough.
HOS 7:4.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7] They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker who needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough.

HOS 7:5.text: The princes are inflamed with wine on the day of our king; so he joins hands with those who mock him.
HOS 7:5.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7] The princes are inflamed with wine on the day of our king; so he joins hands with those who mock him.

HOS 7:6.text: For they prepare their heart like an oven while they lie in wait; all night their anger smolders; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
HOS 7:6.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7 · Adultery In Heart] For they prepare their heart like an oven while they lie in wait; all night their anger smolders; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.

HOS 7:7.text: All of them are hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings fall; not one of them calls upon Me.
HOS 7:7.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7] All of them are hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings fall; not one of them calls upon Me.

HOS 7:8.text: Ephraim mixes with the nations; Ephraim is an unturned cake.
HOS 7:8.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7] Ephraim mixes with the nations; Ephraim is an unturned cake.

HOS 7:9.text: Foreigners consume his strength, but he does not notice. Even his hair is streaked with gray, but he does not know.
HOS 7:9.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7] Foreigners consume his strength, but he does not notice. Even his hair is streaked with gray, but he does not know.

HOS 7:10.text: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them, yet they do not return to the LORD their God; despite all this, they do not seek Him.
HOS 7:10.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7 · Israel] Israel’s arrogance testifies against them, yet they do not return to the LORD their God; despite all this, they do not seek Him.

HOS 7:11.text: So Ephraim has become like a silly, senseless dove— calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.
HOS 7:11.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 7 · Calling] So Ephraim has become like a silly, senseless dove— calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.

HOS 7:12.text: As they go, I will spread My net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the air. I will chastise them when I hear them flocking together.

HOS 8:10.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 8] Though they hire allies among the nations, I will now round them up, and they will begin to diminish under the oppression of the king of princes.

HOS 9:13.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 9 · Children] I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a meadow. But Ephraim will bring out his children for slaughter.

HOS 9:14.bm25Text: [Hosea · Chapter 9] Give them, O LORD— what will You give? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that dry up!

JAS 3:12.text: My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.
JAS 3:12.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 3 · Taming the Tongue] My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.

JAS 3:13.text: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show it by his good conduct, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.
JAS 3:13.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 3 · Humility] Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show it by his good conduct, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.

JAS 3:14.text: But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.
JAS 3:14.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 3 · Jealousy] But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.

JAS 3:15.text: Such wisdom does not come from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.
JAS 3:15.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 3] Such wisdom does not come from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.

JAS 3:16.text: For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice.
JAS 3:16.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 3 · Jealousy] For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice.

JAS 3:17.text: But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.
JAS 3:17.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 3 · Forgiveness, Compassion] But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.

JAS 3:18.text: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness.
JAS 3:18.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 3 · Fruit of the Spirit] Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness.

JAS 4:1.text: What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?
JAS 4:1.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?

JAS 4:2.text: You crave what you do not have; you kill and covet, but are unable to obtain it. You quarrel and fight. You do not have, because you do not ask.
JAS 4:2.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] You crave what you do not have; you kill and covet, but are unable to obtain it. You quarrel and fight. You do not have, because you do not ask.

JAS 4:3.text: And when you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures.
JAS 4:3.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] And when you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures.

JAS 4:4.text: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore, whoever chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God.
JAS 4:4.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4 · Friendship] You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore, whoever chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God.

JAS 4:5.text: Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?
JAS 4:5.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4 · Fruit of the Spirit, Jealousy] Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?

JAS 4:6.text: But He gives us more grace. This is why it says:  “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
JAS 4:6.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4 · Grace] But He gives us more grace. This is why it says:  “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

JAS 4:7.text: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
JAS 4:7.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

JAS 4:8.text: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
JAS 4:8.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.

JAS 4:9.text: Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom.
JAS 4:9.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom.

JAS 4:10.text: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.
JAS 4:10.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.

JAS 4:11.text: Brothers, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law and judges it. And if you judge the law, you are not a practitioner of the law, but a judge of it.
JAS 4:11.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] Brothers, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law and judges it. And if you judge the law, you are not a practitioner of the law, but a judge of it.

JAS 4:12.text: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?
JAS 4:12.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?

JAS 4:13.text: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business, and make a profit.”
JAS 4:13.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business, and make a profit.”

JAS 4:14.text: You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
JAS 4:14.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.

JAS 4:15.text: Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”
JAS 4:15.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”

JAS 4:16.text: As it is, you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.
JAS 4:16.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] As it is, you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.

JAS 4:17.text: Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do, yet fails to do it, is guilty of sin.
JAS 4:17.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 4] Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do, yet fails to do it, is guilty of sin.

JAS 5:1.text: Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.
JAS 5:1.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.

JAS 5:2.text: Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.
JAS 5:2.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.

JAS 5:3.text: Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire.  You have hoarded treasure in the last days.
JAS 5:3.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5 · End Times] Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire.  You have hoarded treasure in the last days.

JAS 5:4.text: Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.
JAS 5:4.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.

JAS 5:5.text: You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.
JAS 5:5.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.

JAS 5:6.text: You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you.
JAS 5:6.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you.

JAS 5:7.text: Be patient, then, brothers, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the soil—how patient he is for the fall and spring rains.
JAS 5:7.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5 · Fruit of the Spirit] Be patient, then, brothers, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the soil—how patient he is for the fall and spring rains.

JAS 5:8.text: You, too, be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.
JAS 5:8.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] You, too, be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.

JAS 5:9.text: Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!
JAS 5:9.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5 · About Forgiveness] Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!

JAS 5:10.text: Brothers, as an example of patience in affliction, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
JAS 5:10.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] Brothers, as an example of patience in affliction, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

JAS 5:11.text: See how blessed we consider those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen the outcome from the Lord. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
JAS 5:11.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5 · Forgiveness, Compassion] See how blessed we consider those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen the outcome from the Lord. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

JAS 5:12.text: Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven or earth or by any other oath. Simply let your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no, so that you will not fall under judgment.
JAS 5:12.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5 · Heaven, Judgment] Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven or earth or by any other oath. Simply let your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no, so that you will not fall under judgment.

JAS 5:13.text: Is any one of you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.
JAS 5:13.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] Is any one of you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.

JAS 5:14.text: Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
JAS 5:14.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5 · Church, Leadership] Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.

JAS 5:15.text: And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.
JAS 5:15.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5 · Forgiveness, Faith] And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.

JAS 5:16.text: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.
JAS 5:16.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.

JAS 5:17.text: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.
JAS 5:17.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.

JAS 5:18.text: Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops.
JAS 5:18.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops.

JAS 5:19.text: My brothers, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring him back,
JAS 5:19.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5] My brothers, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring him back,

JAS 5:20.text: consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.
JAS 5:20.bm25Text: [James · Chapter 5 · Death] consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.

JDG 1:1.text: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites inquired of the LORD, “Who will be the first to go up and fight for us against the Canaanites?”
JDG 1:1.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Death, Destroy Canaanites] After the death of Joshua, the Israelites inquired of the LORD, “Who will be the first to go up and fight for us against the Canaanites?”

JDG 1:2.text: “Judah shall go up,” answered the LORD. “Indeed, I have delivered the land into their hands.”
JDG 1:2.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] “Judah shall go up,” answered the LORD. “Indeed, I have delivered the land into their hands.”

JDG 1:3.text: Then the men of Judah said to their brothers the Simeonites, “Come up with us to our allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites. And we likewise will go with you to your territory.” So the Simeonites went with them.
JDG 1:3.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] Then the men of Judah said to their brothers the Simeonites, “Come up with us to our allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites. And we likewise will go with you to your territory.” So the Simeonites went with them.

JDG 1:4.text: When Judah attacked, the LORD delivered the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands, and they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.
JDG 1:4.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] When Judah attacked, the LORD delivered the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands, and they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.

JDG 1:5.text: And there they found Adoni-bezek and fought against him, striking down the Canaanites and Perizzites.
JDG 1:5.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] And there they found Adoni-bezek and fought against him, striking down the Canaanites and Perizzites.

JDG 1:6.text: As Adoni-bezek fled, they pursued him, seized him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.
JDG 1:6.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] As Adoni-bezek fled, they pursued him, seized him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.

JDG 1:7.text: Then Adoni-bezek said, “Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off have gathered the scraps under my table. As I have done to them, so God has repaid me.” And they brought him to Jerusalem, where he died.
JDG 1:7.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] Then Adoni-bezek said, “Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off have gathered the scraps under my table. As I have done to them, so God has repaid me.” And they brought him to Jerusalem, where he died.

JDG 1:8.text: Then the men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put the city to the sword and set it on fire.
JDG 1:8.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] Then the men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put the city to the sword and set it on fire.

JDG 1:9.text: Afterward, the men of Judah marched down to fight against the Canaanites living in the hill country, in the Negev, and in the foothills.
JDG 1:9.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] Afterward, the men of Judah marched down to fight against the Canaanites living in the hill country, in the Negev, and in the foothills.

JDG 1:10.text: Judah also marched against the Canaanites who were living in Hebron (formerly known as Kiriath-arba), and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
JDG 1:10.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] Judah also marched against the Canaanites who were living in Hebron (formerly known as Kiriath-arba), and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

JDG 1:11.text: From there they marched against the inhabitants of Debir (formerly known as Kiriath-sepher).
JDG 1:11.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] From there they marched against the inhabitants of Debir (formerly known as Kiriath-sepher).

JDG 1:12.text: And Caleb said, “To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.”
JDG 1:12.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Marriage] And Caleb said, “To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.”

JDG 1:13.text: So Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz captured the city, and Caleb gave his daughter Acsah to him in marriage.
JDG 1:13.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Marriage] So Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz captured the city, and Caleb gave his daughter Acsah to him in marriage.

JDG 1:14.text: One day Acsah came to Othniel and urged him to ask her father for a field. When she got off her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What do you desire?”
JDG 1:14.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · God the Father, Lust] One day Acsah came to Othniel and urged him to ask her father for a field. When she got off her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What do you desire?”

JDG 1:15.text: “Give me a blessing,” she answered. “Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well.”  So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs.
JDG 1:15.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Blessing] “Give me a blessing,” she answered. “Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well.”  So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs.

JDG 1:16.text: Now the descendants of Moses’ father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the men of Judah from the City of Palms to the Wilderness of Judah in the Negev near Arad. They went to live among the people.
JDG 1:16.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · God the Father] Now the descendants of Moses’ father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the men of Judah from the City of Palms to the Wilderness of Judah in the Negev near Arad. They went to live among the people.

JDG 1:17.text: Then the men of Judah went with their brothers the Simeonites, attacked the Canaanites living in Zephath, and devoted the city to destruction. So it was called Hormah.
JDG 1:17.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] Then the men of Judah went with their brothers the Simeonites, attacked the Canaanites living in Zephath, and devoted the city to destruction. So it was called Hormah.

JDG 1:18.text: And Judah also captured Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron—each with its territory.
JDG 1:18.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] And Judah also captured Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron—each with its territory.

JDG 1:19.text: The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country; but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plains because they had chariots of iron.
JDG 1:19.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country; but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plains because they had chariots of iron.

JDG 1:20.text: Just as Moses had promised, Judah gave Hebron to Caleb, who drove out the descendants of the three sons of Anak.
JDG 1:20.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] Just as Moses had promised, Judah gave Hebron to Caleb, who drove out the descendants of the three sons of Anak.

JDG 1:21.text: The Benjamites, however, failed to drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So to this day the Jebusites live there among the Benjamites.
JDG 1:21.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] The Benjamites, however, failed to drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So to this day the Jebusites live there among the Benjamites.

JDG 1:22.text: The house of Joseph also attacked Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
JDG 1:22.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] The house of Joseph also attacked Bethel, and the LORD was with them.

JDG 1:23.text: They sent spies to Bethel (formerly known as Luz),
JDG 1:23.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] They sent spies to Bethel (formerly known as Luz),

JDG 1:24.text: and when the spies saw a man coming out of the city, they said to him, “Please show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you kindly.”
JDG 1:24.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] and when the spies saw a man coming out of the city, they said to him, “Please show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you kindly.”

JDG 1:25.text: So the man showed them the entrance to the city, and they put the city to the sword but released that man and all his family.
JDG 1:25.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Family] So the man showed them the entrance to the city, and they put the city to the sword but released that man and all his family.

JDG 1:26.text: And the man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called it Luz, which is its name to this day.
JDG 1:26.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] And the man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called it Luz, which is its name to this day.

JDG 1:27.text: At that time Manasseh failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and their villages; for the Canaanites were determined to dwell in that land.
JDG 1:27.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] At that time Manasseh failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and their villages; for the Canaanites were determined to dwell in that land.

JDG 1:28.text: When Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.
JDG 1:28.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] When Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.

JDG 1:29.text: Ephraim also failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer; so the Canaanites continued to dwell among them in Gezer.
JDG 1:29.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] Ephraim also failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer; so the Canaanites continued to dwell among them in Gezer.

JDG 1:30.text: Zebulun failed to drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol; so the Canaanites lived among them and served as forced laborers.
JDG 1:30.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Destroy Canaanites, Destroy The Canaanites] Zebulun failed to drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol; so the Canaanites lived among them and served as forced laborers.

JDG 1:31.text: Asher failed to drive out the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob.
JDG 1:31.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] Asher failed to drive out the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob.

JDG 1:32.text: So the Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.
JDG 1:32.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Canaanite, Canaanite Conquest] So the Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.

JDG 1:33.text: Naphtali failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath. So the Naphtalites also lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath served them as forced laborers.
JDG 1:33.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1 · Canaanite, Canaanite Conquest] Naphtali failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath. So the Naphtalites also lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath served them as forced laborers.

JDG 1:34.text: The Amorites forced the Danites into the hill country and did not allow them to come down into the plain.
JDG 1:34.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] The Amorites forced the Danites into the hill country and did not allow them to come down into the plain.

JDG 1:35.text: And the Amorites were determined to dwell in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when the house of Joseph grew in strength, they pressed the Amorites into forced labor.
JDG 1:35.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] And the Amorites were determined to dwell in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when the house of Joseph grew in strength, they pressed the Amorites into forced labor.

JDG 1:36.text: And the border of the Amorites extended from the Ascent of Akrabbim to Sela and beyond.
JDG 1:36.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 1] And the border of the Amorites extended from the Ascent of Akrabbim to Sela and beyond.

JDG 2:1.text: Now the angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, “I brought you up out of Egypt and led you into the land that I had promised to your fathers, and I said, ‘I will never break My covenant with you,

JDG 2:2.text: and you are not to make a covenant with the people of this land, but you shall tear down their altars.’  Yet you have not obeyed My voice. What is this you have done?
JDG 2:2.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 2 · Covenant] and you are not to make a covenant with the people of this land, but you shall tear down their altars.’  Yet you have not obeyed My voice. What is this you have done?

JDG 2:3.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 2] So now I tell you that I will not drive out these people before you; they will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you.”

JDG 2:4.text: When the angel of the LORD had spoken these words to all the Israelites, the people lifted up their voices and wept.
JDG 2:4.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 2] When the angel of the LORD had spoken these words to all the Israelites, the people lifted up their voices and wept.

JDG 2:5.text: So they called that place Bochim and offered sacrifices there to the LORD.
JDG 2:5.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 2] So they called that place Bochim and offered sacrifices there to the LORD.

JDG 2:6.text: After Joshua had dismissed the people, the Israelites went out to take possession of the land, each to his own inheritance.
JDG 2:6.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 2 · Inheritance] After Joshua had dismissed the people, the Israelites went out to take possession of the land, each to his own inheritance.

JDG 2:7.text: And the people served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him, who had seen all the great works that the LORD had done for Israel.
JDG 2:7.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 2 · Israel, Leadership] And the people served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him, who had seen all the great works that the LORD had done for Israel.

JDG 6:9.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] I delivered you out of the hands of Egypt and all your oppressors. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.

JDG 6:12.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] And the angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon and said, “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.”

JDG 6:13.text: “Please, my Lord,” Gideon replied, “if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? And where are all His wonders of which our fathers told us, saying, ‘Has not the LORD brought us up out of Egypt?’ But now the LORD has forsaken us and delivered us into the hand of Midian.”

JDG 6:14.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6 · Israel] The LORD turned to him and said, “Go in the strength you have and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not sending you?”

JDG 6:16.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] “Surely I will be with you,” the LORD replied, “and you will strike down all the Midianites as one man.”

JDG 6:17.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6 · Blessing] Gideon answered, “If I have found favor in Your sight, give me a sign that it is You speaking with me.

JDG 6:18.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] Please do not depart from this place until I return to You. Let me bring my offering and set it before You.”  And the LORD said, “I will stay until you return.”

JDG 6:20.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] And the angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened bread, lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” And Gideon did so.

JDG 6:23.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] But the LORD said to him, “Peace be with you. Do not be afraid, for you will not die.”

JDG 6:26.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] Then build a proper altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold. And with the wood of the Asherah pole you cut down, take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering.”

JDG 6:29.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] “Who did this?” they said to one another.  And after they had investigated thoroughly, they were told, “Gideon son of Joash did it.”

JDG 6:30.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] Then the men of the city said to Joash, “Bring out your son. He must die, because he has torn down Baal’s altar and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.”

JDG 6:31.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6 · Death] But Joash said to all who stood against him, “Are you contending for Baal? Are you trying to save him? Whoever pleads his case will be put to death by morning! If Baal is a god, let him contend for himself with the one who has torn down his altar.”

JDG 6:33.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 6] Then all the Midianites, Amalekites, and other people of the east gathered together, crossed over the Jordan, and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.
