JDG 7:18.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 7] When I and all who are with me blow our horns, then you are also to blow your horns from all around the camp and shout, ‘For the LORD and for Gideon!’”

JDG 7:19.text: Gideon and the hundred men with him reached the outskirts of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the changing of the guard. They blew their horns and broke the jars that were in their hands.
JDG 7:19.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 7] Gideon and the hundred men with him reached the outskirts of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the changing of the guard. They blew their horns and broke the jars that were in their hands.

JDG 7:20.text: The three companies blew their horns and shattered their jars. Holding the torches in their left hands and the horns in their right hands, they shouted, “A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!”
JDG 7:20.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 7] The three companies blew their horns and shattered their jars. Holding the torches in their left hands and the horns in their right hands, they shouted, “A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!”

JDG 7:21.text: Each Israelite took his position around the camp, and the entire Midianite army fled, crying out as they ran.
JDG 7:21.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 7] Each Israelite took his position around the camp, and the entire Midianite army fled, crying out as they ran.

JDG 7:22.text: And when the three hundred rams’ horns sounded, the LORD set all the men in the camp against one another with their swords. The army fled to Beth-shittah toward Zererah as far as the border of Abel-meholah near Tabbath.
JDG 7:22.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 7] And when the three hundred rams’ horns sounded, the LORD set all the men in the camp against one another with their swords. The army fled to Beth-shittah toward Zererah as far as the border of Abel-meholah near Tabbath.

JDG 7:23.text: Then the men of Israel were called out from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh, and they pursued the Midianites.
JDG 7:23.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 7 · Israel] Then the men of Israel were called out from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh, and they pursued the Midianites.

JDG 7:24.text: Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim to say, “Come down against the Midianites and seize the waters of the Jordan ahead of them as far as Beth-barah.” So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they captured the waters of the Jordan as far as Beth-barah.
JDG 7:24.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 7 · Angels] Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim to say, “Come down against the Midianites and seize the waters of the Jordan ahead of them as far as Beth-barah.” So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they captured the waters of the Jordan as far as Beth-barah.

JDG 7:25.text: They also captured Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian; and they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. So they pursued the Midianites and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.
JDG 7:25.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 7] They also captured Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian; and they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. So they pursued the Midianites and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.

JDG 8:1.text: Then the men of Ephraim said to Gideon, “Why have you done this to us? Why did you fail to call us when you went to fight against Midian?” And they contended with him violently.
JDG 8:1.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] Then the men of Ephraim said to Gideon, “Why have you done this to us? Why did you fail to call us when you went to fight against Midian?” And they contended with him violently.

JDG 8:2.text: But Gideon answered them, “Now what have I accomplished compared to you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?
JDG 8:2.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] But Gideon answered them, “Now what have I accomplished compared to you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?

JDG 8:3.text: God has delivered Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, into your hand. What was I able to do compared to you?” When he had said this, their anger against him subsided.
JDG 8:3.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] God has delivered Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, into your hand. What was I able to do compared to you?” When he had said this, their anger against him subsided.

JDG 8:4.text: Then Gideon and his three hundred men came to the Jordan and crossed it, exhausted yet still in pursuit.
JDG 8:4.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] Then Gideon and his three hundred men came to the Jordan and crossed it, exhausted yet still in pursuit.

JDG 8:5.text: So Gideon said to the men of Succoth, “Please give my troops some bread, for they are exhausted, and I am still pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
JDG 8:5.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] So Gideon said to the men of Succoth, “Please give my troops some bread, for they are exhausted, and I am still pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”

JDG 8:6.text: But the leaders of Succoth asked, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?”
JDG 8:6.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] But the leaders of Succoth asked, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?”

JDG 8:7.text: “Very well,” Gideon replied, “when the LORD has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness!”
JDG 8:7.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] “Very well,” Gideon replied, “when the LORD has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness!”

JDG 8:8.text: From there he went up to Penuel and asked the same from them, but the men of Penuel gave the same response as the men of Succoth.
JDG 8:8.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] From there he went up to Penuel and asked the same from them, but the men of Penuel gave the same response as the men of Succoth.

JDG 8:9.text: So Gideon told the men of Penuel, “When I return in triumph, I will tear down this tower!”
JDG 8:9.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] So Gideon told the men of Penuel, “When I return in triumph, I will tear down this tower!”

JDG 8:10.text: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their army of about fifteen thousand men—all that were left of the armies of the people of the east. A hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen.
JDG 8:10.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8 · About Forgiveness] Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their army of about fifteen thousand men—all that were left of the armies of the people of the east. A hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen.

JDG 8:11.text: And Gideon went up by way of the caravan route east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he attacked their army, taking them by surprise.
JDG 8:11.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] And Gideon went up by way of the caravan route east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he attacked their army, taking them by surprise.

JDG 8:12.text: When Zebah and Zalmunna fled, Gideon pursued and captured these two kings of Midian, routing their entire army.
JDG 8:12.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] When Zebah and Zalmunna fled, Gideon pursued and captured these two kings of Midian, routing their entire army.

JDG 8:13.text: After this, Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle along the Ascent of Heres.
JDG 8:13.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] After this, Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle along the Ascent of Heres.

JDG 8:14.text: There he captured a young man of Succoth and interrogated him. The young man wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven leaders and elders of Succoth.
JDG 8:14.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8 · Leadership] There he captured a young man of Succoth and interrogated him. The young man wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven leaders and elders of Succoth.

JDG 8:15.text: And Gideon went to the men of Succoth and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your weary men?’”
JDG 8:15.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8 · About Forgiveness] And Gideon went to the men of Succoth and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your weary men?’”

JDG 8:16.text: Then he took the elders of the city, and using the thorns and briers of the wilderness, he disciplined the men of Succoth.
JDG 8:16.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8 · Leadership] Then he took the elders of the city, and using the thorns and briers of the wilderness, he disciplined the men of Succoth.

JDG 8:17.text: He also pulled down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
JDG 8:17.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] He also pulled down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.

JDG 8:18.text: Next, Gideon asked Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?”  “Men like you,” they answered, “each one resembling the son of a king.”
JDG 8:18.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] Next, Gideon asked Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?”  “Men like you,” they answered, “each one resembling the son of a king.”

JDG 8:19.text: “They were my brothers,” Gideon replied, “the sons of my mother! As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”
JDG 8:19.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] “They were my brothers,” Gideon replied, “the sons of my mother! As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”

JDG 8:20.text: So he said to Jether, his firstborn, “Get up and kill them.” But the young man did not draw his sword; he was fearful because he was still a youth.
JDG 8:20.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] So he said to Jether, his firstborn, “Get up and kill them.” But the young man did not draw his sword; he was fearful because he was still a youth.

JDG 8:21.text: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, “Get up and kill us yourself, for as the man is, so is his strength.” So Gideon got up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments from the necks of their camels.
JDG 8:21.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, “Get up and kill us yourself, for as the man is, so is his strength.” So Gideon got up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments from the necks of their camels.

JDG 8:22.text: Then the Israelites said to Gideon, “Rule over us—you and your son and grandson—for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.”
JDG 8:22.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] Then the Israelites said to Gideon, “Rule over us—you and your son and grandson—for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.”

JDG 8:23.text: But Gideon replied, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son. The LORD shall rule over you.”
JDG 8:23.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] But Gideon replied, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son. The LORD shall rule over you.”

JDG 8:24.text: Then he added, “Let me make a request of you, that each of you give me an earring from his plunder.” (For the enemies had gold earrings because they were Ishmaelites.)
JDG 8:24.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] Then he added, “Let me make a request of you, that each of you give me an earring from his plunder.” (For the enemies had gold earrings because they were Ishmaelites.)

JDG 8:25.text: “We will give them gladly,” they replied.  So they spread out a garment, and each man threw an earring from his plunder onto it.
JDG 8:25.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] “We will give them gladly,” they replied.  So they spread out a garment, and each man threw an earring from his plunder onto it.

JDG 8:26.text: The weight of the gold earrings he had requested was 1,700 shekels, in addition to the crescent ornaments, the pendants, the purple garments of the kings of Midian, and the chains from the necks of their camels.
JDG 8:26.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] The weight of the gold earrings he had requested was 1,700 shekels, in addition to the crescent ornaments, the pendants, the purple garments of the kings of Midian, and the chains from the necks of their camels.

JDG 8:27.text: From all this Gideon made an ephod, which he placed in Ophrah, his hometown. But soon all Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household.
JDG 8:27.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8 · Family, Israel] From all this Gideon made an ephod, which he placed in Ophrah, his hometown. But soon all Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household.

JDG 8:28.text: In this way Midian was subdued before the Israelites and did not raise its head again. So the land had rest for forty years in the days of Gideon,
JDG 8:28.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] In this way Midian was subdued before the Israelites and did not raise its head again. So the land had rest for forty years in the days of Gideon,

JDG 8:29.text: and he—Jerubbaal son of Joash—returned home and settled down.
JDG 8:29.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] and he—Jerubbaal son of Joash—returned home and settled down.

JDG 8:30.text: Gideon had seventy sons of his own, since he had many wives.
JDG 8:30.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] Gideon had seventy sons of his own, since he had many wives.

JDG 8:31.text: His concubine, who dwelt in Shechem, also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
JDG 8:31.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] His concubine, who dwelt in Shechem, also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.

JDG 8:32.text: Later, Gideon son of Joash died at a ripe old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
JDG 8:32.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8 · God the Father] Later, Gideon son of Joash died at a ripe old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

JDG 8:33.text: And as soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned and prostituted themselves with the Baals, and they set up Baal-berith as their god.
JDG 8:33.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] And as soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned and prostituted themselves with the Baals, and they set up Baal-berith as their god.

JDG 8:34.text: The Israelites failed to remember the LORD their God who had delivered them from the hands of all their enemies on every side.
JDG 8:34.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8] The Israelites failed to remember the LORD their God who had delivered them from the hands of all their enemies on every side.

JDG 8:35.text: They did not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) for all the good things he had done for Israel.
JDG 8:35.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 8 · Grace, Israel] They did not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) for all the good things he had done for Israel.

JDG 9:1.text: Now Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to his mother’s brothers at Shechem and said to them and to all the clan of his mother,
JDG 9:1.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] Now Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to his mother’s brothers at Shechem and said to them and to all the clan of his mother,

JDG 9:2.text: “Please ask all the leaders of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.”
JDG 9:2.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] “Please ask all the leaders of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.”

JDG 9:3.text: And when his mother’s brothers spoke all these words about him in the presence of all the leaders of Shechem, their hearts were inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, “He is our brother.”
JDG 9:3.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · About Forgiveness] And when his mother’s brothers spoke all these words about him in the presence of all the leaders of Shechem, their hearts were inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, “He is our brother.”

JDG 9:4.text: So they gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, with which Abimelech hired some worthless and reckless men to follow him.
JDG 9:4.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] So they gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, with which Abimelech hired some worthless and reckless men to follow him.

JDG 9:5.text: He went to his father’s house in Ophrah, and on one stone murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, survived, because he hid himself.
JDG 9:5.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · God the Father] He went to his father’s house in Ophrah, and on one stone murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, survived, because he hid himself.

JDG 9:6.text: Then all the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo gathered beside the oak at the pillar in Shechem and proceeded to make Abimelech their king.
JDG 9:6.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] Then all the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo gathered beside the oak at the pillar in Shechem and proceeded to make Abimelech their king.

JDG 9:7.text: When this was reported to Jotham, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim, raised his voice, and cried out:  “Listen to me, O leaders of Shechem, and may God listen to you.
JDG 9:7.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] When this was reported to Jotham, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim, raised his voice, and cried out:  “Listen to me, O leaders of Shechem, and may God listen to you.

JDG 9:8.text: One day the trees set out to anoint a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’
JDG 9:8.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] One day the trees set out to anoint a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’

JDG 9:9.text: But the olive tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my oil that honors both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’
JDG 9:9.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Generosity] But the olive tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my oil that honors both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’

JDG 9:10.text: Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’
JDG 9:10.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’

JDG 9:11.text: But the fig tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my sweetness and my good fruit, to hold sway over the trees?’
JDG 9:11.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Fruit of the Spirit, Generosity] But the fig tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my sweetness and my good fruit, to hold sway over the trees?’

JDG 9:12.text: Then the trees said to the grapevine, ‘Come and reign over us.’
JDG 9:12.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] Then the trees said to the grapevine, ‘Come and reign over us.’

JDG 9:13.text: But the grapevine replied, ‘Should I stop giving my wine that cheers both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’
JDG 9:13.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Generosity] But the grapevine replied, ‘Should I stop giving my wine that cheers both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’

JDG 9:14.text: Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘Come and reign over us.’
JDG 9:14.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘Come and reign over us.’

JDG 9:15.text: But the thornbush replied, ‘If you really are anointing me as king over you, come and find refuge in my shade. But if not, may fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.’
JDG 9:15.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Anointing] But the thornbush replied, ‘If you really are anointing me as king over you, come and find refuge in my shade. But if not, may fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.’

JDG 9:16.text: Now if you have acted faithfully and honestly in making Abimelech king, if you have done well by Jerubbaal and his family, and if you have done to him as he deserves—
JDG 9:16.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Faith, Family] Now if you have acted faithfully and honestly in making Abimelech king, if you have done well by Jerubbaal and his family, and if you have done to him as he deserves—

JDG 9:17.text: for my father fought for you and risked his life to deliver you from the hand of Midian,
JDG 9:17.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · God the Father] for my father fought for you and risked his life to deliver you from the hand of Midian,

JDG 9:18.text: but you have risen up against my father’s house this day and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, and you have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the leaders of Shechem because he is your brother—
JDG 9:18.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · God the Father] but you have risen up against my father’s house this day and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, and you have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the leaders of Shechem because he is your brother—

JDG 9:19.text: if you have acted faithfully and honestly toward Jerubbaal and his house this day, then may you rejoice in Abimelech, and he in you.
JDG 9:19.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Faith] if you have acted faithfully and honestly toward Jerubbaal and his house this day, then may you rejoice in Abimelech, and he in you.

JDG 9:20.text: But if not, may fire come from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and may fire come from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech.”
JDG 9:20.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] But if not, may fire come from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and may fire come from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech.”

JDG 9:21.text: Then Jotham ran away, escaping to Beer, and he lived there for fear of his brother Abimelech.
JDG 9:21.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] Then Jotham ran away, escaping to Beer, and he lived there for fear of his brother Abimelech.

JDG 9:22.text: After Abimelech had reigned over Israel for three years,
JDG 9:22.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Israel] After Abimelech had reigned over Israel for three years,

JDG 9:23.text: God sent a spirit of animosity between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem and caused them to treat Abimelech deceitfully,
JDG 9:23.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Fruit of the Spirit] God sent a spirit of animosity between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem and caused them to treat Abimelech deceitfully,

JDG 9:24.text: in order that the crime against the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come to justice and their blood be avenged on their brother Abimelech and on the leaders of Shechem, who had helped him murder his brothers.
JDG 9:24.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Justice] in order that the crime against the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come to justice and their blood be avenged on their brother Abimelech and on the leaders of Shechem, who had helped him murder his brothers.

JDG 9:25.text: The leaders of Shechem set up an ambush against Abimelech on the hilltops, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road. So this was reported to Abimelech.
JDG 9:25.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] The leaders of Shechem set up an ambush against Abimelech on the hilltops, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road. So this was reported to Abimelech.

JDG 9:26.text: Meanwhile, Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and crossed into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem put their confidence in him.
JDG 9:26.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Assurance] Meanwhile, Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and crossed into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem put their confidence in him.

JDG 9:27.text: And after they had gone out into the fields, gathered grapes from their vineyards, and trodden them, they held a festival and went into the house of their god; and as they ate and drank, they cursed Abimelech.
JDG 9:27.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] And after they had gone out into the fields, gathered grapes from their vineyards, and trodden them, they held a festival and went into the house of their god; and as they ate and drank, they cursed Abimelech.

JDG 9:28.text: Then Gaal son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is not Zebul his officer? You are to serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem. Why should we serve Abimelech?
JDG 9:28.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · God the Father] Then Gaal son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is not Zebul his officer? You are to serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem. Why should we serve Abimelech?

JDG 9:29.text: If only this people were under my authority, I would remove Abimelech; I would say to him, ‘Muster your army and come out!’”
JDG 9:29.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] If only this people were under my authority, I would remove Abimelech; I would say to him, ‘Muster your army and come out!’”

JDG 9:30.text: When Zebul the governor of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, he burned with anger.
JDG 9:30.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] When Zebul the governor of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, he burned with anger.

JDG 9:31.text: So he covertly sent messengers to Abimelech to say, “Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.
JDG 9:31.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9 · Angels] So he covertly sent messengers to Abimelech to say, “Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.

JDG 9:32.text: Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields.
JDG 9:32.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields.

JDG 9:33.text: And in the morning at sunrise, get up and advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, do to them whatever you are able.”
JDG 9:33.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] And in the morning at sunrise, get up and advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, do to them whatever you are able.”

JDG 9:34.text: So Abimelech and all his troops set out by night and lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
JDG 9:34.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] So Abimelech and all his troops set out by night and lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.

JDG 9:35.text: Now Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate just as Abimelech and his men came out from their hiding places.
JDG 9:35.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] Now Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate just as Abimelech and his men came out from their hiding places.

JDG 9:36.text: When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, “Look, people are coming down from the mountains!”  But Zebul replied, “The shadows of the mountains look like men to you.”
JDG 9:36.bm25Text: [Judges · Chapter 9] When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, “Look, people are coming down from the mountains!”  But Zebul replied, “The shadows of the mountains look like men to you.”

JOB 20:22.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 20] In the midst of his plenty, he will be distressed; the full force of misery will come upon him.

JOB 20:23.text: When he has filled his stomach, God will vent His fury upon him, raining it down on him as he eats.
JOB 20:23.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 20] When he has filled his stomach, God will vent His fury upon him, raining it down on him as he eats.

JOB 20:24.text: Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce him.
JOB 20:24.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 20] Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce him.

JOB 20:25.text: It is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver. Terrors come over him.
JOB 20:25.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 20] It is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver. Terrors come over him.

JOB 20:26.text: Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.
JOB 20:26.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 20] Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.

JOB 20:27.text: The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
JOB 20:27.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 20] The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.

JOB 20:28.text: The possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God’s wrath.
JOB 20:28.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 20] The possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God’s wrath.

JOB 20:29.text: This is the wicked man’s portion from God, the inheritance God has appointed him.”
JOB 20:29.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 20 · Inheritance] This is the wicked man’s portion from God, the inheritance God has appointed him.”

JOB 21:2.text: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.
JOB 21:2.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Comfort] “Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.

JOB 21:3.text: Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.
JOB 21:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.

JOB 21:4.text: Is my complaint against a man? Then why should I not be impatient?
JOB 21:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Is my complaint against a man? Then why should I not be impatient?

JOB 21:5.text: Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.
JOB 21:5.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.

JOB 21:6.text: When I remember, terror takes hold, and my body trembles in horror.
JOB 21:6.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] When I remember, terror takes hold, and my body trembles in horror.

JOB 21:7.text: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?
JOB 21:7.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?

JOB 21:8.text: Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.
JOB 21:8.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Children] Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.

JOB 21:9.text: Their homes are safe from fear; no rod of punishment from God is upon them.
JOB 21:9.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Their homes are safe from fear; no rod of punishment from God is upon them.

JOB 21:10.text: Their bulls breed without fail; their cows bear calves and do not miscarry.
JOB 21:10.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Their bulls breed without fail; their cows bear calves and do not miscarry.

JOB 21:11.text: They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about,
JOB 21:11.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · About Forgiveness, Children] They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about,

JOB 21:12.text: singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.
JOB 21:12.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.

JOB 21:13.text: They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.
JOB 21:13.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Blessing, Death] They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.

JOB 21:14.text: Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.
JOB 21:14.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Lust] Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.

JOB 21:15.text: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’
JOB 21:15.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’

JOB 21:16.text: Still, their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.
JOB 21:16.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Blessing] Still, their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.

JOB 21:17.text: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?
JOB 21:17.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Devote To Destruction, Light] How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?

JOB 21:18.text: Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?
JOB 21:18.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?

JOB 21:19.text: It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.
JOB 21:19.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Children] It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.

JOB 21:20.text: Let his eyes see his own destruction; let him drink for himself the wrath of the Almighty.
JOB 21:20.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Devote To Destruction] Let his eyes see his own destruction; let him drink for himself the wrath of the Almighty.

JOB 21:21.text: For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has run out?
JOB 21:21.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · About Forgiveness, Family] For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has run out?

JOB 21:22.text: Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?
JOB 21:22.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?

JOB 21:23.text: One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease.
JOB 21:23.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease.

JOB 21:24.text: His body is well nourished, and his bones are rich with marrow.
JOB 21:24.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] His body is well nourished, and his bones are rich with marrow.

JOB 21:25.text: Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.
JOB 21:25.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Blessing] Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.

JOB 21:26.text: But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.
JOB 21:26.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.

JOB 21:27.text: Behold, I know your thoughts full well, the schemes by which you would wrong me.
JOB 21:27.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Behold, I know your thoughts full well, the schemes by which you would wrong me.

JOB 21:28.text: For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?’
JOB 21:28.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?’

JOB 21:29.text: Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their reports?
JOB 21:29.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their reports?

JOB 21:30.text: Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.
JOB 21:30.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.

JOB 21:31.text: Who denounces his behavior to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?
JOB 21:31.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] Who denounces his behavior to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?

JOB 21:32.text: He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
JOB 21:32.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Death] He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.

JOB 21:33.text: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number.
JOB 21:33.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21] The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number.

JOB 21:34.text: So how can you comfort me with empty words? For your answers remain full of falsehood.”
JOB 21:34.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 21 · Comfort, Falsehood] So how can you comfort me with empty words? For your answers remain full of falsehood.”

JOB 22:1.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

JOB 22:2.text: “Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?
JOB 22:2.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] “Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?

JOB 22:3.text: Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does He profit if your ways are blameless?
JOB 22:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does He profit if your ways are blameless?

JOB 22:4.text: Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?
JOB 22:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22 · Judgment] Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?

JOB 22:5.text: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?
JOB 22:5.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?

JOB 22:6.text: For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.
JOB 22:6.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.

JOB 22:7.text: You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished,
JOB 22:7.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished,

JOB 22:8.text: while the land belonged to a mighty man, and a man of honor lived on it.
JOB 22:8.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] while the land belonged to a mighty man, and a man of honor lived on it.

JOB 22:9.text: You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.
JOB 22:9.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.

JOB 22:10.text: Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you;
JOB 22:10.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you;

JOB 22:11.text: it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
JOB 22:11.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.

JOB 22:12.text: Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!
JOB 22:12.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!

JOB 22:13.text: Yet you say: ‘What does God know? Does He judge through thick darkness?
JOB 22:13.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] Yet you say: ‘What does God know? Does He judge through thick darkness?

JOB 22:14.text: Thick clouds veil Him so He does not see us as He traverses the vault of heaven.’
JOB 22:14.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22 · Heaven] Thick clouds veil Him so He does not see us as He traverses the vault of heaven.’

JOB 22:15.text: Will you stay on the ancient path that wicked men have trod?
JOB 22:15.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] Will you stay on the ancient path that wicked men have trod?

JOB 22:16.text: They were snatched away before their time, and their foundations were swept away by a flood.
JOB 22:16.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] They were snatched away before their time, and their foundations were swept away by a flood.

JOB 22:17.text: They said to God, ‘Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?’
JOB 22:17.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] They said to God, ‘Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?’

JOB 22:18.text: But it was He who filled their houses with good things; so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.
JOB 22:18.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] But it was He who filled their houses with good things; so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.

JOB 22:19.text: The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them:
JOB 22:19.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them:

JOB 22:20.text: ‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their excess.’
JOB 22:20.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] ‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their excess.’

JOB 22:21.text: Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you.
JOB 22:21.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you.

JOB 22:22.text: Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.
JOB 22:22.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22 · Adultery In Heart] Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.

JOB 22:23.text: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice from your tents
JOB 22:23.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice from your tents

JOB 22:24.text: and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines,
JOB 22:24.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines,

JOB 22:25.text: then the Almighty will be your gold and the finest silver for you.
JOB 22:25.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] then the Almighty will be your gold and the finest silver for you.

JOB 22:26.text: Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
JOB 22:26.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.

JOB 22:27.text: You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
JOB 22:27.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.

JOB 22:28.text: Your decisions will be carried out, and light will shine on your ways.
JOB 22:28.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22 · Light] Your decisions will be carried out, and light will shine on your ways.

JOB 22:29.text: When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly.
JOB 22:29.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly.

JOB 22:30.text: He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.”
JOB 22:30.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 22] He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.”

JOB 23:2.text: “Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.
JOB 23:2.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] “Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.

JOB 23:3.text: If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat.
JOB 23:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat.

JOB 23:4.text: I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.
JOB 23:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.

JOB 23:5.text: I would learn how He would answer, and consider what He would say.
JOB 23:5.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] I would learn how He would answer, and consider what He would say.

JOB 23:6.text: Would He contend with me in His great power? No, He would certainly take note of me.
JOB 23:6.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] Would He contend with me in His great power? No, He would certainly take note of me.

JOB 23:7.text: Then an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge.
JOB 23:7.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] Then an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge.

JOB 23:8.text: If I go east, He is not there, and if I go west, I cannot find Him.
JOB 23:8.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] If I go east, He is not there, and if I go west, I cannot find Him.

JOB 23:9.text: When He is at work in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him.
JOB 23:9.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] When He is at work in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him.

JOB 23:10.text: Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.
JOB 23:10.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.

JOB 23:11.text: My feet have followed in His tracks; I have kept His way without turning aside.
JOB 23:11.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] My feet have followed in His tracks; I have kept His way without turning aside.

JOB 23:12.text: I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my daily bread.
JOB 23:12.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my daily bread.

JOB 23:13.text: But He is unchangeable, and who can oppose Him? He does what He desires.
JOB 23:13.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] But He is unchangeable, and who can oppose Him? He does what He desires.

JOB 23:14.text: For He carries out His decree against me, and He has many such plans.
JOB 23:14.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] For He carries out His decree against me, and He has many such plans.

JOB 23:15.text: Therefore I am terrified in His presence; when I consider this, I fear Him.
JOB 23:15.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] Therefore I am terrified in His presence; when I consider this, I fear Him.

JOB 23:16.text: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.
JOB 23:16.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23 · Adultery In Heart] God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.

JOB 23:17.text: Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.
JOB 23:17.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 23] Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.

JOB 24:1.text: “Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?
JOB 24:1.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · End Times, Judgment] “Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?

JOB 24:2.text: Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.
JOB 24:2.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.

JOB 24:3.text: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.
JOB 24:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.

JOB 24:4.text: They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.
JOB 24:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.

JOB 24:5.text: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children.
JOB 24:5.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · Children] Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children.

JOB 24:6.text: They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.
JOB 24:6.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.

JOB 24:7.text: Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.
JOB 24:7.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.

JOB 24:8.text: Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.
JOB 24:8.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.

JOB 24:9.text: The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.
JOB 24:9.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.

JOB 24:10.text: Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.
JOB 24:10.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · About Forgiveness] Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.

JOB 24:11.text: They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.
JOB 24:11.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.

JOB 24:12.text: From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.
JOB 24:12.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.

JOB 24:13.text: Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths.
JOB 24:13.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · Light] Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths.

JOB 24:14.text: When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.
JOB 24:14.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.

JOB 24:15.text: The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face.
JOB 24:15.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · Adulterer] The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face.

JOB 24:16.text: In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in, never to experience the light.
JOB 24:16.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · Light] In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in, never to experience the light.

JOB 24:17.text: For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness!
JOB 24:17.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness!

JOB 24:18.text: They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.
JOB 24:18.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · Inheritance] They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.

JOB 24:19.text: As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.
JOB 24:19.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · Death] As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.

JOB 24:20.text: The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is like a broken tree.
JOB 24:20.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is like a broken tree.

JOB 24:21.text: They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.
JOB 24:21.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · Grace] They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.

JOB 24:22.text: Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.
JOB 24:22.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · Assurance] Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.

JOB 24:23.text: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.
JOB 24:23.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.

JOB 24:24.text: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
JOB 24:24.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24 · Ascension] They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.

JOB 24:25.text: If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”
JOB 24:25.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 24] If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”

JOB 25:1.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 25] Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

JOB 25:2.text: “Dominion and awe belong to God; He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.
JOB 25:2.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 25 · Heaven] “Dominion and awe belong to God; He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.

JOB 25:3.text: Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise?
JOB 25:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 25 · Light] Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise?

JOB 25:4.text: How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
JOB 25:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 25] How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?

JOB 25:5.text: If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight,
JOB 25:5.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 25] If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight,

JOB 25:6.text: how much less man, who is but a maggot, and the son of man, who is but a worm!”
JOB 25:6.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 25] how much less man, who is but a maggot, and the son of man, who is but a worm!”

JOB 26:2.text: “How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!
JOB 26:2.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 26] “How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!

JOB 26:3.text: How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight!
JOB 26:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 26] How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight!

JOB 26:4.text: To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?
JOB 26:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 26 · Fruit of the Spirit] To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?

JOB 26:5.text: The dead tremble— those beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.

JOB 39:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] They crouch down and bring forth their young; they deliver their newborn.

JOB 39:4.text: Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.
JOB 39:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.

JOB 39:5.text: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?
JOB 39:5.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?

JOB 39:6.text: I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.
JOB 39:6.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.

JOB 39:7.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] He scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver.

JOB 39:8.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.

JOB 39:9.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger at night?

JOB 39:10.text: Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?
JOB 39:10.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?

JOB 39:11.text: Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?
JOB 39:11.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?

JOB 39:12.text: Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
JOB 39:12.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39 · Faith] Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?

JOB 39:13.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.

JOB 39:14.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.

JOB 39:15.text: She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.
JOB 39:15.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.

JOB 39:16.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] She treats her young harshly, as if not her own, with no concern that her labor was in vain.

JOB 39:17.text: For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.
JOB 39:17.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.

JOB 39:18.text: Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
JOB 39:18.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.

JOB 39:19.text: Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?
JOB 39:19.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?

JOB 39:20.text: Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?
JOB 39:20.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?

JOB 39:21.text: He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.
JOB 39:21.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.

JOB 39:22.text: He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.
JOB 39:22.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.

JOB 39:23.text: A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.
JOB 39:23.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.

JOB 39:24.text: Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.
JOB 39:24.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.

JOB 39:25.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] At the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor. He catches the scent of battle from afar— the shouts of captains and the cry of war.

JOB 39:26.text: Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?
JOB 39:26.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?

JOB 39:27.text: Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?
JOB 39:27.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?

JOB 39:28.text: He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.
JOB 39:28.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.

JOB 39:29.text: From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.
JOB 39:29.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.

JOB 39:30.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 39] His young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there he is.”

JOB 40:1.text: And the LORD said to Job:
JOB 40:1.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] And the LORD said to Job:

JOB 40:2.text: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”
JOB 40:2.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”

JOB 40:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] Then Job answered the LORD:

JOB 40:4.text: “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.
JOB 40:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.

JOB 40:5.text: I have spoken once, but I have no answer— twice, but I have nothing to add.”
JOB 40:5.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] I have spoken once, but I have no answer— twice, but I have nothing to add.”

JOB 40:6.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
JOB 40:6.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:

JOB 40:7.text: “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
JOB 40:7.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.

JOB 40:8.text: Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?
JOB 40:8.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40 · Justice] Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?

JOB 40:9.text: Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?
JOB 40:9.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?

JOB 40:10.text: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.
JOB 40:10.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40 · Glory] Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.

JOB 40:11.text: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.
JOB 40:11.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.

JOB 40:12.text: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.
JOB 40:12.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.

JOB 40:13.text: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.
JOB 40:13.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40 · Death] Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.

JOB 40:14.text: Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.
JOB 40:14.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.

JOB 40:15.text: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.
JOB 40:15.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.

JOB 40:16.text: See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.
JOB 40:16.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.

JOB 40:17.text: His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
JOB 40:17.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.

JOB 40:18.text: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.
JOB 40:18.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.

JOB 40:19.text: He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.
JOB 40:19.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40 · Creation] He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.

JOB 40:20.text: The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.
JOB 40:20.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.

JOB 40:21.text: He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.
JOB 40:21.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.

JOB 40:22.text: The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.
JOB 40:22.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.

JOB 40:23.text: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.
JOB 40:23.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.

JOB 40:24.text: Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?
JOB 40:24.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 40] Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?

JOB 41:1.text: “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?
JOB 41:1.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?

JOB 41:2.text: Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
JOB 41:2.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?

JOB 41:3.text: Will he beg you for mercy or speak to you softly?
JOB 41:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41 · Forgiveness, Compassion] Will he beg you for mercy or speak to you softly?

JOB 41:4.text: Will he make a covenant with you to take him as a slave for life?
JOB 41:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41 · Covenant] Will he make a covenant with you to take him as a slave for life?

JOB 41:5.text: Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?
JOB 41:5.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?

JOB 41:6.text: Will traders barter for him or divide him among the merchants?
JOB 41:6.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Will traders barter for him or divide him among the merchants?

JOB 41:7.text: Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?
JOB 41:7.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?

JOB 41:8.text: If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never repeat it!
JOB 41:8.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never repeat it!

JOB 41:9.text: Surely hope of overcoming him is false. Is not the sight of him overwhelming?
JOB 41:9.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41 · False Gods, False Witness] Surely hope of overcoming him is false. Is not the sight of him overwhelming?

JOB 41:10.text: No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan. Then who is able to stand against Me?
JOB 41:10.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan. Then who is able to stand against Me?

JOB 41:11.text: Who has given to Me that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.
JOB 41:11.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41 · Heaven] Who has given to Me that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.

JOB 41:12.text: I cannot keep silent about his limbs, his power and graceful form.
JOB 41:12.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41 · About Forgiveness] I cannot keep silent about his limbs, his power and graceful form.

JOB 41:13.text: Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?
JOB 41:13.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?

JOB 41:14.text: Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?
JOB 41:14.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?

JOB 41:15.text: His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.
JOB 41:15.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.

JOB 41:16.text: One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.
JOB 41:16.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.

JOB 41:17.text: They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.
JOB 41:17.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.

JOB 41:18.text: His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.
JOB 41:18.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41 · Light] His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.

JOB 41:19.text: Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!
JOB 41:19.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!

JOB 41:20.text: Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
JOB 41:20.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.

JOB 41:21.text: His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.
JOB 41:21.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.

JOB 41:22.text: Strength resides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.
JOB 41:22.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Strength resides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.

JOB 41:23.text: The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.
JOB 41:23.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.

JOB 41:24.text: His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone!
JOB 41:24.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone!

JOB 41:25.text: When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; they withdraw before his thrashing.
JOB 41:25.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; they withdraw before his thrashing.

JOB 41:26.text: The sword that reaches him has no effect, nor does the spear or dart or arrow.
JOB 41:26.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] The sword that reaches him has no effect, nor does the spear or dart or arrow.

JOB 41:27.text: He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
JOB 41:27.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.

JOB 41:28.text: No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.
JOB 41:28.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.

JOB 41:29.text: A club is regarded as straw, and he laughs at the sound of the lance.
JOB 41:29.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] A club is regarded as straw, and he laughs at the sound of the lance.

JOB 41:30.text: His undersides are jagged potsherds, spreading out the mud like a threshing sledge.
JOB 41:30.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] His undersides are jagged potsherds, spreading out the mud like a threshing sledge.

JOB 41:31.text: He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.
JOB 41:31.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.

JOB 41:32.text: He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair!
JOB 41:32.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair!

JOB 41:33.text: Nothing on earth is his equal— a creature devoid of fear!
JOB 41:33.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] Nothing on earth is his equal— a creature devoid of fear!

JOB 41:34.text: He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.”
JOB 41:34.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 41] He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.”

JOB 42:1.text: Then Job replied to the LORD:
JOB 42:1.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 42] Then Job replied to the LORD:

JOB 42:2.text: “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.
JOB 42:2.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 42] “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.

JOB 42:3.text: You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
JOB 42:3.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 42] You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.

JOB 42:4.text: You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’
JOB 42:4.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 42] You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’

JOB 42:5.text: My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.
JOB 42:5.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 42] My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.

JOB 42:6.text: Therefore I retract my words, and I repent in dust and ashes.”
JOB 42:6.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 42] Therefore I retract my words, and I repent in dust and ashes.”

JOB 42:7.text: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.

JOB 42:8.text: So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”
JOB 42:8.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 42 · About Forgiveness] So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”

JOB 42:9.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 42] So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s request.

JOB 42:12.bm25Text: [Job · Chapter 42 · Female] So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.

JOL 1:9.bm25Text: [Joel · Chapter 1] Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests are in mourning, those who minister before the LORD.
