ROM 11:26.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11 · Israel] And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written:  “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove godlessness from Jacob.

ROM 11:27.text: And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.”
ROM 11:27.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11 · Covenant] And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.”

ROM 11:28.text: Regarding the gospel, they are enemies on your account; but regarding election, they are loved on account of the patriarchs.
ROM 11:28.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11 · Love, Election] Regarding the gospel, they are enemies on your account; but regarding election, they are loved on account of the patriarchs.

ROM 11:29.text: For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.
ROM 11:29.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11] For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.

ROM 11:30.text: Just as you who formerly disobeyed God have now received mercy through their disobedience,
ROM 11:30.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11 · Forgiveness, Compassion] Just as you who formerly disobeyed God have now received mercy through their disobedience,

ROM 11:31.text: so they too have now disobeyed, in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.
ROM 11:31.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11 · Forgiveness, Compassion] so they too have now disobeyed, in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.

ROM 11:32.text: For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.
ROM 11:32.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11 · Forgiveness, Compassion] For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.

ROM 11:33.text: O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!
ROM 11:33.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11] O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!

ROM 11:34.text: “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?”
ROM 11:34.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11] “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?”

ROM 11:35.text: “Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?”
ROM 11:35.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11] “Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?”

ROM 11:36.text: For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen.
ROM 11:36.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 11 · Glory] For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen.

ROM 12:1.text: Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.
ROM 12:1.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Forgiveness, Compassion] Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.

ROM 12:2.text: Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.
ROM 12:2.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.

ROM 12:3.text: For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.
ROM 12:3.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Faith, Grace] For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.

ROM 12:4.text: Just as each of us has one body with many members, and not all members have the same function,
ROM 12:4.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Body of Christ] Just as each of us has one body with many members, and not all members have the same function,

ROM 12:5.text: so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another.
ROM 12:5.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another.

ROM 12:6.text: We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If one’s gift is prophecy, let him use it in proportion to his faith;
ROM 12:6.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Faith, Grace] We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If one’s gift is prophecy, let him use it in proportion to his faith;

ROM 12:7.text: if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;
ROM 12:7.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;

ROM 12:8.text: if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.
ROM 12:8.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Forgiveness, Compassion] if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.

ROM 12:9.text: Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.
ROM 12:9.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Love] Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.

ROM 12:10.text: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.
ROM 12:10.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Love] Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.

ROM 12:11.text: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
ROM 12:11.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.

ROM 12:12.text: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.
ROM 12:12.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.

ROM 12:13.text: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.
ROM 12:13.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Hospitality] Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.

ROM 12:14.text: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
ROM 12:14.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Curse God] Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.

ROM 12:15.text: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
ROM 12:15.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.

ROM 12:16.text: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.
ROM 12:16.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.

ROM 12:17.text: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
ROM 12:17.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.

ROM 12:18.text: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.
ROM 12:18.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.

ROM 12:19.text: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
ROM 12:19.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12 · Love] Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”

ROM 12:20.text: On the contrary,  “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”
ROM 12:20.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] On the contrary,  “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”

ROM 12:21.text: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
ROM 12:21.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 12] Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

ROM 13:1.text: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
ROM 13:1.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13] Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.

ROM 13:2.text: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.
ROM 13:2.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13 · Judgment] Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.

ROM 13:3.text: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.
ROM 13:3.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13] For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.

ROM 13:4.text: For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.
ROM 13:4.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13] For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.

ROM 13:5.text: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.
ROM 13:5.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13] Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.

ROM 13:6.text: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.
ROM 13:6.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13 · Devote To Destruction] This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.

ROM 13:7.text: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.
ROM 13:7.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13] Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.

ROM 13:8.text: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
ROM 13:8.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13 · Love] Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

ROM 13:9.text: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
ROM 13:9.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13 · Love, Adultery] The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

ROM 13:10.text: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
ROM 13:10.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13 · Love] Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.

ROM 13:11.text: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
ROM 13:11.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13 · Faith] And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.

ROM 13:12.text: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
ROM 13:12.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13 · Armor of God, Light] The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.

ROM 13:13.text: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
ROM 13:13.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13 · Jealousy] Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.

ROM 13:14.text: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.
ROM 13:14.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 13 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.

ROM 14:1.text: Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.
ROM 14:1.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Faith, Judgment] Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.

ROM 14:2.text: For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.
ROM 14:2.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Faith] For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.

ROM 14:3.text: The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.
ROM 14:3.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.

ROM 14:4.text: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
ROM 14:4.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.

ROM 14:5.text: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
ROM 14:5.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.

ROM 14:6.text: He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.
ROM 14:6.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.

ROM 14:7.text: For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.
ROM 14:7.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.

ROM 14:8.text: If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
ROM 14:8.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.

ROM 14:9.text: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.
ROM 14:9.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.

ROM 14:10.text: Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.
ROM 14:10.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Judgment] Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.

ROM 14:11.text: It is written:  “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”
ROM 14:11.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] It is written:  “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”

ROM 14:12.text: So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.
ROM 14:12.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.

ROM 14:13.text: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.
ROM 14:13.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.

ROM 14:14.text: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.
ROM 14:14.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Jesus Christ] I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.

ROM 14:15.text: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.
ROM 14:15.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Love, Body of Christ] If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.

ROM 14:16.text: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.
ROM 14:16.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.

ROM 14:17.text: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
ROM 14:17.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Fruit of the Spirit, Kingdom of God] For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

ROM 14:18.text: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.
ROM 14:18.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.

ROM 14:19.text: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.
ROM 14:19.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Encouragement] So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.

ROM 14:20.text: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.
ROM 14:20.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Destroy Canaan, Destroy Canaanites] Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.

ROM 14:21.text: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.
ROM 14:21.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14] It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.

ROM 14:22.text: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
ROM 14:22.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · About Forgiveness, Faith] Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.

ROM 14:23.text: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
ROM 14:23.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 14 · Faith] But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

ROM 15:1.text: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.
ROM 15:1.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.

ROM 15:2.text: Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.
ROM 15:2.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.

ROM 15:3.text: For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”
ROM 15:3.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”

ROM 15:4.text: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.
ROM 15:4.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Comfort, Encouragement] For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.

ROM 15:5.text: Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,
ROM 15:5.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, Comfort] Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,

ROM 15:6.text: so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM 15:6.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, God the Father] so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

ROM 15:7.text: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.
ROM 15:7.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, Glory] Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.

ROM 15:8.text: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs,
ROM 15:8.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs,

ROM 15:9.text: so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written:  “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”
ROM 15:9.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Forgiveness, Compassion] so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written:  “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”

ROM 15:10.text: Again, it says:  “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”
ROM 15:10.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] Again, it says:  “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”

ROM 15:11.text: And again:  “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”
ROM 15:11.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] And again:  “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”

ROM 15:12.text: And once more, Isaiah says:  “The Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.”
ROM 15:12.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] And once more, Isaiah says:  “The Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.”

ROM 15:13.text: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
ROM 15:13.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Faith, Fruit of the Spirit] Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

ROM 15:14.text: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
ROM 15:14.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.

ROM 15:15.text: However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me
ROM 15:15.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Grace] However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me

ROM 15:16.text: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
ROM 15:16.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, Fruit of the Spirit] to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

ROM 15:17.text: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.
ROM 15:17.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.

ROM 15:18.text: I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,
ROM 15:18.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,

ROM 15:19.text: by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
ROM 15:19.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, Fruit of the Spirit] by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.

ROM 15:20.text: In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.
ROM 15:20.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Body of Christ, Gospel] In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.

ROM 15:21.text: Rather, as it is written:  “Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
ROM 15:21.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · About Forgiveness] Rather, as it is written:  “Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”

ROM 15:22.text: That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.
ROM 15:22.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.

ROM 15:23.text: But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you,
ROM 15:23.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you,

ROM 15:24.text: I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.
ROM 15:24.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.

ROM 15:25.text: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.
ROM 15:25.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.

ROM 15:26.text: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
ROM 15:26.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.

ROM 15:27.text: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.
ROM 15:27.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.

ROM 15:28.text: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.
ROM 15:28.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15] So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.

ROM 15:29.text: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
ROM 15:29.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 15 · Blessing, Body of Christ] I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.

ROM 16:2.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16] Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.

ROM 16:4.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16] who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.

ROM 16:7.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16 · Apostles, Body of Christ] Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.

ROM 16:9.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16 · Love, Body of Christ] Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.

ROM 16:10.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16 · Body of Christ, Family] Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ.  Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.

ROM 16:15.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16] Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.

ROM 16:16.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16 · Body of Christ, Jesus Christ] Greet one another with a holy kiss.  All the churches of Christ send you greetings.

ROM 16:17.text: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.
ROM 16:17.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16] Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.

ROM 16:18.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16 · Body of Christ, Deceive] For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.

ROM 16:19.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16 · About Forgiveness] Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.

ROM 16:20.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16 · Body of Christ, Grace] The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

ROM 16:22.bm25Text: [Romans · Chapter 16] I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.

RUT 1:1.text: In the days when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land. And a certain man from Bethlehem in Judah, with his wife and two sons, went to reside in the land of Moab.
RUT 1:1.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] In the days when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land. And a certain man from Bethlehem in Judah, with his wife and two sons, went to reside in the land of Moab.

RUT 1:2.text: The man’s name was Elimelech, his wife’s name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah, and they entered the land of Moab and settled there.
RUT 1:2.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] The man’s name was Elimelech, his wife’s name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah, and they entered the land of Moab and settled there.

RUT 1:3.text: Then Naomi’s husband Elimelech died, and she was left with her two sons,
RUT 1:3.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] Then Naomi’s husband Elimelech died, and she was left with her two sons,

RUT 1:4.text: who took Moabite women as their wives, one named Orpah and the other named Ruth.  And after they had lived in Moab about ten years,
RUT 1:4.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1 · About Forgiveness, Biblical Women] who took Moabite women as their wives, one named Orpah and the other named Ruth.  And after they had lived in Moab about ten years,

RUT 1:5.text: both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and without her husband.
RUT 1:5.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and without her husband.

RUT 1:6.text: When Naomi heard in Moab that the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food, she and her daughters-in-law prepared to leave the land of Moab.
RUT 1:6.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] When Naomi heard in Moab that the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food, she and her daughters-in-law prepared to leave the land of Moab.

RUT 1:7.text: Accompanied by her two daughters-in-law, she left the place where she had been living and set out on the road leading back to the land of Judah.
RUT 1:7.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] Accompanied by her two daughters-in-law, she left the place where she had been living and set out on the road leading back to the land of Judah.

RUT 1:8.text: Then Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you to your mother’s home. May the LORD show you loving devotion, as you have shown to your dead and to me.
RUT 1:8.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1 · Devotion] Then Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you to your mother’s home. May the LORD show you loving devotion, as you have shown to your dead and to me.

RUT 1:9.text: May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband.”  And she kissed them as they wept aloud
RUT 1:9.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband.”  And she kissed them as they wept aloud

RUT 1:10.text: and said, “Surely we will return with you to your people.”
RUT 1:10.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] and said, “Surely we will return with you to your people.”

RUT 1:11.text: But Naomi replied, “Return home, my daughters. Why would you go with me? Are there still sons in my womb to become your husbands?
RUT 1:11.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1 · Husbands] But Naomi replied, “Return home, my daughters. Why would you go with me? Are there still sons in my womb to become your husbands?

RUT 1:12.text: Return home, my daughters. Go on, for I am too old to have another husband. Even if I thought there was hope for me to have a husband tonight and to bear sons,
RUT 1:12.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] Return home, my daughters. Go on, for I am too old to have another husband. Even if I thought there was hope for me to have a husband tonight and to bear sons,

RUT 1:13.text: would you wait for them to grow up? Would you refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, it grieves me very much for your sakes that the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.”
RUT 1:13.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1 · Husbands] would you wait for them to grow up? Would you refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, it grieves me very much for your sakes that the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.”

RUT 1:14.text: Again they wept aloud, and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.
RUT 1:14.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] Again they wept aloud, and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.

RUT 1:15.text: “Look,” said Naomi, “your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; follow her back home.”
RUT 1:15.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] “Look,” said Naomi, “your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; follow her back home.”

RUT 1:16.text: But Ruth replied:  “Do not urge me to leave you or to turn from following you. For wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you live, I will live; your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.
RUT 1:16.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] But Ruth replied:  “Do not urge me to leave you or to turn from following you. For wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you live, I will live; your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.

RUT 1:17.text: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me.”
RUT 1:17.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1 · Death] Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me.”

RUT 1:18.text: When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her.
RUT 1:18.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her.

RUT 1:19.text: So Naomi and Ruth traveled until they came to Bethlehem. When they entered Bethlehem, the whole city was stirred because of them, and the women of the city exclaimed, “Can this be Naomi?”
RUT 1:19.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1 · Biblical Women, Heroic Women] So Naomi and Ruth traveled until they came to Bethlehem. When they entered Bethlehem, the whole city was stirred because of them, and the women of the city exclaimed, “Can this be Naomi?”

RUT 1:20.text: “Do not call me Naomi,” she replied. “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.
RUT 1:20.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] “Do not call me Naomi,” she replied. “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.

RUT 1:21.text: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? After all, the LORD has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me.”
RUT 1:21.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? After all, the LORD has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me.”

RUT 1:22.text: So Naomi returned from the land of Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth the Moabitess. And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
RUT 1:22.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 1] So Naomi returned from the land of Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth the Moabitess. And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

RUT 2:1.text: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side, a prominent man of noble character from the clan of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.
RUT 2:1.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side, a prominent man of noble character from the clan of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.

RUT 2:2.text: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, “Please let me go into the fields and glean heads of grain after someone in whose sight I may find favor.”  “Go ahead, my daughter,” Naomi replied.
RUT 2:2.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2 · Blessing] And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, “Please let me go into the fields and glean heads of grain after someone in whose sight I may find favor.”  “Go ahead, my daughter,” Naomi replied.

RUT 2:3.text: So Ruth departed and went out into the field and gleaned after the harvesters. And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.
RUT 2:3.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] So Ruth departed and went out into the field and gleaned after the harvesters. And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.

RUT 2:4.text: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, “The LORD be with you.”  “The LORD bless you,” they replied.
RUT 2:4.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, “The LORD be with you.”  “The LORD bless you,” they replied.

RUT 2:5.text: And Boaz asked the foreman of his harvesters, “Whose young woman is this?”
RUT 2:5.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] And Boaz asked the foreman of his harvesters, “Whose young woman is this?”

RUT 2:6.text: The foreman answered, “She is the Moabitess who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab.
RUT 2:6.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] The foreman answered, “She is the Moabitess who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab.

RUT 2:7.text: She has said, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves after the harvesters.’ So she came out and has continued from morning until now, except that she rested a short time in the shelter.”
RUT 2:7.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] She has said, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves after the harvesters.’ So she came out and has continued from morning until now, except that she rested a short time in the shelter.”

RUT 2:8.text: Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Do not go and glean in another field, and do not go away from this place, but stay here close to my servant girls.
RUT 2:8.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Do not go and glean in another field, and do not go away from this place, but stay here close to my servant girls.

RUT 2:9.text: Let your eyes be on the field they are harvesting, and follow along after these girls. Indeed, I have ordered the young men not to touch you. And when you are thirsty, go and drink from the jars the young men have filled.”
RUT 2:9.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] Let your eyes be on the field they are harvesting, and follow along after these girls. Indeed, I have ordered the young men not to touch you. And when you are thirsty, go and drink from the jars the young men have filled.”

RUT 2:10.text: At this, she fell on her face, bowing low to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you should take notice of me, even though I am a foreigner?”
RUT 2:10.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2 · Blessing] At this, she fell on her face, bowing low to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you should take notice of me, even though I am a foreigner?”

RUT 2:11.text: Boaz replied, “I have been made fully aware of all you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth, and how you came to a people you did not know before.
RUT 2:11.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2 · Death, God the Father] Boaz replied, “I have been made fully aware of all you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth, and how you came to a people you did not know before.

RUT 2:12.text: May the LORD repay your work, and may you receive a rich reward from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have taken refuge.”
RUT 2:12.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2 · Israel] May the LORD repay your work, and may you receive a rich reward from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have taken refuge.”

RUT 2:13.text: “My lord,” she said, “may I continue to find favor in your eyes, for you have comforted and spoken kindly to your maidservant, though I am not like one of your servant girls.”
RUT 2:13.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2 · Blessing] “My lord,” she said, “may I continue to find favor in your eyes, for you have comforted and spoken kindly to your maidservant, though I am not like one of your servant girls.”

RUT 2:14.text: At mealtime Boaz said to her, “Come over here; have some bread and dip it into the vinegar sauce.” So she sat down beside the harvesters, and he offered her roasted grain, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.
RUT 2:14.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] At mealtime Boaz said to her, “Come over here; have some bread and dip it into the vinegar sauce.” So she sat down beside the harvesters, and he offered her roasted grain, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.

RUT 2:15.text: When Ruth got up to glean, Boaz ordered his young men, “Even if she gathers among the sheaves, do not insult her.
RUT 2:15.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] When Ruth got up to glean, Boaz ordered his young men, “Even if she gathers among the sheaves, do not insult her.

RUT 2:16.text: Rather, pull out for her some stalks from the bundles and leave them for her to gather. Do not rebuke her.”
RUT 2:16.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] Rather, pull out for her some stalks from the bundles and leave them for her to gather. Do not rebuke her.”

RUT 2:17.text: So Ruth gathered grain in the field until evening. And when she beat out what she had gleaned, it was about an ephah of barley.
RUT 2:17.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2 · About Forgiveness] So Ruth gathered grain in the field until evening. And when she beat out what she had gleaned, it was about an ephah of barley.

RUT 2:18.text: She picked up the grain and went into the town, where her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. And she brought out what she had saved from her meal and gave it to Naomi.
RUT 2:18.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] She picked up the grain and went into the town, where her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. And she brought out what she had saved from her meal and gave it to Naomi.

RUT 2:19.text: Then her mother-in-law asked her, “Where did you glean today, and where did you work? Blessed be the man who noticed you.”  So she told her mother-in-law where she had worked. “The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz,” she said.
RUT 2:19.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] Then her mother-in-law asked her, “Where did you glean today, and where did you work? Blessed be the man who noticed you.”  So she told her mother-in-law where she had worked. “The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz,” she said.

RUT 2:20.text: Then Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the LORD, who has not withdrawn His kindness from the living or the dead.” Naomi continued, “The man is a close relative. He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.”
RUT 2:20.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2 · Grace] Then Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the LORD, who has not withdrawn His kindness from the living or the dead.” Naomi continued, “The man is a close relative. He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.”

RUT 2:21.text: Then Ruth the Moabitess said, “He also told me, ‘Stay with my young men until they have finished gathering all my harvest.’”
RUT 2:21.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] Then Ruth the Moabitess said, “He also told me, ‘Stay with my young men until they have finished gathering all my harvest.’”

RUT 2:22.text: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law Ruth, “My daughter, it is good for you to work with his young women, so that nothing will happen to you in another field.”
RUT 2:22.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2 · Biblical Women, Heroic Women] And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law Ruth, “My daughter, it is good for you to work with his young women, so that nothing will happen to you in another field.”

RUT 2:23.text: So Ruth stayed close to the servant girls of Boaz to glean grain until the barley and wheat harvests were finished. And she lived with her mother-in-law.
RUT 2:23.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 2] So Ruth stayed close to the servant girls of Boaz to glean grain until the barley and wheat harvests were finished. And she lived with her mother-in-law.

RUT 3:1.text: One day Ruth’s mother-in-law Naomi said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you?
RUT 3:1.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] One day Ruth’s mother-in-law Naomi said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you?

RUT 3:2.text: Now is not Boaz, with whose servant girls you have been working, a relative of ours? In fact, tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.
RUT 3:2.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] Now is not Boaz, with whose servant girls you have been working, a relative of ours? In fact, tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.

RUT 3:3.text: Therefore wash yourself, put on perfume, and wear your best clothes. Go down to the threshing floor, but do not let the man know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
RUT 3:3.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] Therefore wash yourself, put on perfume, and wear your best clothes. Go down to the threshing floor, but do not let the man know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.

RUT 3:4.text: When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go in and uncover his feet, and lie down, and he will explain to you what you should do.”
RUT 3:4.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3 · Explain Romans] When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go in and uncover his feet, and lie down, and he will explain to you what you should do.”

RUT 3:5.text: “I will do everything you say,” Ruth answered.
RUT 3:5.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] “I will do everything you say,” Ruth answered.

RUT 3:6.text: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.
RUT 3:6.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.

RUT 3:7.text: After Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then Ruth went in secretly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
RUT 3:7.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] After Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then Ruth went in secretly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.

RUT 3:8.text: At midnight, Boaz was startled, turned over, and there lying at his feet was a woman!
RUT 3:8.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3 · Lying] At midnight, Boaz was startled, turned over, and there lying at his feet was a woman!

RUT 3:9.text: “Who are you?” he asked.  “I am your servant Ruth,” she replied. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer.”
RUT 3:9.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] “Who are you?” he asked.  “I am your servant Ruth,” she replied. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer.”

RUT 3:10.text: Then Boaz said, “May the LORD bless you, my daughter. You have shown more kindness now than before, because you have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.
RUT 3:10.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3 · Grace] Then Boaz said, “May the LORD bless you, my daughter. You have shown more kindness now than before, because you have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.

RUT 3:11.text: And now do not be afraid, my daughter. I will do for you whatever you request, since all my fellow townspeople know that you are a woman of noble character.
RUT 3:11.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] And now do not be afraid, my daughter. I will do for you whatever you request, since all my fellow townspeople know that you are a woman of noble character.

RUT 3:12.text: Yes, it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I.
RUT 3:12.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] Yes, it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I.

RUT 3:13.text: Stay here tonight, and in the morning, if he wants to redeem you, good. Let him redeem you. But if he does not want to redeem you, as surely as the LORD lives, I will. Now lie here until morning.”
RUT 3:13.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] Stay here tonight, and in the morning, if he wants to redeem you, good. Let him redeem you. But if he does not want to redeem you, as surely as the LORD lives, I will. Now lie here until morning.”

RUT 3:14.text: So she lay down at his feet until morning, but she got up before anyone else could recognize her.  Then Boaz said, “Do not let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.”
RUT 3:14.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] So she lay down at his feet until morning, but she got up before anyone else could recognize her.  Then Boaz said, “Do not let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.”

RUT 3:15.text: And he told her, “Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” When she did so, he shoveled six measures of barley into her shawl. Then he went into the city.
RUT 3:15.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] And he told her, “Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” When she did so, he shoveled six measures of barley into her shawl. Then he went into the city.

RUT 3:16.text: When Ruth returned to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked her, “How did it go, my daughter?”  Then Ruth told her all that Boaz had done for her.
RUT 3:16.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] When Ruth returned to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked her, “How did it go, my daughter?”  Then Ruth told her all that Boaz had done for her.

RUT 3:17.text: And she said, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
RUT 3:17.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] And she said, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”

RUT 3:18.text: “Wait, my daughter,” said Naomi, “until you find out how things go, for he will not rest unless he has resolved the matter today.”
RUT 3:18.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 3] “Wait, my daughter,” said Naomi, “until you find out how things go, for he will not rest unless he has resolved the matter today.”

RUT 4:1.text: Meanwhile, Boaz went to the gate and sat down there. Soon the kinsman-redeemer of whom he had spoken came along, and Boaz said, “Come over here, my friend, and sit down.” So he went over and sat down.
RUT 4:1.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4] Meanwhile, Boaz went to the gate and sat down there. Soon the kinsman-redeemer of whom he had spoken came along, and Boaz said, “Come over here, my friend, and sit down.” So he went over and sat down.

RUT 4:2.text: Then Boaz took ten of the elders of the city and said, “Sit here,” and they did so.
RUT 4:2.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Leadership] Then Boaz took ten of the elders of the city and said, “Sit here,” and they did so.

RUT 4:3.text: And he said to the kinsman-redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from the land of Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.
RUT 4:3.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4] And he said to the kinsman-redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from the land of Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

RUT 4:4.text: I thought I should inform you that you may buy it back in the presence of those seated here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you want to redeem it, do so. But if you will not redeem it, tell me so I may know, because there is no one but you to redeem it, and I am next after you.”  “I will redeem it,” he replied.
RUT 4:4.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Leadership] I thought I should inform you that you may buy it back in the presence of those seated here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you want to redeem it, do so. But if you will not redeem it, tell me so I may know, because there is no one but you to redeem it, and I am next after you.”  “I will redeem it,” he replied.

RUT 4:5.text: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the land from Naomi and also from Ruth the Moabitess, you must also acquire the widow of the deceased in order to raise up the name of the deceased on his inheritance.”
RUT 4:5.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Inheritance] Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the land from Naomi and also from Ruth the Moabitess, you must also acquire the widow of the deceased in order to raise up the name of the deceased on his inheritance.”

RUT 4:6.text: The kinsman-redeemer replied, “I cannot redeem it myself, or I would jeopardize my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption, because I cannot redeem it.”
RUT 4:6.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Inheritance] The kinsman-redeemer replied, “I cannot redeem it myself, or I would jeopardize my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption, because I cannot redeem it.”

RUT 4:7.text: Now in former times in Israel, concerning the redemption or exchange of property, to make any matter legally binding a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party, and this was a confirmation in Israel.
RUT 4:7.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · End Times, Israel] Now in former times in Israel, concerning the redemption or exchange of property, to make any matter legally binding a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party, and this was a confirmation in Israel.

RUT 4:8.text: So the kinsman-redeemer removed his sandal and said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself.”
RUT 4:8.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4] So the kinsman-redeemer removed his sandal and said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself.”

RUT 4:9.text: At this, Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I am buying from Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon.
RUT 4:9.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Leadership] At this, Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I am buying from Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon.

RUT 4:10.text: Moreover, I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife, to raise up the name of the deceased through his inheritance, so that his name will not disappear from among his brothers or from the gate of his home. You are witnesses today.”
RUT 4:10.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Inheritance] Moreover, I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife, to raise up the name of the deceased through his inheritance, so that his name will not disappear from among his brothers or from the gate of his home. You are witnesses today.”

RUT 4:11.text: “We are witnesses,” said the elders and all the people at the gate. “May the LORD make the woman entering your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel. May you be prosperous in Ephrathah and famous in Bethlehem.
RUT 4:11.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Israel, Leadership] “We are witnesses,” said the elders and all the people at the gate. “May the LORD make the woman entering your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel. May you be prosperous in Ephrathah and famous in Bethlehem.

RUT 4:12.text: And may your house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, because of the offspring the LORD will give you by this young woman.”
RUT 4:12.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Children] And may your house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, because of the offspring the LORD will give you by this young woman.”

RUT 4:13.text: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. And when he had relations with her, the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son.
RUT 4:13.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4] So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. And when he had relations with her, the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son.

RUT 4:14.text: Then the women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you this day without a kinsman-redeemer. May his name become famous in Israel.
RUT 4:14.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Biblical Women, Heroic Women] Then the women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you this day without a kinsman-redeemer. May his name become famous in Israel.

RUT 4:15.text: He will renew your life and sustain you in your old age. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you and is better to you than seven sons, has given him birth.”
RUT 4:15.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Love] He will renew your life and sustain you in your old age. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you and is better to you than seven sons, has given him birth.”

RUT 4:16.text: And Naomi took the child, placed him on her lap, and became a nurse to him.
RUT 4:16.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4] And Naomi took the child, placed him on her lap, and became a nurse to him.

RUT 4:17.text: The neighbor women said, “A son has been born to Naomi,” and they named him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.
RUT 4:17.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · Biblical Women, God the Father] The neighbor women said, “A son has been born to Naomi,” and they named him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.

RUT 4:18.text: Now these are the generations of Perez:  Perez was the father of Hezron,
RUT 4:18.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · God the Father] Now these are the generations of Perez:  Perez was the father of Hezron,

RUT 4:19.text: Hezron was the father of Ram,   Ram was the father of Amminadab,
RUT 4:19.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · God the Father] Hezron was the father of Ram,   Ram was the father of Amminadab,

RUT 4:20.text: Amminadab was the father of Nahshon,   Nahshon was the father of Salmon,
RUT 4:20.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · God the Father] Amminadab was the father of Nahshon,   Nahshon was the father of Salmon,

RUT 4:21.text: Salmon was the father of Boaz,   Boaz was the father of Obed,
RUT 4:21.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · God the Father] Salmon was the father of Boaz,   Boaz was the father of Obed,

RUT 4:22.text: Obed was the father of Jesse,   and Jesse was the father of David.
RUT 4:22.bm25Text: [Ruth · Chapter 4 · God the Father] Obed was the father of Jesse,   and Jesse was the father of David.

SNG 1:1.text: This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.
SNG 1:1.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1] This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.

SNG 1:2.text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.
SNG 1:2.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1 · Love] Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.

SNG 1:3.text: The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the maidens adore you.
SNG 1:3.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1] The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the maidens adore you.

SNG 1:4.text: Take me away with you—let us hurry! May the king bring me to his chambers.    We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine.    It is only right that they adore you.
SNG 1:4.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1 · Love] Take me away with you—let us hurry! May the king bring me to his chambers.    We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine.    It is only right that they adore you.

SNG 1:5.text: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
SNG 1:5.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1 · Love] I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.

SNG 1:6.text: Do not stare because I am dark, for the sun has gazed upon me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me a keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have neglected.
SNG 1:6.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1] Do not stare because I am dark, for the sun has gazed upon me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me a keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have neglected.

SNG 1:7.text: Tell me, O one I love, where do you pasture your sheep? Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions?
SNG 1:7.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1 · Love] Tell me, O one I love, where do you pasture your sheep? Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions?

SNG 1:8.text: If you do not know, O fairest of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats near the tents of the shepherds.
SNG 1:8.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1 · Biblical Women, Heroic Women] If you do not know, O fairest of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats near the tents of the shepherds.

SNG 1:9.text: I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.
SNG 1:9.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1] I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.

SNG 1:10.text: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.
SNG 1:10.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1] Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.

SNG 1:11.text: We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with beads of silver.
SNG 1:11.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1] We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with beads of silver.

SNG 1:12.text: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
SNG 1:12.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1] While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.

SNG 1:13.text: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.
SNG 1:13.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1 · Love] My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.

SNG 1:14.text: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.
SNG 1:14.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1 · Love] My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.

SNG 1:15.text: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves.
SNG 1:15.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1] How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves.

SNG 1:16.text: How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how delightful! The soft grass is our bed.
SNG 1:16.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1 · Love] How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how delightful! The soft grass is our bed.

SNG 1:17.text: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are fragrant firs.
SNG 1:17.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 1] The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are fragrant firs.

SNG 2:1.text: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley.
SNG 2:1.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2] I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley.

SNG 2:2.text: Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens.
SNG 2:2.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2] Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens.

SNG 2:3.text: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
SNG 2:3.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love, Fruit of the Spirit] Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.

SNG 2:4.text: He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.
SNG 2:4.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love] He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.

SNG 2:5.text: Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.
SNG 2:5.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love] Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.

SNG 2:6.text: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
SNG 2:6.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2] His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.

SNG 2:7.text: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
SNG 2:7.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love] O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.

SNG 2:8.text: Listen! My beloved approaches. Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.
SNG 2:8.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love] Listen! My beloved approaches. Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.

SNG 2:9.text: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.
SNG 2:9.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love] My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.

SNG 2:10.text: My beloved calls to me, “Arise, my darling. Come away with me, my beautiful one.
SNG 2:10.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love] My beloved calls to me, “Arise, my darling. Come away with me, my beautiful one.

SNG 2:11.text: For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.
SNG 2:11.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2] For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.

SNG 2:12.text: The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.
SNG 2:12.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2] The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.

SNG 2:13.text: The fig tree ripens its figs; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come away, my darling; come away with me, my beautiful one.”
SNG 2:13.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2] The fig tree ripens its figs; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come away, my darling; come away with me, my beautiful one.”

SNG 2:14.text: O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely.
SNG 2:14.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love] O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely.

SNG 2:15.text: Catch for us the foxes— the little foxes that ruin the vineyards— for our vineyards are in bloom.
SNG 2:15.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2] Catch for us the foxes— the little foxes that ruin the vineyards— for our vineyards are in bloom.

SNG 2:16.text: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
SNG 2:16.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love] My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.

SNG 2:17.text: Before the day breaks and shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.
SNG 2:17.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 2 · Love] Before the day breaks and shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.

SNG 3:1.text: On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.
SNG 3:1.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3 · Love] On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.

SNG 3:2.text: I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love. So I sought him but did not find him.
SNG 3:2.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3 · Love, About Forgiveness] I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love. So I sought him but did not find him.

SNG 3:3.text: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: “Have you seen the one I love?”
SNG 3:3.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3 · Love] I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: “Have you seen the one I love?”

SNG 3:4.text: I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.
SNG 3:4.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3 · Love] I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.

SNG 3:5.text: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
SNG 3:5.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3 · Love] O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.

SNG 3:6.text: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant?
SNG 3:6.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3] Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant?

SNG 3:7.text: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.
SNG 3:7.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3 · Israel] Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.

SNG 3:8.text: All are skilled with the sword, experienced in warfare. Each has his sword at his side prepared for the terror of the night.
SNG 3:8.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3] All are skilled with the sword, experienced in warfare. Each has his sword at his side prepared for the terror of the night.

SNG 3:9.text: King Solomon has made his carriage out of the timber of Lebanon.
SNG 3:9.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3] King Solomon has made his carriage out of the timber of Lebanon.

SNG 3:10.text: He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric. Its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
SNG 3:10.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3 · Love] He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric. Its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.

SNG 3:11.text: Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze at King Solomon, wearing the crown his mother bestowed on the day of his wedding— the day of his heart’s rejoicing.
SNG 3:11.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 3 · Adultery In Heart, Joy] Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze at King Solomon, wearing the crown his mother bestowed on the day of his wedding— the day of his heart’s rejoicing.

SNG 4:1.text: How beautiful you are, my darling— how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.
SNG 4:1.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4] How beautiful you are, my darling— how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.

SNG 4:2.text: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.
SNG 4:2.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4 · Baptism] Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.

SNG 4:3.text: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is lovely. Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
SNG 4:3.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4 · Love] Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is lovely. Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.

SNG 4:4.text: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.
SNG 4:4.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4] Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.

SNG 4:5.text: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.
SNG 4:5.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4] Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.

SNG 4:6.text: Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will make my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
SNG 4:6.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4] Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will make my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.

SNG 4:7.text: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw.
SNG 4:7.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4] You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw.

SNG 4:8.text: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon! Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summits of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.
SNG 4:8.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4] Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon! Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summits of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.

SNG 4:9.text: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your neck.
SNG 4:9.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4 · Adultery In Heart] You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your neck.

SNG 4:10.text: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is much better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.
SNG 4:10.bm25Text: [Song of Solomon · Chapter 4 · Love] How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is much better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.

SNG 4:11.text: Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like the honeycomb; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the aroma of Lebanon.
